mcqs.subject: Dermatology
mcqs.question: Which of the following can be used in a patient suffering from acyclovir-resistant recurrent herpes labialis?
mcqs.explanation: In case of resistance to acyclovir, foscarnet or cidofovir can be used to treat herpes . They act on viral DNA polymerases thus blocking DNA replication.

mcqs.subject: Dermatology
mcqs.question: What is the most common causative organism for verruca vulgaris?
mcqs.explanation: Verruca vulgaris or common wart is most commonly caused by human papillomavirus-2 (HPV -2) but is also related to types 1, 4, 27, and 57 . Common warts are usually asymptomatic . They show acanthosis, hyperkeratosis , and papillomatosis and present as firm papules with a rough horny surface . The most commonly affected sites are on the backs of the hands and fingers, and, in children on the knees. Pseudo -Koebner phenomenon may be observed. Treatment is usually with topical agents such as salicylic acid, caustics , glutaraldehyde , formalin, or with laser, cryotherapy , surgical removal.390 verruca vulgaris.

mcqs.subject: Dermatology
mcqs.question: Identify the incorrect statement regarding scabies .

options.b: Itching starts 3 to 4 weeks after infection
options.c: Animal scabies is characterized by burrows
options.d: Circle of Hebra is formed by connecting body parts commonly involved

mcqs.explanation: Burrows are absent in animal scabies . Skin lesions resulting from contact with animal scabies are usually composed of small pruritic weals or papules , which are frequently excoriated , and resemble human scabies , but without burrows. Water-washed diseases are infections that are caused by poor personal hygiene resulting from inadequate water availability for e.g. scabies . The characteristic symptoms of a scabies infection include intense itching which usually manifests 3-4 weeks after infestation and superficial burrows (pathognomonic). Circle of Hebra is an imaginary circle formed by connecting the main sites of involvement in scabies .442

mcqs.subject: Dermatology
mcqs.question: In which of the following patients would you expect to see a positive Dory flop sign?

options.a: A young woman with a painless beefy red granulomatous ulcer on her vulva
options.b: A middle -aged man with an painless indurated lesion on his penis
options.c: A circumcised teenager with multiple painful vesicles over his penis
options.d: A lady with a painless indurated ulcer over her labia majora

mcqs.explanation: The Dory flop sign is described in an uncircumcised male with an indurated lesion of primary syphilis on the underside of the coronal sulcus . Here, prepucial retraction causes the foreskin to flip suddenly . Hence it would only be seen in the middle -aged man with the indurated lesion on his penis . The Dory flop sign can help distinguish chancres from other nonindurated causes of genital ulcer disease , such as Herpes simplex virus infection and chancroid. It is named after the movement of a dory, a small wooden fishing boat, which flips suddenly when overturned. Option A: This young woman has granuloma inguinale , which is a non - indurated lesion. Option C: This circumcised teenager has herpes genitalis . Option D: Though this lady has an indurated lesion (chancre), the dory flop sign can be demonstrated only in uncircumcised males.461

mcqs.subject: Dermatology
mcqs.question: A 21 -year-old homeless pregnant woman gives birth to a premature infant with a palmoplantar bullous eruption . The RPR titer of the cord blood is elevated . Which of the following is not a feature of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Elevated RPR titer of the cord blood is indicative of congenital syphilis in the infant. Seventh nerve palsy is not a feature of congenital syphilis . It is associated with 8th nerve deafness , along with tinnitus and vertigo. It is a part of Hutchinson's triad which includes the following : • Interstitial keratitis • Eighth nerve deafness • Hutchinson's teeth One of the features of congenital syphilis is periostitis of the skull which results in parrot's nodes or hot-cross bun appearance . Most newborns with congenital syphilis are asymptomatic at birth. However, a vesiculobullous rash called syphilitic pemphigus may be present at delivery . After 2 weeks , a maculopapular rash is more common. Clinical signs usually appear between weeks 3 to 8 of life , usually within 3 months.466

mcqs.subject: Dermatology
mcqs.question: A 29-year-old primigravida is diagnosed with chlamydial cervicitis. What is the drug of choice ?
mcqs.explanation: A single dose of azithromycin 1g is the drug of choice in pregnant women with uncomplicated chlamydial infection . The drug of choice for chlamydia infection in adults and adolescents is doxycycline 100 mg orally BD for 7 days. It is contraindicated in pregnancy. Alternative regimens are: • Azithromycin 1g orally, single dose • Levofloxacin 500mg OD for 7 days Azithromycin is preferred due to its greater effectiveness and lower cost. Option A: Doxycycline is contraindicated in pregnancy as it causes depression of bone growth and enamel hypoplasia in the fetus . Option B: Ceftriaxone is used for the treatment of gonococcal infections . Option D: Amoxicillin is used as an alternative regimen as it is less effective .

mcqs.subject: Dermatology
mcqs.question: Which of the following cutaneous disorders is not associated with a nucleotide excision repair defect ?
mcqs.explanation: 507 Muir–Torre syndrome is a rare autosomal dominant disorder of DNA mismatch repair. It occurs due to mutation in one of the DNA mismatch repair genes (MSH\0372, MLH\0371, MSH\0376). It is characterized by sebaceous gland neoplasms , keratoacanthomas associated with gastrointestinal and genitourinary malignancies.

mcqs.subject: Dermatology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common cutaneous presentation of subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus ?
mcqs.explanation: Subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus presents most commonly as a non\037scarring papulosquamous eruption . It can also present as annular polycyclic lesions . Sites of lesions: • Above the waist • Around the neck • On the trunk • Outer aspects of the arms The image below shows psoriasiform lesions of subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A patient is incidentally noted to have the following finding. It is also present on the other ear. Which of the following is the cause for such abnormality?

options.a: Persistent opening of first branchial cleft

mcqs.explanation: The given image showing the presence of sinus seen between the tragus and crus of the helix is suggestive of the preauricular sinus. It is due to improper fusion of the auricular tubercle formed from the first and second arches. The preauricular sinus is apparent at birth and is usually bilateral. There may be occasional sebaceous discharge from the punctum. It does not regress spontaneously .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: What is the structure marked in the given image?
mcqs.explanation: The marked structure is incus. This is an image taken during mastoidectomy . The incus articulates with the malleus and has a short process and a long process . The long process articulates with the head of the stapes .CT: chorda tympani; I: incus; JB : jugular bulb; LSC: lateral semicirular canal; M: malleus ; PSC: posterior semicircular canal; S: stapes; SM: stapedius muscle ; SSC: superior semicircular canal; VIIms : mastoid segment of VII cranial nerve; VIIts : tympanic segment of VII cranial nerve.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: In a 7-year-old child with hearing loss and intellectual disability , you notice the following external ear anomaly. What could the anomaly in this case be?
mcqs.explanation: The external ear anomaly seen here is pre-auricular tag/appendage . Pre-auricular tags/appendages are congenital external ear anomalies. They are seen as skin -covered pieces of cartilage anywhere between the tragus and the angle of the mouth. The clinical features of facial asymmetry, intellectual disability , limbal dermoid, and pre-auricular tags and mixed or conductive hearing loss point to a diagnosis of Goldenhar syndrome (oculoauriculovertebral spectrum). Clinical features include : • Hypoplasia of the malar , maxillary, and mandibular regions • Macrostomia and microtia • Preauricular and facial skin tags • Hemivertebrae (usually cervical) • Intellectual disability • Cardiac, renal, and central nervous system (CNS) anomalies • Ocular features - Limbal dermoids, upper lid notching or coloboma, microphthalmos, disc coloboma

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A patient presents to the OPD with the following finding and history of pus discharge from the same area. What is the likely etiology of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and the image are suggestive of preauricular sinus seen between the tragus and crus of the helix. It is the most common congenital anomaly of the 1st branchial arch, due to the incomplete fusion of the hillocks of His that develop to form the pinna. It can get repeatedly infected and form an abscess , which would then require excision.91

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: An 8-month-old child was brought to your OPD with the following finding. What is your diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given image showing malformed small pinna appearing like tubercles are suggestive of microtia. It is frequently accompanied by hearing loss.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A professional wrestler presents to your OPD with the deformity shown below . What is the most likely cause of the same?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows a cauliflower ear deformity , which is likely due to auricular hematoma. Auricular hematoma is a collection of blood between the auricular cartilage and its perichondrium. If left untreated , the extravasated blood may clot and then organize, resulting in a typical deformity called cauliflower ear. It is also called pugilistic or boxer's ear. It is often seen in boxers, wrestlers , and rugby players due to blunt trauma. Treatment comprises of aspiration of the hematoma under strict aseptic precautions and a pressure dressing , to prevent reaccumulation. Aspiration may need to be repeated . If aspiration fails, incision and drainage should be done. All cases should receive prophylactic antibiotics.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: What is the most likely diagnosis in a patient who presents with a painful ear swelling as shown below ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of painful, erythematous ear swelling is suggestive of perichondritis. The most common cause is trauma either iatrogenic (surgical incision) or non-iatrogenic (laceration, hematoma). It can be due to the extension of infection from diffuse otitis externa or furuncle of the meatus . The most common organism responsible is Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The image given below shows a patient with a cauliflower ear deformity . It is also known as perichondrial hematoma or wrestler 's ear. It is usually caused by repeated episodes of trauma.Chondrodermatitis chronica helicis is a small, nodular, tender , chronic inflammatory lesion occurring on the helix of the ear. It is shown in the image below .94 Otitis externa, also called swimmer's ear, is the inflammation of the ear canal. It has the following appearance :

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A middle -aged man presents with a lesion as shown below . He is unable to sleep on the affected side . There is no history of trauma. What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: A small tender nodule in the helix in a middle -aged patient is suggestive of chondrodermatitis nodularis chronica helicis . The patient will have difficulty sleeping on the affected side . Treatment includes excision of the lesion.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A patient is planned for excision of the following lesion. Which of the following measures will not prevent its recurrence post -excision?
mcqs.explanation: 95 The given image shows a keloid of the pinna and neoadjuvant chemotherapy does not reduce its recurrence post excision. Keloid commonly occurs following trauma. The common sites are lobule and helix. There is a high chance of recurrence after excision, which can be prevented by: • Intralesional steroids • Pre and post -operative radiotherapy

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A young man presented with irritation and itching in the ear, associated with watery discharge and a musty odor. Otoscopic imaging is shown below . What is the causative organism?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario along with the otoscopic image showing black-headed filamentous growth is suggestive of otomycosis by Aspergillus niger. Irritation and itching are the most predominant symptoms of Aspergillus niger infection . Pain is predominant in Aspergillus flavus infection . The fungal mass in otomycosis is likened to a wet blotting paper /wet newspaper appearance . The appearances of otomycosis on otoscopy and the causative organisms are: • Black-headed filamentous growth - Aspergillus niger infection • Green or brown - Aspergillus fumigatus infection • White and creamy deposit - Candida infection Rhizopus oryzae is one of the causative agents of mucormycosis. The common clinical form of this opportunistic infection is rhino-orbital-cerebral mucormycosis (ROCM). It is rarely implicated in otomycosis .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A worried mother brings her febrile infant to the ER. He is crying incessantly and clutching his ear. He had the following finding on otoscopy . What is the most likely organism implicated in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario along with the image showing congested tympanic membrane with purulent effusion and absent cone of light is suggestive of acute suppurative otitis media. The most likely organism implicated is Streptococcus pneumoniae . Organisms causing ASOM in infants and young children: • Streptococcus pneumoniae (most common) • Haemophilus influenzae • Moraxella catarrhalis • Streptococcus pyogenes • Staphylococcus aureus • Pseudomonas aeruginosa113

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Otologic examination of a febrile child with otalgia is shown below . What is the stage of acute suppurative otitis media seen here?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical picture and image show the stage of pre-suppuration of acute suppurative otitis media (ASOM). During this stage , due to prolonged tubal occlusion , pyogenic organisms invade the tympanic cavity. An inflammatory exudate appears in the middle ear and there is congestion of pars tensa. A leash of blood vessels appears along with the handle of malleus and at the periphery of the tympanic membrane imparting it a cart-wheel appearance . Later, the whole of the tympanic membrane including pars flaccida becomes uniformly red. Symptoms of this stage include marked earache, a high degree of fever, hearing loss, and tinnitus (seen only in adults ). Tuning fork tests show the conductive type of hearing loss.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: You see a child with delayed development of speech as part of a health visit in a local school. The otoscopic appearance of the ear is shown below . Hearing loss of 20 dB is detected in audiometric tests . What is your diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and image suggest a diagnosis of serous otitis media. The golden yellow discoloration of the tympanic membrane is caused by the clear watery straw-colored effusion filling the middle ear. Since the fluid is clear, one can see the structures of the middle ear quite clearly on otoscopy . Patients having serous otitis media will have hearing loss that rarely exceeds 40 dB. This deafness can pass unnoticed , and maybe accidentally discovered during audiometric screening tests . Because of hearing loss, the development of speech is delayed or defective . Otoscopic findings in serous otitis media: • Fluid level and air bubbles are seen when fluid is thin and the tympanic membrane transparent. • In chronic cases , the fluid becomes very sticky. Hence , the name glue ear. • The tympanic membrane is often dull and opaque with a loss of light reflex . • The mobility of the tympanic membrane is restricted .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Otoscopic image of a patient with a history of repeated middle ear infections is shown below . Which one of the following statements is true regarding this condition?

options.c: It is also known as epidermosis

mcqs.explanation: 128 The image shows the presence of a large mass of white keratin debris in the left upper quadrant of the left tympanic membrane. This along with clinical scenario is suggestive of cholesteatoma which is also known as epidermosis or keratoma Cholesteatoma is the presence of stratified squamous epithelium in middle ear where it is not usually present , i.e., skin in wrong place. A central white mass, consisting of keratin debris is produced by the matrix. For this reason, it has also been named epidermosis or keratoma. The term cholesteatoma is a misnomer because it neither contains cholesterol crystals nor it is a tumor to merit the suffix "oma."

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: An 8-year-old boy was referred to an otolaryngologist for subjective left -sided hearing loss. A hearing test revealed mild conductive hearing loss at low and middle frequencies . Otoendoscopy showed a mass with the appearance as shown below . Which of the following criteria is used to diagnose this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with the otoendoscopy showing a white pearly mass behind the intact eardrum in the anterosuperior quadrant is suggestive of congenital cholesteatoma . Levenson criteria should be satisfied in order to diagnose this condition. Levenson criteria: • A white mass behind the normal tympanic membrane • Normal pars tensa and pars flaccida • No prior history of otorrhoea • No prior history of otological procedure • Episodes of otitis media with effusion should not be considered as exclusion criteria. Another popular guideline used is Derlaki and Clemis which includes all the above except for the 4th criteria.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which embryological structure gives rise to the pinna?
mcqs.explanation: The 1st and 2nd branchial arches give rise to the pinna (auricle) through six mesenchymal proliferation. These proliferations are called auricular hillocks and they fuse to form the auricle. The tissue from the second arch forms nearly all of the pinna. The tissue from the first arch forms the tragus and external auditory meatus . Image showing the development of pinna:8

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old woman undergoes a rhinoplasty procedure to correct a deformity of her nose. Auricular cartilage is harvested from her right pinna. Which of the following sites cannot be used to harvest the cartilage ?
mcqs.explanation: Incisura terminalis cannot be used to harvest cartilage as it is devoid of cartilage . It is the part of the pinna between the tragus and the crus of helix. Being devoid of cartilage , the incision for endaural approach for ear surgery can be made here. The lobule is also devoid of cartilage . Hence , it is the safest site for piercing. The parts of the pinna are:19

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A patient develops tingling and numbness along the upper part of the medial surface of the pinna. Which nerve is most likely to be affected ?
mcqs.explanation: The upper part of the medial surface of the pinna is supplied by the lesser occipital nerve.Nerve Derivation Region supplied Greater/Great auricular nerve Cervical plexus C2,C Medial surface and posterior part of the lateral surface Lesser occipital nerve Cervical plexus C2 Superior portion of medial su rface Auricular branch Vagus (X) Concha and antihelixSome su pply medial surface (eminetia concha) Auriculotemporal nerve Mandibular (V3 ) Tragus, crus of helix and adja cent helix Facial (VII ) Small region in the root of co ncha and retroauricular groo ve26

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: You are approaching the middle ear via the mastoid through the facial recess . Regarding anatomical relations of facial recess , which of the following is true?

options.a: Bound medially by horizontal part of facial nerve

mcqs.explanation: Facial recess or the posterior sinus is a depression in the posterior wall lateral to the pyramid. It is bounded medially by the vertical part of the facial nerve, laterally by the chorda tympani and above, by the fossa incudis. Facial recess is important surgically , as direct access can be made through this into the middle ear without disturbing the posterior canal wall. This is called intact canal wall technique . Image showing the facial recess :44

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true regarding the course of chorda tympani in the middle ear?

options.b: Enters middle ear lateral to tympanic membrane
options.c: Runs in between the malleus and incus
options.d: Enters middle ear via the canal of Huguier

mcqs.explanation: In the middle ear, the chorda tympani runs in between the malleus and incus. Image showing the course of chorda tympani:51

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: The bony cochlea is a coiled tube making _____ turns around a bony pyramid called ____
mcqs.explanation: The bony cochlea is a coiled tube making 2.5 to 2.75 turns round a central pyramid of bone called modiolus .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: The endolymphatic duct is a continuation of which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: The endolymphatic duct is formed by the union of two ducts , one each from the saccule and the utricle.76 Ductus reunions connect the cochlear duct to the saccule . The aqueduct of cochlea (cochlear aqueduct ) connects scala tympani to the subarachnoid space .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false about wax?

options.a: Contains secretions of glands in the external auditory canal
options.b: Formed by dried up middle ear discharge
options.d: Is extruded out on its own during jaw movements

mcqs.explanation: Wax or cerumen is not made up of middle ear discharge . Composition of wax: • Secretions of ceruminous glands (modified apocrine sweat glands) • Secretions of the sebaceous gland (fatty secretion ) • Desquamated epithelial cells • Hair Wax is normally expelled by the movement of the jaw during eating , talking. Functions include antibacterial action and trapping of foreign bodies and dirt. Impacted wax causes a sensation of blockage of the ear, reduced hearing, vertigo, tinnitus. Treatment: • Softening with ceruminolytics like 2% paradichlorobenzene , 5% sodium bicarbonate in equal parts of glycerine and water. • Syringing or instrumentation or suction clearance.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A 23 -year-old woman presented to the OPD with complaints of excruciating pain in the right ear, deafness and decreased sleep . On examination, she had right-sided LMN facial nerve paralysis and bulging tympanic membrane on otoscopy . Which of the following best describes the procedure to be done?

options.b: Removal of disease and reconstruction of hearing

mcqs.explanation: The above clinical scenario points to a diagnosis of acute suppurative otitis media (ASOM) complicated by right-sided LMN facial nerve palsy . Otoscopic finding of bulging tympanic membrane is an indication to perform myringotomy i.e., surgical opening in the tympanic membrane. Treatment of facial nerve paralysis secondary to otitis media114 • Conservative management is preferred , using antibiotics and corticosteroids . • Myringotomy and a ventilation tube should be added when spontaneous perforation of the tympanic membrane has not occurred. • Facial nerve decompression is not usually necessary . Tympanoplasty is the removal of disease from the middle ear and reconstruction of hearing with or without myringoplasty .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following theories does not explain the origin of cholesteatoma ?

options.b: Ruedi's theory of basal cell hyperplasia
options.d: von Bekesy theory of mucosal metaplasia

mcqs.explanation: von B\351k\351sy proposed the traveling wave theory , whereas Sade 's metaplasia theory explains the origin of cholesteatoma . Cholesteatoma can be of 2 main types : • Congenital cholesteatoma - explained by the presence of congenital cell rests within the middle ear and other parts of the temporal bone. • Acquired cholesteatoma - explained by a pathology either within the mastoid air cell system and eustachian tube drainage, or the tympanic membrane epithelium .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Wullstein 's classification is used for which of the following procedures ?
mcqs.explanation: Zollner and Wullstein 's classification is used to classify tympanoplasty .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: You are an OBGYN resident and your patient is one of your staff nurses. She is a primigravida who has just been diagnosed with otosclerosis and wants to know its inheritance pattern. Which of the following is the inheritance pattern for otosclerosis ?
mcqs.explanation: Otosclerosis has an autosomal dominant type of inheritance. About 50% of the cases of otosclerosis have a positive family history while the rest are sporadic. Genetic studies reveal that it is an autosomal dominant trait with incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity .162

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: An ENT surgeon has referred a patient with otosclerosis posted for stapedotomy to your anesthesia OPD. She has no known co-morbidities. Which of the following techniques will you recommend for the above patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Stapedotomy is preferred to be done under local anesthesia because - • Immediate on-table improvement of hearing can be assessed • Damage to the inner ear can be assessed by the patient 's symptoms of vertigo/ nystagmus • Damage to the facial nerve can be checked .168

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs is a vasodilator of the inner ear?
mcqs.explanation: Betahistine is a vasodilator of the inner ear. It is used in the treatment of Meniere 's disease . It is reported to act by: • Improving microvascular circulation in the stria vascularis of the cochlea • Inhibiting vestibular nuclei activity

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true for the 2nd genu of the facial nerve?

options.b: It gives the second branch of the facial nerve
options.c: It lies on the inferior wall of the middle ear
options.d: It is at the junction of 3rd and 4th intratemporal segments

mcqs.explanation: 213 The 2nd genu of the facial nerve lies at the junction of the 3rd and the 4th intratemporal segments , between the tympanic and the mastoid segments . The 2nd genu of the facial nerve is formed where the horizontal facial nerve takes a turn inferiorly at the junction between the medial and posterior walls of the middle ear. It continues as the vertical segment of the facial nerve behind the posterior wall of the middle ear. It does not contain a ganglion and does not give any branches. The course of the facial nerve has 3 parts- • Intracranial • Intratemporal • Extracranial . Intratemporal part of the facial nerve has 4 segments - • Meatal • Labyrinthine • Tympanic/horizontal • Mastoid /vertical segments . Option A: Gasserian ganglion is present in the trigeminal nerve. Option B: The temporal segment of the facial nerve ends with the 2nd genu . The nerve then passes vertically downward to form the mastoid segment . The 2nd branch of facial nerve (nerve to stapedius ) arises from this segment close to the level of 2nd genu and not from the 2nd genu .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old housewife presents with facial weakness on the right side , difficulty in closing the right eye , and loss of taste sensation. A diagnosis of Bell's palsy is made. Which of the following is false regarding this condition?

options.d: Males are affected more commonly than females

mcqs.explanation: Bell's palsy affects both males and females equally. It is an acute onset idiopathic ipsilateral LMN facial nerve palsy . Most of the evidence supports the viral etiology due to herpes simplex , herpes zoster, or the Epstein –Barr virus. Positive family history is present in 6–8% of patients . Most of the patients recover fully and the remaining require surgery. Recurrent facial palsy is seen in 3–10 % of cases .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: An intern is assisting the surgeon in total parotidectomy . During the procedure , he accidentally injured the facial nerve. Which of the following cannot be used as a graft for repair in this case?
mcqs.explanation: The mandibular nerve cannot be used as a graft for facial nerve surgeries . Only those nerves whose functions can be sacrificed are chosen as grafts and these are usually sensory nerves. The most commonly used grafts for facial nerve are: • Greater auricular nerve (can be extracted from the same incision) • Lateral cutaneous nerve of thigh • Sural nerve (when a large segment is required).238

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.chapter: Physiology of hearing and Tuning fork tests
mcqs.question: What is the lever ratio of the ear ossicles ?
mcqs.explanation: The lever ratio of the ear ossicles is 1.3:1. The handle of the malleus is 1.3 times longer than the long process of the incus, providing a mechanical advantage of 1.3.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.chapter: Physiology of hearing and Tuning fork tests
mcqs.question: A young female diagnosed with otosclerosis presented to the ENT OPD with worsening hearing loss. Which of the following will be the most likely observation on the Bing test ?

options.a: Hears louder when canal is occluded
options.c: Hears softer when canal is occluded
options.d: The test is said to be positive

mcqs.explanation: The patient diagnosed with otosclerosis will have a conductive type of hearing loss and will appreciate no change in the Bing test . Here, the Bing test is said to be negative . Bing test is a test of bone conduction and examines the effect of occlusion of the ear canal on hearing. A vibrating tuning fork is placed on the mastoid. The examiner alternately closes and opens the ear canal by pressing on the tragus inwards. Bing positive : A normal person or one with sensorineural hearing loss hears louder when the ear canal is occluded and softer when the canal is open . Bing negative : A patient with conductive hearing loss will appreciate no change.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about the cartilaginous part of the external nose?
mcqs.explanation: The external nose is made up of 3 paired and 1 unpaired cartilages . Paired cartilages : • Upper lateral cartilage - From nasal bone above to alar cartilage below .292 • Lower lateral (alar) cartilage - U-shaped . Lateral crus forms the ala and medial crus runs in the columella . Limen nasi or limen vestibuli is the junction of the upper and lower lateral cartilages . • Lesser alar (sesamoid) cartilage - multiple , above, and lateral to the alar cartilage . The septal cartilage is the only unpaired cartilage . It forms the midline of the lower 2/3rd of the dorsum of nose and supports lower 2/3rd of the dorsum of external nose.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a paranasal sinus?
mcqs.explanation: 308 Pyriform sinus (fossa) is a part of hypopharynx. It lies on either side of the larynx and extends from pharyngoepiglottic fold to the upper end of oesophagus . Sinuses are air-containing cavities in certain bones of skull. It is divided into 2 groups . Anterior group includes • Maxillary • Frontal • Anterior ethmoidal sinuses . Posterior group includes • Posterior ethmoid • Sphenoid sinuses .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A worried mother brought her 4-year-old son to the ER with complaints of a nose bleed . On examination , the bleed was found to be from the Kiesselbach 's plexus . Which of the following arteries does not contribute to its formation?
mcqs.explanation: The posterior ethmoidal artery does not contribute to the formation of Kiesselbach 's plexus . Kiesselbach 's plexus is the vascular anastomosis situated at Little's area (anteroinferior part of the septum ). The contributing arteries are as follows: • Sphenopalatine and greater palatine branches of the maxillary artery, which in turn is a branch of the external carotid artery. • Septal branch of the superior labial artery which in turn is a branch of the facial artery. The facial artery is a branch of the external carotid artery. • Anterior ethmoidal branch of the ophthalmic division of internal carotid artery.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.chapter: Congenital Anomalies of Nose and Disease of Nose
mcqs.question: A patient presented with atrophic dry nasal mucosa, extensive crustations, and a woody hard external nose. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical condition is suggestive of rhinoscleroma. Rhinoscleroma is caused by Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis (Frisch bacillus ). It has 3 stages : • Atrophic stage – Crusting and foul smelling nasal discharge similar to atrophic rhinitis. • Granulomatous stage – Painless, non ulcerative Granulomatous nodules with subdermal infiltration giving feel of woody /hebra nose. • Cicatricial stage – Fibrosis leading to stenosis of vestibule , pharynx, larynx. Deformity is called tapir nose.Option A: Atrophic rhinitis doesn 't cause woody nose. Option B: Rhinophyma or potato tumor is due to hypertrophy of sebaceous gland and presents as swelling over tip of nose.352 Option C: Rhinosporidiosis is a granulomatous condition caused by Rhinosporidium seeberi and presents with nasal discharge , epistaxis and nasal obstruction by a polypoidal mass.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.chapter: Disorder of Nasal Septum and Nasal Polyposis
mcqs.question: A middle -aged man with tertiary syphilis presented with complaints of epistaxis , nasal crusting, and nasal twang on speaking. On examination, nasal septal perforation was noted . What is the most likely site for the perforation?

options.d: Junction of the bony and cartilaginous septum

mcqs.explanation: The given patient is having nasal septal perforation due to syphilis . The most common site of involvement in syphilis is the bony nasal septum . Other chronic granulomatous conditions like lupus , tuberculosis , and leprosy can cause perforation in the cartilaginous part. Wegener's granulomatosis causes perforation of both bony and cartilaginous parts.380

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following is called blow -out fractures?

options.b: Fracture of lateral wall of orbit
options.c: Fracture of medial wall of orbit

mcqs.explanation: Fracture of the floor of the orbit is called blow -out fracture. It occurs when a large blunt object strikes the globe .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common malignant tumor of the nasal cavity?
mcqs.explanation: Squamous cell carcinoma is the most common malignant tumor of the nasal cavity, seen in about 80% of cases .

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common cause of sinusitis?
mcqs.explanation: Nasal infections are the most common cause of sinusitis since sinus mucosa is a continuation of nasal mucosa and infections from the nose can travel directly by continuity or by way of submucosal lymphatics . The most common cause of acute sinusitis is viral rhinitis followed by bacterial invasion . Other causes : • Dental infections cause maxillary sinus infections . • Trauma • Swimming and diving.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A middle -aged patient with a history of recurrent upper respiratory tract infections presents with diplopia and protrusion of the left eyeball . Inflammation of which of the following paranasal sinuses would most likely lead to this complication?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical vignette is suggestive of orbital complications secondary to sinusitis. The orbit and its contents are closely related to the ethmoid , frontal, and maxillary sinuses , but most of the complications , however, follow infection of ethmoids as they are separated from the orbit only by a thin lamina of bone called lamina papyracea.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old man is diagnosed with carcinoma limited to the hypopharynx. Which of the following sites will not be involved?
mcqs.explanation: Epiglottis is part of the supraglottic larynx. The hypopharynx is made of 3 parts: • Pyriform sinus • Posterior Pharyngeal Wall • Post-cricoid region

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A 6-year-old child has been posted for an adenoidectomy procedure . Which of the following conditions if present in this child will be a contraindication to performing the surgery?
mcqs.explanation: Cleft palate is a contraindication to perform adenoidectomy as removal of adenoids causes velopharyngeal insufficiency . Velopharyngeal insufficiency is a condition where the soft palate does not close tightly against the back of the throat. This leads to air coming out the nose (characterized by hypernasality ) during speech . Contraindications for adenoidectomy : • Cleft palate or submucous palate . • Hemorrhagic diathesis . • Acute infection of the upper respiratory tract.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: An ENT junior resident observed a symptomless yellowish swelling over the tonsil when he was examining a patient for a buccal sore. The swelling was easily drained. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of a tonsillar cyst . It is a condition due to blockage of a tonsillar crypt and appears as a yellowish swelling over the tonsil. Very often , it is symptomless and can be easily drained. Option A: Intratonsillar abscess is an accumulation of pus within the substance of the tonsil. It usually follows a blockage of the opening of the crypt in acute follicular tonsillitis . There is marked local pain and dysphagia . Tonsil appears swollen and red. Option B: Tonsilloliths (calculus of the tonsil) are seen in chronic tonsillitis when its crypt is blocked with retention of debris. Inorganic salts of calcium and magnesium are then deposited leading to the formation of a stone . It may gradually enlarge and then ulcerate through the tonsil. It generally causes local discomfort or foreign body sensation.474 Option D: In follicular tonsillitis , purulent material is present at the opening of the crypts as yellow dots . It presents with fever, dysphagia, and sore throat.

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: In which of the following clinical scenarios will you not perform an intraoral incision?

options.a: A 21 -year-old woman with fever, hot potato voice and bulging of soft palate and anterior pillar above the tonsil on the right side .
options.b: A 50-year-old diabetic man with fever, neck swelling over upper \037 rd of the left sternocleidomastoid and the tonsils on the same side pushed medially
options.c: A 3-year-old child with fever and swelling in the posterior pharyngeal wall lateral to the midline
options.d: A 50-year-old man with fever due to penetrating injury of oral mucosa by wood splinters

mcqs.explanation: An intraoral incision is not sufficient in the case of option B - parapharyngeal abscess . An external neck incision must be made always to ensure complete drainage of the abscess . Option A- This is a case of quinsy as the child has odynophagia and a hot potato voice. Option B - This is a case of parapharyngeal abscess as the swelling is in the upper 1/3rd of the neck and the tonsil of the same side is pushed medially Option C- This is a case of retropharyngeal abscess since there is fever and swelling in the posterior pharyngeal wall lateral to the midline. Option D- This is a case of Sublingual abscess involving the sublingual space which is caused by penetrating injuries of oral mucosa due to fishbone or wood splinters . Indications for Incision and Drainage: • Sublingual abscess : Always intraoral incision • Parapharyngeal abscess : Always external neck incision. • Peritonsillar abscess : Always intraoral . • Retropharyngeal abscess : • Intraoral - in rose position • External - Dean approach • Ludwig's angina: • Intraoral —if the infection is still localized to sublingual space . • External—if the infection involves submaxillary space .491

mcqs.question: A teenager has a mass in his nasopharynx that has minimally spread into the sphenoid sinus with no lateral extension . Which stage of nasopharyngeal angiofibroma could this be?
mcqs.explanation: The mass has spread into the sphenoid sinus with no lateral extension , so it's Stage 1B according to the Radkowski classification . mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: A patient with persistent cervical lymphadenopathy now came with spontaneous epistaxis . Nasal endoscopy showed a mass arising from the fossa of Rosenmuller. Biopsy from the mass revealed a keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma . What is the treatment of choice in this case?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of nasopharyngeal carcinoma . The treatment of choice is radiotherapy. Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is extremely radiosensitive, hence treatment of local and regional disease is invariably radiotherapy. Stage I and II are treated by radiotherapy alone. Stage III and IV are treated with radiotherapy and chemotherapy . Chemotherapy can be neoadjuvant, concurrent, or adjuvant to radiotherapy.515

mcqs.subject: ENT
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an intrinsic membrane of the larynx?
mcqs.explanation: The cricothyroid membrane is an intrinsic membrane of the larynx as it connects laryngeal structures to each other. Extrinsic membranes and ligaments connect laryngeal structures with surrounding structures outside the laryngeal framework like the trachea or hyoid. These are: • Cricotracheal membrane • Thyrohyoid membrane • Hyoepiglottic ligament . Intrinsic membranes and ligaments connect laryngeal structures with each other. These are: • Cricovocal membrane • Quadrangular membrane • Cricothyroid ligament • Thyroepiglottic ligament .[Image unavailable] [Image unavailable] [Image unavailable]

mcqs.explanation: The child's age is likely to be 13 years. In the given X-ray image of the wrist and hand, all the carpal bones are seen. The lower epiphysis of the first metacarpal has not united with the shaft. This suggests that the age of the child is between 8 to 15 years. mcqs.question: A girl was allegedly kidnapped by a man. In court, she says that she is a major and is married to the man. X-ray images of her elbow, wrist and pelvis are given. What is the approximate age of the girl ?

mcqs.question: How would the structures marked as 1 and 2 be described in a female skull?
mcqs.explanation: The structures marked as 1 and 2 are the frontal and parietal eminences. mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: Identify the following post-mortem change.
mcqs.explanation: The image shows suggilation. Postmortem lividity (suggilation/ postmortem hypostasis/ postmortem staining/ livor mortis/ vibices) develops in the dependent portions of the body due to engorged vessels showing through the skin.88

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: What does the following image show?
mcqs.explanation: In the given image, margins are irregular and staining is not uniform. There is no area of contact pallor in the region of shoulder blades. This is indicative of a bruise. The difference between a bruise and postmortem lividity is given below:Features Bruise Postmortem lividity Cause Ruptured vessels (either supe rficial or deep ) Engorged vessels showing thr ough the skin Location At the site of blunt trauma On dependent parts89 Features Bruise Postmortem lividity Margins Irregular Clearly defined Swelling and abrasio n Present Absent Contact pallor Absent Present on shoulder blades

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: The following postmortem finding is noted on a dead body. This finding is most prominent a fter how many hours of death?
mcqs.explanation: The given picture shows postmortem marbling. It starts in 24 hours and becomes prominent in 36-48 hours. The blood in the vessels is haemolysed, which stains the vessel walls and the adjacent tissues, giving rise to a marbled appearance. It is greenish-brown or purplish-red discoloration of superficial veins due to the formation of sulfhemoglo bin w hich diffuses into tissues. It is distinctly appreciable on the abdomen, shoulders, chest, and inguinal region.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: Identify the injury in the image below.
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows an abrasion. An abrasion is the most superficial of injuries. It does not penetrate the full thickness of the epidermis. A pure abrasion does not bleed, as blood vessels are confined to the dermis. However, the dermal papillae are corrugated in nature. Thus, many abrasions enter the dermis and bleeding commonly occurs.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: A bruise on the upper arm of an alleged victim of the assault has the following appearance. What is the age of the injury based on colour of this bruise?
mcqs.explanation: The bruise in the given image has a yellow appearance which is attributed to the presence of bilirubin . This finding makes the bruise about 7-12 days old. Bruises are mechanical injuries that are characterized by the extravasation of blood into subcutaneous or subepithelial tissue spaces. The continuity of the overlying skin is preserved. These injuries are typical consequences of blunt force trauma. The extravasated blood serves as a sign of inflammation to attract macrophages, which degrade t he h emoglobin into various compounds (hemosiderin, haematoidin , and bilirubin). This gives rise to shifting color changes that begin at the wound's periphery and migrate towards the center as time goes on.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: You are asked to conduct an autopsy of a person who was found dead at his home. You notice the given findings on the body. W hich t est can be used to differentiate this from antemortem bruising ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows postmortem hypostasis. The classic test used to differentiate a bruise from hypostasis is the incision test. The suspected area is incised to see if the underlying blood is intravascular (hypostasis) or infiltrating the tissues outside the vessels (contusion). Option A: Gettler's chloride test is used to differentiate between freshwater and saltwater drowning. It is not widely used now. Option C: In the precipitin test, a specific antiserum is made t o react with the seminal fluid, blood , or saliva. A positive test will confirm human origin. Option D: Breslau's second life test is done to determine whether a child was born alive or not.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: The autopsy of a victim reveals similar findings seen in the given image. Which of the following would have caused this injury?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows 'tram-line' bruising. It would have most likely been produced by a stick or an iron rod. It occurs when the skin surface is struck by a rod or rectangular sectioned object. The weapon sinks into the skin on impact. This causes the edges to drag the skin downwards and the traction, t ears the marginal blood vessels. The centre compresses the skin. This causes little or no damage to the vessels in the absence of underlying bone.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: In a 45-year-old man with a history of burning, the following finding was seen. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows a 'Marjolin ulcer' which is a rare type of SCC (squamous cell carcinoma) that arises in sites of chronic wounds or scars. The malignant transformation is slow, with an average latency time of approx 30 years. The tumor may initially present as: • Ulceration • Nodules • Rolled or everted wound margins • Excessive granulation tissue • A rapid increase in size • Bleeding on touch.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient presents with a skin lesion, as shown in the image below. Which of the following is least likely to cause it?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a scald injury. A chemical fire is going to cause a burn, not a scald. Scalds are sharply demarcated lesions with reddening, desquamation, and blistering. When tipped or splashed, the hot liquid runs under gravity so that trickle patterns may be seen.159 It is caused due to tissue damage from hot liquids like: • Hot water • Hot oils • Molten rubber • Liquid chemicals • Steam.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: While performing an autopsy on a burn victim, the following cutaneous findings were noted. What is the term used to describe these burns?
mcqs.explanation: The term used to describe the burns shown in the image is filigree burn or arborescent burn or Lichtenberg's flower or feathering. It is a finding in burns due to lightning. The fern-like pattern of erythema in the skin indicates the path taken by the electrical discharge. It usually occurs over the shoulder or the flanks within an hour of the injury and disappears in a160 day or two. It occurs due to the rupture of small vessels and is seen in a fern-like pattern or the branching of a tree. Option B: When the skin is in firm contact with an electrical conductor, splitting of the layers of the epidermis or those of the epidermal-dermal junction. This may in turn produce a raised blister known as a Joule burn. The image below shows a Joule burn:Option C: When the contact is less firm, an air gap is formed between the skin and the conductor. Thus the current traverses the gap as a spark. This leads to a distinct hard brownish keratin nodule raised above the surrounding surface known as a spark lesion. Option A: Crocodile skin effect is caused by high-tension current burns, where the voltage is in the multi-kilovolt range, sparking may occur over many centimeters. This can cause multiple spark lesions giving rise to a c rocodile-skin e ffect . The image below shows multiple spark lesions and the inset shows the crocodile skin effect:161 Image below shows the various electrical marks.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following marked distances is described as the caliber of a rifled gun?
mcqs.explanation: The caliber of a rifled gun is described as the marked distance C in the image. Caliber is measured as the distance between two diametrically opposite lands. It is the i nternal dimension of the barrel and is measured in millimeters or inches.Note: For a smooth barrel weapon, it is measured as the distance between two diametrically opposite points on the inner circumference.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: A victim of child trafficking was brought to you by the police for age determination. Which of the following would you use as an accurate method for determining the same?
mcqs.explanation: From the given options, mineralization of teeth is the more accurate method of age determination in childhood. The relationship between the chronological age and dental age is stronger than between chronological age and skeletal age. Two aspects of tooth development have been used in the estimation of dental age: • The emergence of teeth - superior part of the crown of the tooth appearing level with the surface of the alveolar bone • The stage of mineralization of crowns and r oots during development Estimation of dental age using mineralization stages of crowns and roots of developing teeth includes visualization from a radiographic image. This helps in viewing both erupted and unerupted teeth. It is a more accurate method of estimating age than emergence, because emergence is an event whose exact time of occurrence is not accurately known. The study of dental microstructure is the most accurate method of age determination in childhood . T his involves counting perikymata (incremental lines on the surface of tooth enamel). Note : Eruption is a continuous process by which a tooth moves from its crypt in the jaw bone to its position of occlusion in the mouth. It is different from emergence. Emergence denotes that a tooth has pierced the gingiva.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: When does the fusion of the spheno-occipital suture usually occur in females?
mcqs.explanation: The spheno-occipital suture fuses by about 18–20 years in females and by about 20–22 years in males. The timing of cranial suture closure was one of the first techniques used to estimate the age of adult individuals. The spheno-occipital suture on the skull base is particularly useful for aging young adults. The other cranial sutures show more variation in the timing of closure. Sagittal suture is used for age determination. Sutures ossify on the endocranial surface befo re t hey ossify on the ectocranial surface, and this must also be taken into account when using this method. Overall, this method of age determination is less reliable. Age of fusion of skull sutures:Suture Age of fusio n Metopic suture 2-4 years Spheno -occipital suture 18-22 years Posterior third of sagittal sut ure 30-40 years Anterior third of sagittal sutu re 40-50 years Middle third of sagittal sutur e 50-60 years Coronal suture 40-50 years Sphenotemporal suture 50-60 years Squamous temporal suture >80 years17

mcqs.question: The forensic department has received the post mortem remains of a partly decayed body recovered from the outskirts near an international airport. They notice that oval cross-section of hair is seen on the scalp. What would have been the likely race of the person?
mcqs.explanation: Round or ovoid cross section of hair is found in caucasian race. Race determination from hair:Hair cross section Race Elliptical Negroid s Round to Ovoid Caucaso ids Circular/ Cylindrical Mongol oids

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the Bertillon system used for?
mcqs.explanation: The Bertillon system is used for identification based on anthropometry. The origins of forensic anthropology can be traced to the end of the nineteenth century when the French criminologist Alphonse Bertillon devised the first classification and identification system to identify criminals, based on anthropometry.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: While investigating a case of homicide, the forensic team finds that the fingerprints left behind have no delta forma tion. W hich fingerprint pattern is described here?
mcqs.explanation: Plain arches have no delta. Classification of fingerprints into different patterns is based on delta and core formation. Delta is a triangular arrangement formed where three separate ridge line flows come together. Core is the centermost portion of a ridge flow pattern. The number of delta and core for each pattern is given below. The image given below shows the delta and core in the different fingerprint patterns. For each type, the position of the core is marked with a green c ircle, and the delta is marked with a blue triangle.Pattern Delta Core Loop 1 Plain arc h 0 Tented ar ch 1 delta at the base of the upth rust Whorl 2 Accident al >2 Note: Dactylography or dermatoglyphics is the study of fingerprint patterns. The first fingerprint bureau in India was established in Kolkata.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: A deceased male was brought to the morgue for a \037post-mortem examination. His relatives reported that he had a tattoo over his skin, which was not found on examination. Which of th e following structures would you examine?
mcqs.explanation: The lymph nodes should be examined in this case. Some amount of material or dye used for creating tattoo marks is transported through lymph to the regional lymph nodes. Hence, in cases where a tattoo mark has disappeared naturally or has been removed, the lymph nodes must be examined.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: What is Zasko's phenomenon related to?
mcqs.explanation: Zasko's phenomenon/ tendon reaction is related to muscular changes following death. It is elicited in the quadriceps femoris muscle. Striking the lower third of the muscle about 10 cms above the patella with a reflex hammer causes upward movement of the patella due to contraction of the muscle. It can be seen 1 to 2 hours after death.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements are true about cadaveric rigidity in contrast to cadaveric spasm?
mcqs.explanation: Cadaveric rigidity is also known as rigor mortis. It is due to the depletion of ATP and indicates time since death. Muscle stiffening is not marked a nd can be overcome by moderate force. The rigor starts occurring 1-2 hours after death (postmortem nature) and muscles do not respond to electrical stimuli. Cadaveric spasm / instantaneous rigor/ cataleptic rigidity/ death clutch is a phenomenon where a group of muscles in a state of contraction at the time of death remains contracted after death until molecular death occurs.91 Cadaveric spasm is an antemortem phenomenon and occurs immediately after death. There is no stage of primary relaxation. It is seen in cases of deaths coupled with emotional disturbances like: • In cases of excitement, fear, severe pain • Exhaustion at the time of death • Cerebral hemorrhage • Injury to the nervous system • Drowning • Strychnine poisoning Examples: • In case of drowning, weeds and grass caught in hand during struggle remain firmly grasped even after death. This i ndicates that the person was alive when entering the water • In case of suicides, weapons remain firmly grasped in the hand

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the odor of the mummified body?
mcqs.explanation: The mummified body is odorless.95

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: An ASHA worker brings the body of a newborn to casualty saying that the child was delivered dead at home. You suspect it as live birth and request an autopsy. All of the following will confirm a live birth except:

options.a: Presence of milk in the stomach
options.c: Presence of meconium in the large bowel

mcqs.explanation: The absence (and not presence) of meconium in the large bowel is a confirmatory sign of live birth. Confirmatory signs of live birth: • Presence of milk in the stomach • Absence of meconium in the large bowel, exception being breech d elivery. • Exfoliation of skin • Closure of fetal channels • Changes in the umbilical cord Live birth can be excluded if : • Signs of maceration are present104 • Signs of immaturity are present. If the child has not attained the viable age (7 months), it could not have been born alive.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following sites is more prone to bruising with blunt trauma?
mcqs.explanation: The shins are particularly prone to bruising with blunt trauma. Resilient areas, such as the abdominal wall and buttocks, bruise less with a given impact. The head, chest, and shins are more prone to bruising. This is because these regions have underlying bone and less subcutaneous tissue.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: You are examining the body of a patient who was found dead at his house. Multiple linear incised wounds are noted on the ulnar border of the forearm. What are these suggestive of?
mcqs.explanation: In the given scenario, multiple linear incised wounds on the inner side (ulnar border) of the forearm are most likely to be defence wounds. They are sustained when a victim is trying to protect himself from attacks (homicide). The attack may be by fists, feet, and blunt or sharp instruments.122 In case of a blunt instrument, fist or feet: • Bruises are most common along with abrasions • Commonly on the extensor and ulnar aspect of the forearms, wrists, back of the hand, and knuckles • May be seen on thighs due to an attempt to protect genitals In the case of a sharp instrument: • Seen on the ulnar side of the forearm, wrist, hand, and fingers • Cuts on the flexures of phalanges occur if the victim tries to seize the weapon Firearm injury: • Arms may be used to shield the trunk or head f rom the blast • An entrance and an exit wound in the upper arm may be seen • The missile may then re-penetrate the trunk Options C and D: Tentative cuts or hesitation wounds are self-inflicted wounds made while attempting to commit suicide.They are usually on the radial side of the forearm.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following scoring systems is used to assess the risk of mortality in a burns patient?
mcqs.explanation: The Baux score was used for many years to predict mortality in burns. Baux score: Mortality risk = age + %TBSA Advancements in burn care have lowered overall mortality to the point that the Baux score may no longer be accurate. However, age and burn size, as well as inhalation injury, continues to be the most robust indicators for burn mortality.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: In which of the following condition can Curling's ulcer be seen?
mcqs.explanation: Curling's ulcers are seen in burn victims. This is seen due to intravascular depletion leading to mucosal ischemia and disruption of the protective m ucosal barrier. H2 -receptor antagonists or PPIs have proved effective against the development of stress gastritis. Note: Brain tumors, traumatic head injury, and other intracranial processes including infections can cause increased intracranial pressure. This leads to overstimulation of the vagus nerve. As a result, increased secretion of gastric acid may occur which leads to gastro-duodenal ulcer formation known as Cushing's ulcer.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following are constituents of smokeless gunpowder?
mcqs.explanation: Smokeless gunpowder contains nitroglycerine, nitrocellulose and nitroguanidine.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: The lead fragments when stripped from the bullet as it travels through the body, cause multiple fragments along the wound track. What is this phenomenon called?
mcqs.explanation: Lead snowstorm is the phenomenon caused by a firearm wound, when lead fragments are stripped from the bullet as it travels through the body. It causing multiple fragments t o be present along the wound track. This phenomenon is caused by semi-jacketed hunting ammunition used in rifled guns.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: A 33-year-old man who was found dead in his home was taken for a postmortem examination. It revealed clogging of the respiratory tract by semi-digested food particles consisting of rice and vegetable matter. This would fall under which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of suffocation due to aspiration of food particles. It is classified under mechanical asphyxia. Mechanical asphyxia can be classified depending on the respiratory block: • Compression / constriction of the neck - Hanging, strangulation, throttling • Blocking external orifices of respiration, i.e. mouth and/or nostrils - Smothering, overlying, suffocation, gagging • Impaction of foreign bodies in respiratory tract - Choking • Compression a nd mechanical fixation of the chest and abdomen preventing the respiratory movements - Traumatic asphyxia / crush asphyxia • Inhalation of fluid into the respiratory tract - Drowning200

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: Police were investigating a serial killer who hangs his victims upside down which eventually led to their death. What is the most likely cause of death in these victims?
mcqs.explanation: In an inverted crucifixion, death occurs due to postural asphyxia. In the case of inverted crucifixion, asphyxia occurs a s a result of the impedance of inspiration by the weight of the abdominal viscera upon the diaphragm.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: Seminal stains are found near the penis on the legs of a victim brought to you for autopsy. These stains are an absolute indicator of which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: The finding of emission of semen at autopsy is a non-specific finding and does not indicate sexual activity or any particular mode of death.211 The mere emission of semen found at autopsy does not confirm sexual activity in itself, as post-mortem discharge of semen from the meatus is common in any type of death, not only in asphyxia.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following electrolytes is measured in Gettler's test?
mcqs.explanation: Gettler's test measures the chloride content of left and right side of the heart. A difference of 25 mg% in chloride concentrations between the two sides of the heart is an indication of death due to drowning. This test was used to identify the cause of drowning. • Freshwater drowning - chloride content of left heart is lower than that of the right heart • Saltwater drowning - chloride content of right heart is lower than that of t he left heart Gettler 's claims have been refuted and the test is no longer accepted.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: In India, what is the minimum age for a boy to be charged with rape?
mcqs.explanation: In India, there is no age limit under which a boy is considered physically incapable of committing rape. In such cases, the development of a child along with the development of sexual organs is taken into consideration while deciding if he is capable of performing rape or not. The court decides the question of potency on case to case basis.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: A 19-year-old boy is brought to the doctor because his family found him dressed a s a woman. He says that he derives sexual pleasure from this act. However, he has no wish to undergo sex-change surgery. What is this type of perversion called?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of fetishistic transvestism.235 It is a paraphilia characterized by recurrent sexually arousing fantasies, sexual urges, or behavior involving the wearing of clothes of the opposite sex and appearing as a member of the opposite sex. It is also called transvestic fetishism. It is usually seen in males who obtain sexual pleasure by wearing female clothes. Fetishistic transvestism is a paraphilia whereas transvestism is a gender identity disorder. There is no hormonal/genital abnormality in fetishis tic t ransvestism. Option A: Transsexualism refers to an obsessional desire to become a member of the opposite sex and seek surgery for anatomical alterations. Option C: Frotteurism refers to a person who obtains sexual gratification by contact with another person (rubbing his private parts against female buttocks, breasts, or thighs, in public places). It is punishable under Sec 292 BNS (Section 290 IPC), with a fine of up to 1000 rupees. Option D: Gender dysphoria is a term t hat describes a sense of unease that a person has due to a mismatch between their biological sex and their gender identity. This sense of unease or dissatisfaction can lead to depression and anxiety and can have a harmful impact on daily life.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: In which of the following conditions is Robert's sign seen?
mcqs.explanation: Robert's sign is a radiological sign which refers to the presence of a gas shadow within the chambers of the heart or the greater vessels like aorta. It is seen in cases of foetal death in utero. It is a sign of maceration.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: Posthumous child is a

options.a: Child delivered after the death of parents
options.b: Child delivered after the death of biological father

mcqs.explanation: The child delivered after the death of the biological father, or a child delivered after the death of the biological mother, usually when delivered by a cesarean section is a posthumous child. Illegitimate child is a child born out of wedlock i.e. when the parents are n ot married. Supposititious child or fictitious child is when a woman pretends to go through pregnancy and delivery. Later, she produces a living child as her own for obtaining money or for the purpose of claiming the property.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: A servant adds sleeping pills to his master's food with the intention of robbery. Under which section of the BNS would he be charged?
mcqs.explanation: This man would be charged with BNS Section 123 (IPC 328) which deals with administering poison/ any stupefying, intoxicating, or unwholesome drug, with the intention of causing hurt or committing an offense. Option A: BNS Section 106 (IPC 304A) deals with causing death by negligence. Option B: BNS S ection 122 (IPC 334) deals with voluntarily causing hurt / grievous hurt on sudden provocation. Option D: BNS Section 117 (IPC 322 ) deals with voluntarily causing grievous hurt.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: In which of the following patients is performing gastric lavage an absolute contraindication?

options.a: A patient with a history of kerosene consumption
options.b: A patient with a history of acetaminophen overdose
options.c: A patient with a history of tricyclic antidepressant overdose
options.d: A patient with a history of opioid poisoning

mcqs.explanation: Gastric lavage is not done in a case of kerosene poisoning. It can cause aspiration and pneumonitis. Gastric lavage is rarely indicated as the procedure has numerous complications. It may be considered in cases where there is recent (<1 hour) ingestion of life-threatening amounts of a toxin, for which there is no treat ment o nce absorbed. With drugs that slow down gastrointestinal motility or cause pylorospasm (e.g., anticholinergics, opioids, salicylates), lavage can be done up to 24 hours.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: Why is forced acidic diuresis not recommended as a treatment in case of poisoning?

options.a: It can cause acute liver injury
options.c: I t can cause cardiac arrhythmia

mcqs.explanation: Forced acidic diuresis is not indicated in any scenario as its potential risks (such as rhabdomyolysis, a cute renal injury) outweigh any potential benefits. Note: Though some books say that acidic diuresis is indicated in few poisoning, it is only theoretic. Forced acidic diuresis is never indicated due to the associated risks.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: You are suspecting organophosphorus poisoning in a farmer who presented with chronic fatigue and urinary incontinence. What would be the most accurate investigation to assess potential toxicity?

options.d: Urinary levels of o rganophosphorus compound metabolites

mcqs.explanation: RBC cholinesterase enzyme activity is the most accurate indicator to assess potential organophosphorus (OP) toxicity. I t is an indicator of synaptic cholinesterase inhibition. However , plasma butyrylcholinesterase is easier to assay and more easily available. Hence, it is more commonly used. Measurement of parent compound in blood and metabolites urine are rarely carried out in a clinical setting. Note: The correlation between cholinesterase activity, clinical symptoms, and atropine dose is inconsistent. Hence, treatment should be guided predominately by clinical symptoms.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: In which of the following conditions will you use calcium gluconate for management in an emergency?
mcqs.explanation: Calcium gluconate is used in the management of hypocalcemia(in oxalic acid and hydrofluoric acid poisoning), and cardiotoxicity(in hyperkalemia and hypermagnesemia). Calcium gluconate is not used in the management of hypomagnesemia and hypokalemia.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the drug of choice for cyanide toxicity?
mcqs.explanation: Hydroxocobalamin and sodium thiosulfate are the preferred antidotes in cyanide toxicity. • If hydroxocobalamin is available, give hydroxocobalamin a nd sodium thiosulfate. • If hydroxocobalamin is not available, give amyl nitrite and sodium nitrite and sodium thiosulfate. Avoid nitrites if the patient has contraindications to nitrites. Hydroxocobalamin is preferred over sodium nitrite as it does not interfere with the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood. Also, sodium nitrite can induce fatal methemoglobinemia in patients who are critically ill from another cause. Mechanism of action of antidotes: D icobalt EDTA can also bind cyanide, but it causes severe side effects.Mechanism of antidote Example Binding of cyanide Direct binding of cyanide , fol lowed by clearance Hydroxocobalamin Induction of methemoglobin emia When cyanide binds methem oglobin, a relatively less toxic cyanomethemoglobin is for med Sodium nitriteAmyl nitrit e291 Mechanism of antidote Example Use of sulfur donors This involves maximizing the availability of sulfur donors f or rhodanese , a ubiquitous e nzyme that detoxifies cyanide by transforming it to thiocya nate Sodium thiosulfate

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old man with acute alcohol intoxication was being tested in the ER. When stimulated by pinching, his pupils dilated with a slow return. What is this sign called?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario is suggestive of McEwan's sign. Pupils are contracted, but stimulating the person (e.g., pinching or slapping) causes them to dilate, with a slow return. This is a characteristic finding of ethanol toxicity, seen at BAC levels >250 mg%.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient with calcium oxalate monohydrate crystals in the urine is diagnosed with ethylene glycol poisoning. What is the drug of choice for treating this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Fomepizole is the drug of choice for the treatment of ethylene glycol poisoning. Treatment of ethylene glycol poisoning: • Fomepizole (preferred) or ethanol (if fomepizole is unavailable) - inhibits the enzyme alcohol dehydrogenase • Sodium bicarbonate - correct systemic acidosis • Hemodialysis - for elevated toxic alcohol l evels, severe acid-base derangements, or evidence of end-organ toxicity • Co-factors (folic acid, thiamine, and pyridoxine) - optimizes non-toxic metabolic pathways for the elimination of parent alcohol or its metabolites304

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: A 34-year-old man presented to the ER with severe dehydration and weakness. History was suggestive of multiple episodes of watery diarrhea and non-bilious vomiting since morning. His breath reeked of garlic odor. ECG showed QT prolongation. Which o f the following samples must be collected for a definitive diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario points towards the diagnosis of acute arsenic poisoning. For a definitive diagnosis, the arsenic levels are measured in 24-hour urine samples. If the baseline urinary level is within normal limits and arsenic intoxication is still suspected, hair and nail clippings should be harvested for laboratory analysis. Due to the rapid distribution of arse nic i n tissues, blood arsenic levels are unreliable.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.question: The ouch-ouch disease is due to the toxicity of which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: Itai-Itai disease (Japan), also called ouch-ouch disease is due to bone pain caused by cadmium. Cadmium causes nephrotoxicity leading to hypercalciuria. This subsequently causes osteomalacia leading to bone pain.

mcqs.subject: Forensic Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Organic Irritants - Plant and Animal Poisons
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the characteristic clinical feature seen in a patient with aconite poisoning?
mcqs.explanation: The characteristic finding of aconite toxicity is numbness and tingling. Aconite is also known as monk's hood or wolf's bane. The roots are the most poisonous part of the plant and are mistaken for horseradish root. The toxic principle is aconitine. It acts on the voltage-sensitive sodium channels of the cell m embranes of excitable tissues. Aconitine first stimulates and then paralyzes the peripheral terminations of sensory and secretory nerves, CNS, and nerves of the myocardium, skeletal and smooth muscles. Patients present mainly with a combination of gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, and neurological features. Numbness and tingling are characteristic features. The fatal period is 2-6 hours. Aconite is commonly used for homicidal poisoning because: • Cheap a nd e asily available • Short fatal period • Extremely unstable and destroyed by putrefaction

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old woman presented to the clinic with the lesions shown below . Which of the following conditions is/are associated with this lesion?
mcqs.explanation: The lesions shown in the image are spider naevi (nevus araneus). They are seen in: • Estrogen excess states such as pregnancy and OCP use18 • Chronic liver disease - especially alcoholic liver disease • Thyrotoxicosis They are vascular lesions characterized by the tortuous dilatation of arterioles just underneath the skin . On applying and releasing pressure over the lesion they typically fill from the centre outward .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: You observed the following finding in a patient in the OPD. Which among the following conditions is least likely to cause this finding?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows digital clubbing. Among the given options , aortic dissection is least likely to cause digital clubbing . Clubbing is a selective bulbous enlargement of the distal segments of the fingers and toes due to the proliferation of connective tissue , particularly on the dorsal surface . Causes of clubbing are: • Pulmonary • Bronchogenic carcinoma • Lung abscess , empyema , bronchiectasis • Interstitial lung diseases • Cystic fibrosis • Sarcoidosis • Asbestosis • GI • Inflammatory bowel disease (Ulcerative colitis , Crohn's disease ) • Sprue , celiac disease • Neoplasms - esophagus , liver, bowel • Cirrhosis - juvenile and biliary • Chronic active hepatitis • Cardiovascular • Cyanotic congenital heart disease • Subacute bacterial endocarditis • Aortic aneurysm • Arteriovenous fistula • Patent ductus arteriosus with right to left shunt • Atrial myxoma • Endocrine • Grave's disease (thyroid acropachy)19 • CNS • Hemiplegia (unilateral clubbing ) • Skin disease • Palmoplantar keratoderma • Fischer-Volavsek syndrome. • Malignancies • Thyroid cancer • Thymus cancer • Hodgkin disease • Disseminated chronic myeloid leukemia. Note : Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) does not cause clubbing . If clubbing is present in a patient with COPD, underlying lung cancer and bronchiectasis must be ruled out.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old patient presents with loss of appetite , jaundice , and easy bruisability. He is a chronic alcohol user, and the following abnormality is noted on examination. What is the most likely cause of this nail change?
mcqs.explanation: The nail change seen in the given image is leukonychia totalis . It is a prominent feature of hypoalbuminemic states . The given clinical scenario is suggestive of liver cirrhosis, which leads to hypoalbuminemia . Leukonychia is an opaque whitish discoloration of the nail and is seen in the following conditions: • Dietary deficiency : Protein-energy malnutrition, pellagra , zinc deficiency • Drugs: Cytotoxic agents , Steroids , Retinoids, Pilocarpine • Dermatological pathology : Alopecia areata, erythema multiforme , exfoliative dermatitis, and SLE • Systemic diseases : Liver cirrhosis, renal failure, and cardiac failure • Miscellaneous : Trauma , malignancy, and toxins (arsenic, fluoride ) • Idiopathic Note : The leukonychia secondary to arsenic poisoning is termed leukonychia striata or Aldrich–Mees lines.20

mcqs.subject: Medicine
