mcqs.question: A patient with rheumatic heart disease now presents with fever and the following nail finding. The nail lesions most likely are?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of infective endocarditis (IE). Splinter hemorrhages are seen in the nails of these patients .23 Subungual splinter hemorrhages are classically identified as dark -red, linear petechiae in the nail bed . Other peripheral manifestations of infective endocarditis include the following : • Petechiae : Common but nonspecific finding • Purulent purpura • Osler nodes : Tender subcutaneous nodules usually found on the distal pads of the digits • Janeway lesions : Nontender maculae on the palms and soles • Roth spots : Relatively rare retinal hemorrhages with small, clear centers

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old man presented to the OPD with a fever for the past 5 days. On examination, tender lesions were found on his extremities as marked below . What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The most probable diagnosis for this patient is infective endocarditis . Tender violaceous subcutaneous nodules in the fingers shown in the image are Osler nodes . They usually occur in the pads of fingers and toes but can also occur on the thenar and hypothenar eminences . Other lesions that are highly suggestive of infective endocarditis include : • Roth spots : These are exudative , edematous hemorrhagic lesions of the retina with pale centres . • Janeway lesions : They are nontender, slightly raised haemorrhages on the palms and soles . The image is shown below .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: In the given acid-base nomogram diagram, areas marked A and D indicate which of the following conditions?

options.a: Chronic respiratory acidosis, acute metabolic alkalosis
options.b: Acute Metabolic alkalosis, acute respiratory acidosis
options.c: Acute respiratory acidosis, acute respiratory alkalosis
options.d: Acute respiratory acidosis, acute metabolic alkalosis

mcqs.explanation: In the given illustrated acid-base nomogram, the letters A and D indicate acute respiratory acidosis and acute respiratory alkalosis. An acid-base nomogram, also known as a Davenport diagram, is a graphical representation of acid-base balance to interpret arterial blood gas (ABG) results . It helps determine the primary acid-base disorder and identify compensatory mechanisms.47 The y-axis of the acid-base nomogram represents the arterial bicarbonate (HCO3-) levels , and the x-axis represents the arterial pH values. The shaded areas are the range of values of the normal respiratory and metabolic compensations for primary acid-base disturbances .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A middle -aged man presented to the OPD with complaints of difficulty in chewing and a gradual change in voice over the last year. Examination revealed coarse facial features . The image of his hand (right side ) compared to the physician's hand is shown below . Which of the following long-term complications would you not commonly see in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: 64 The given scenario and the enlarged hands in the patient , as shown in the image, point towards a diagnosis of acromegaly. Diabetes insipidus is not a feature of acromegaly, but diabetes mellitus can develop in patients with acromegaly. Clinical features of acromegaly are: Note : Diabetes insipidus can be seen as a complication post Transsphenoidal Surgery for pituitary adenomas and other sellar tumours not as complication of Acromegaly per se.System Features Musculoskeletal GigantismPrognathism (protr usion of jaw)Carpal tunnel sy ndromeParesthesia (due to n erve entrapment )Proximal m yopathyHypertrophy of front al bones Skin and soft tissues Acral enlargement in hands a nd feet (due to thickening of soft tissues )HyperhidrosisAc anthosis nigricans and skin t ags Visceralomegaly Enlargement of most organs especially the tongue , thyroid, salivary gland, liver, spleen , kidney, and prostate Ophthalmic Visual field defects (macro-pi tuitary adenoma)Ophthalmo plegia (cranial nerve palsy )H eadache Metabolic Low renin with increased ald osteroneDiabetes mellitus (du e to GH-induced insulin resis tance)Hypercalcemia , hyperp hosphatemia , and hypercalci uriaHypertriglyceridemia Reproductive Loss of libido and impotence in malesMenstrual abnormali ties and galactorrhea Cardiopulmonary Left ventricular hypertrophy / septal hypertrophyHypertens ionObstructive sleep apnea65

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: The middle -aged man shown in the image, noticed that his shoes no longer fit him and his finger ring is getting tightened . Insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) levels are elevated . Which of the following tests will help to confirm the diagnosis?

options.a: Insulin-like Growth Factor -1 Binding Protein - 3 (IGFBP-3) level

mcqs.explanation: The given scenario and the presence of coarse facial features and prognathism, as shown in the image, points towards a diagnosis of acromegaly. An oral glucose tolerance test with GH levels is used to confirm acromegaly.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 10 -year-old boy is referred for evaluation of progressively worsening headaches and visual field defects . An MRI brain is done and shows the following findings. Which of the following statements is incorrect about this condition?

options.b: Surgery is curative in most patients
options.d: Calcifications are seen in adamantinomatous type

mcqs.explanation: The given MRI showing a suprasellar mass with calcifications is suggestive of a craniopharyngioma . Surgery is not curative in the majority of patients as the tumor is adherent to surrounding structures . They are benign epithelial cell -containing tumors and are of two types : • Adamantinomatous - calcifications and keratin nodules are seen • Papillary - calcifications are rare Biopsy reveals machinery or motor-oil-like fluid within the cyst that contains cholesterol crystals. The treatment of choice is transcranial or transsphenoidal resection . It must be followed by postoperative radiation to prevent recurrence.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: The radio-iodine uptake scan of a patient evaluated for swelling of the thyroid is shown below . Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given image showing localized overactivity (increased uptake ) in the left lobe of the thyroid i.e., hot nodule , with suppression of the remainder of the gland, is suggestive of a hypersecreting adenoma. Other options : Option B: The likelihood of malignancies like papillary Carcinoma thyroid is low (5%) in the case of a hot nodule . Option C: Graves disease shows diffusely increased uptake on a thyroid scan. Option D: Lateral aberrant thyroid presents with swelling of cervical lymph nodes and not thyroid. It is due to skip metastasis from papillary thyroid carcinoma to the ipsilateral cervical lymph nodes . The thyroid scan appearance in different conditions is shown in the image below :120 Diagnostic isotope studies , such as 99mTc -pertechnetate and iodine-123 , are becoming less common in thyroid imaging because some warm swellings (5%) which are actually malignant could be mistaken as benign. Isotope scanning is most valuable when assessing a hyperthyroid patient presenting with a nodule or nodularity in the thyroid. It helps to identify overactivity in the gland, which can differentiate between a toxic nodule that suppresses the rest of the gland and a toxic multinodular goitre with multiple areas of increased uptake .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs can cause the condition shown below ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows the absence of scalp hair and skin, along with calvarial defects (skull bone defects ), suggestive of aplasia cutis congenita . This is commonly associated with carbimazole and methimazole . These drugs can also cause other defects such as: • Choanal atresia • Tracheoesophageal fistula • Fetal goiter

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 31 -year-old woman is rushed to the ED with a severe headache and vomiting. Past history includes a total thyroidectomy for thyroid cancer 3 months ago. Her BP is 200 /100 mm Hg and pulse is 110 /min. On examination, a marfanoid habitus is noted along with the findings shown. Which of the following is likely to be predominantly elevated ?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario with a history of thyroid cancer (likely medullary carcinoma ) and the image showing mucosal neuromas points towards MEN2B syndrome. Her current presentation is suggestive of a pheochromocytoma . She is likely to have predominantly elevated levels of epinephrine and its metabolite , metanephrine . This is due to the higher expression of the PNMT enzyme associated with the mutations in MEN2 syndromes (both 2A and 2B ). The higher levels of epinephrine result in a more symptomatic presentation . In contrast, low PNMT expression is seen in von -Hippel -Lindau (VHL ) syndrome. This leads to a predominant elevation of norepinephrine and normetanephrine levels . It is less symptomatic compared to MEN2 syndrome.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old woman visits a gynecologist with complaints of irregular and infrequent menstrual cycles . She is also upset that she has gained 12 kg over the past few months. Her face appears as shown in the image below . Her blood pressure at this visit is 144/98 mm Hg and she has multiple purple striae over her abdomen. Which of the following investigations should you advise this patient ?

options.c: Serum testosterone levels and abdominal USG

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario along with the image showing moon facies with acne and hirsutism are suggestive of Cushing's syndrome. It can be diagnosed with the help of a single midnight serum cortisol measurement . Option A: Cosyntropin (ACTH) stimulation test is used for the diagnosis of Addison's disease . Options C and D: Serum testosterone , abdominal USG, and LH : FSH ratio, are used to confirm a diagnosis of the polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS). Though PCOS can present with similar features , it is not typically associated with moon facies , purple striae, or hypertension .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old woman was diagnosed with Hashimoto's thyroiditis and was started on levothyroxine 2 weeks ago. She now presents to your clinic with abdominal pain and dizziness. The left and right images below show her current appearance and her appearance last month, respectively . Which of the following is not a feature of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given image showing skin hyperpigmentation in a patient with severe dizziness and a history of autoimmune thyroiditis points to a diagnosis of Addison's disease . Hyperglycemia is not a feature of this condition. Hypocortisolism leads to hypoglycemia in these patients . Addison's disease is primary adrenal insufficiency characterized by the disruption of glucocorticoid , mineralocorticoid, and androgen secretion . Primary adrenal insufficiency is most commonly caused by autoimmune adrenalitis and coincident autoimmune disease occurring in these patients most frequently includes thyroid autoimmune disease , vitiligo, and premature ovarian failure. Clinical features of Addison's disease :160 Hormone Clinical features Hypoaldosteronism Abdominal pain, nausea, vo miting, salt craving Dizziness, postural hypotensi on AKI due to volume depletion Hyponatremia Hyperkalemia, metabolic aci dosis Hypocortisolism Anorexia, weight loss, fatigue , myalgia, arthralgia Fever (increased IL -1) Depression Postural hypotension Hypoglycemia Hyponatremia (loss of feedba ck inhibition of ADH) Slightly increased TSH (loss of feedback inhibition) Hypoandrogenism Loss of libido Loss of pubic and axillary hai r Elevated ACTH HyperpigmentationLevothyroxine can precipitate adrenal insufficiency or crisis in undiagnosed patients . In patients with concurrent adrenal insufficiency and hypothyroidism , a course of steroids must be given before giving thyroid replacement .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Diabetes Mellitus: Complications and their Mana...
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old diabetic woman presents to the OPD with the following skin lesions . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given image showing irregular plaques with yellowish discoloration and telangiectasias are suggestive of necrobiosis lipoidica diabeticorum. It is an inflammatory granulomatous disorder of the skin due to collagen degeneration and lipid deposition . It is usually seen in young women with diabetes mellitus . The lesions usually begin in the pretibial region. It begins as papules that gradually enlarge and darken to form erythematous plaques with irregular margins, atrophic centers , and central ulceration. Option A: Necrolytic migratory erythema is a feature of glucagonoma . It is a waxing and waning rash that appears as shown below .Option B: Diabetic dermopathy or shin spots are commonly seen in elderly men. It presents as pigmented pretibial papules as shown below .206 Option D: Granuloma annulare presents with small papules arranged in an annular pattern. There is no yellowish discoloration or telangiectasias, as shown below .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A soldier posted in Siachen is brought unconscious to the emergency ward. In order to rule out hypothermia , how will you best measure his temperature ?
mcqs.explanation: In the given clinical scenario, the rectal temperature would be the best site to measure the core body temperature . At extremes of high or low temperatures , like in Siachen, the axillary and the oral temperatures are highly misleading and should not be used to measure the core body temperature . The infrared tympanic thermometer measures the temperature of the eardrum which is representative of the core body temperature. However, it often ends up measuring the temperature of the ear canal. This is because of inadequate insertion into the ear canal due to poor manufacturing design or the presence of cerumen. Hence , it is not a reliable method of measuring the core body temperature .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: The arterial blood gas findings of a patient are pH = 7.12, pCO2 = 50, HCO3 = 28. What is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The above findings give the diagnosis of respiratory acidosis with metabolic compensation . Interpretation of the ABG: Step 1: pH is reduced (7.12), hence acidosis. Step 2: Since pCO2 is raised (50 mmHg), it is respiratory acidosis. Step 3: HCO3 is raised (28 mEq/L ) suggesting there is metabolic compensation .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What levels of prolactin are definitely suggestive of prolactinoma?
mcqs.explanation: The diagnosis of a prolactinoma is highly likely when prolactin levels are > �Mg/L. The normal range of serum prolactin (PRL ) is 5-20 �Mg/L. Prolactin levels < �Mg/L can be due to non-functioning pituitary adenomas or non-neoplastic causes of hyperprolactinemia . MRI brain must be done in all patients with hyperprolactinemia. Prolactinoma are tumors arising from the lactotroph cells of the pituitary gland, they can be classified as microadenoma(<1cm in diameter , usually non invasive ) or macroadenoma(>1cm, locally invasive to adjacent structures ). Clinical features include amenorrhea, infertility , and galactorrhea in women, impotence , loss of libido, infertility in men and if tumor extends beyond sella , there can be visual field defects and other mass effects . Treatment - In asymptomatic patients and those where fertility is not desired , they do not require treatment and can be monitored using regular PRL measurements and MRI. In symptomatic microadenoma cases , oral dopamine agonists (cabergoline and bromocriptine) form the main treatment for hyperprolactinemia and reduction of tumor volume. For macroadenoma, before starting dopamine agonists visual field testing is to be done , and reassess it with MRI changes every 6-12 month intervals until maximum reduction is achieved , in unresponsive cases consider surgery.75

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following patients cannot undergo radioiodine therapy ?
mcqs.explanation: Lactating mothers cannot undergo radioiodine therapy . Pregnancy and breastfeeding are absolute contraindications of radioiodine therapy . Patients can safely conceive 6 months after undergoing radioiodine treatment . Radioiodine therapy in patients with severe ophthalmopathy can be given with caution along with prednisone to prevent exacerbation of ophthalmopathy .121

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following causes ACTH-dependent Cushing's syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Cushing's disease causes ACTH-dependent Cushing's syndrome. It occurs due to an ACTH-secreting pituitary adenoma.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Diabetes Mellitus: Types, Clinical Features and...
mcqs.question: Which of the following would cause type 1 diabetes in an adult patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Type 1 diabetes mellitus in an adult is suggestive of latent autoimmune diabetes in adults (LADA ). LADA is common in thin-built adults between 30-50 years and is associated with autoantibodies . As the progression of the disease is less rapid than in children, clinical features may mimic type 2 diabetes . However, patients usually require insulin treatment within 5 years. Option A: Patients with latent diabetes become diabetic under stressful conditions. However, upon removal of stress , they become non-diabetic . Option B: MODY or maturity-onset diabetes of the young is a monogenic form of diabetes that occurs < 25 years. There is impaired insulin secretion , but no antibodies . Option C : Brittle diabetes is seen in children with type 1 DM. It presents with wide fluctuation in blood sugar levels .177

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Diabetes Mellitus: Complications and their Mana...
mcqs.question: Which of the following types of renal tubular acidosis can develop in individuals with diabetes mellitus ?
mcqs.explanation: Type IV renal tubular acidosis (RTA) may occur in individuals with diabetes mellitus types 1 and 2. Type IV RTA occurs due to hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism . Low plasma renin activity is common in diabetic patients due to: • Impaired conversion of prorenin to renin • Volume expansion in diabetic nephropathy suppresses renin release These individuals have a tendency to develop hyperkalemia and acidemia, which can be exacerbated by the use of ACEI and ARBs . Hence , these drugs should be avoided.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Genetic mutations causing pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) deficiency presents with all of the following except:
mcqs.explanation: Cachexia is not a feature of mutations of the pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) gene . It is associated with the following characteristics: • Absence of \030-MSH • Severe obesity - \030-MSH inhibits appetite in the hypothalamus • Pale skin and red hair • Absence of ACTH • Secondary adrenal insufficiency

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is recommended as first-line therapy in a patient with chronic hepatitis B?
mcqs.explanation: 287 First-line drugs used for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B include entecavir and tenofovir. Second -line drugs for this condition include : • Lamivudine • Adefovir • Telbivudine Pegylated interferon can also be used in its treatment .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Acute Liver Failure and Liver Transplantation
mcqs.question: A patient presented with fever and pain abdomen. He had undergone liver transplantation a month ago and is taking immunosuppressants . On examination, abdominal guarding was present and on auscultation , no bowel sounds were heard. Doppler showed hepatic artery thrombosis. Which of the following medications is he most likely on?
mcqs.explanation: 312 The given clinical scenario is suggestive of peritonitis due to hepatic artery thrombosis. Sirolimus is known to cause hepatic artery thrombosis in liver transplant recipients . Sirolimus is an mTOR inhibitor and prevents T cell activation. It is not used commonly in liver transplant recipients because of the increased frequency of hepatic artery thrombosis in the first month posttransplantation . However, they can be used in patients with calcineurin inhibitor-related nephrotoxicity .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following antibiotics could be used in the treatment of patients with hepatic encephalopathy ?
mcqs.explanation: Rifaximin can be used in the treatment of hepatic encephalopathy . It lowers blood ammonia levels .346 Treatment of hepatic encephalopathy includes : • Correction of precipitating factors • Lactulose - decreased GI transit time due to cathartic actions leading to increased elimination of ammonia • Rifaximin - lowers the blood ammonia levels • L-ornithine L-aspartate - stimulate the urea cycle , with resulting loss of ammonia

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common viral cause of diarrhea in adults ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common viral cause of diarrhoea in adults (and overall) is norovirus (Norwalk virus). In children, the most common cause is rotavirus .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient with inflammatory bowel disease presents with ocular pain, photophobia , and blurred vision. Which among the following is the most likely cause ?
mcqs.explanation: Uveitis is the most common cause of the given symptoms in a patient with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Uveitis is an ophthalmic manifestation of IBD . It is associated with both ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease . It can develop during remission and is seen even after bowel resection . Prompt intervention with glucocorticoids is required to prevent scarring and visual impairment. The other common ophthalmic manifestations in IBD are conjunctivitis and episcleritis . Episcleritis , more common in Crohn's, is a benign disorder presenting with mild ocular burning.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Overexpression of which of the following causes Menetrier 's disease ?
mcqs.explanation: Overexpression of TGF-\030 (transforming growth factor-alpha) causes Menetrier 's disease . This overexpression results in overstimulation of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) pathway and increased proliferation of mucous cells , resulting in mucous cell (foveolar) hyperplasia .443

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: An elderly man presents to the ER with severe headache , blurring of vision, and oliguria. Examination reveals BP of 200 /100mmHg and papilledema . Skin thickening is noted over his hands, with contractures in the wrist and fingers. Investigations reveal serum creatinine of 3mg/dL and peripheral smear shows schistocytes . What is the drug of choice ?
mcqs.explanation: 498 The given clinical scenario is suggestive of scleroderma renal crisis. The drug of choice is ACE inhibitors. Scleroderma renal crisis is a medical emergency characterized by acute onset malignant hypertension and kidney failure, usually in the absence of previous evidence of significant kidney disease . The use of steroids is associated with an increased risk of scleroderma renal crisis. Clinical features of scleroderma renal crisis are: • Accelerated hypertension - headache , vomiting, blurring of vision, hypertensive retinopathy , and hypertensive encephalopathy . • Acute kidney injury - oliguria, mild proteinuria, microscopic hematuria, renal failure. • Pulmonary edema , congestive heart failure. • Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (schistocytes ), thrombocytopenia . In patients with persistent hypertension , the addition of angiotensin II receptor blockers, calcium channel blockers, and direct renin inhibitors should be considered .499

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient presents with painful knee swelling , dysuria, and conjunctivitis. Which of the following infectious agents is least likely to cause this?
mcqs.explanation: 536 The given scenario of arthritis, urethritis, and conjunctivitis is suggestive of reactive arthritis. It is not caused by Neisseria gonorrhea. Disseminated gonococcal infection causes gonococcal arthritis. It comprises localized septic arthritis and arthritis-dermatitis syndrome. Reactive arthritis is usually caused due to LPS (lipopolysaccharide ) component of the gram -negative organisms or cross-reactivity with synovial antigens. The common causative organisms include : • Chlamydia trachomatis (most common) • Salmonella • Shigella • Yersinia • Campylobacter

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of death in patients with rheumatoid arthritis?
mcqs.explanation: The most common cause of death in patients with rheumatoid arthritis is cardiovascular disease .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: All are components of CURB65 except

options.c: Blood urea nitrogen value greater than 7 mmol/L
options.d: Systolic blood pressure less than 100 mm Hg

mcqs.explanation: Among the options , systolic blood pressure less than 100 mm Hg (Option D) is not a component of CURB-65. CURB65 includes blood pressure , systolic \02690 mmHg or diastolic \02660 mmHg. CURB-65 criteria is used to assess the severity of illness in a case community-acquired pneumonia. It includes confusion (C), urea >7 mmol/L (U), respiratory rate \03730/min (R), blood pressure systolic \02690 mmHg or diastolic \02660 mmHg (B) and an age of \03765 years. Pneumonia severity index (PSI) is another index to assess the severity of illness and the risk of mortality in the case of pneumonia. It includes 20 variables and depending on the score, patients are assigned into one of the 5 classes . Class, I, II , III - at low risk of death and can be treated on an outpatient basis Class IV & V require hospitalization

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient with fever, productive cough , night sweats , and clubbing is diagnosed with lung abscess . Which of the following is an unlikely complication of this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Lung carcinoma is unlikely in patients with lung abscesses . Lung carcinoma may cause lung abscess (in 10 -15% of cases ) but lung abscess is not a premalignant condition. Complications of lung abscess : • Empyema • Pneumatocele • Bronchopleural fistula • Bronchiectasis • Metastatic infections like brain abscess • Life-threatening hemoptysis • Massive aspiration of lung abscess contents

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a component of Syndrome Z?
mcqs.explanation: Syndrome Z is defined as a combination of obstructive sleep apnea syndrome with metabolic syndrome. LDL more than 100 mg/dL is not a criterion for the diagnosis of metabolic syndrome. Metabolic syndrome is diagnosed based on The NCEP: ATP III Criteria. Three or more of the following must be present : • Central obesity : waist circumference >102 cm (M), >88 cm (F) • Hypertriglyceridemia : triglyceride level \037150 mg/dL or specific medication • Low HDL cholesterol : <40 mg/dL and <50 mg/dL for men and women, respectively , or specific medication • Hypertension: blood pressure \037130 mmHg systolic or \03785 mmHg diastolic or specific medication • Fasting plasma glucose level \037100 mg/dL or specific medication or previously diagnosed type 2 diabetes684

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: In a patient undergoing hemodialysis , which of the following can be used to monitor the adequacy of dialysis ?
mcqs.explanation: The adequacy of dialysis is determined by the urea reduction ratio. It is defined as the fractional reduction in blood urea nitrogen per hemodialysis session . It is calculated as (Co - C) / Co, where : Co - predialysis serum urea C - postdialysis serum urea The target urea reduction ratio is 65–70%.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 6-month-old infant is being evaluated for failure to thrive. Lab investigations are as follows . Hypokalemia is found to improve following alkalinization therapy . What type of renal stones is this infant at a higher risk of developing ?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario is suggestive of type 1 RTA . In this condition, calcium phosphate and oxalate stones are formed in the distal convoluting tubules (DCT ).764 In this condition, there is a defect in H+ secretion by the distal tubules . This leads to: • Normal anion gap metabolic acidosis • Urinary pH > 5.5 • Hypokalemia • Impaired H+ secretion causes K+ wasting • It improves following alkalinization therapy with NaHCO3 Acidemia leads to hypercalcemia and then hypercalciuria. There is also hypocitraturia as acidemia induces increased cell citrate utilization. Normally, citrate in the urine binds to calcium and increases its solubility . In the absence of citrate in the urine, calcium begins to precipitate . This leads to nephrocalcinosis and calcium phosphate and oxalate stones .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: On auscultation of a patient , you hear a murmur between S1 and S2. Which of the following conditions is not likely to be associated with this finding?
mcqs.explanation: A murmur occurring between S1 and S2 is a systolic murmur . Pulmonary regurgitation produces a diastolic murmur. The causes of systolic murmurs are as follows : • Mid-systolic - aortic stenosis , pulmonic stenosis , ASD, HOCM. • Holosystolic /pansystolic - mitral regurgitation , tricuspid regurgitation , VSD. • Late systolic - mitral valve prolapse . The causes of diastolic murmurs are as follows : • Early diastolic - aortic regurgitation , pulmonic regurgitation .798 • Mid/late diastolic - mitral stenosis , tricuspid stenosis , Austin-Flint. The causes of continuous murmurs are as follows : • Patent ductus arteriosus (machinery or Gibson's murmur ). • Venous hum • AV fistula • Ruptured sinus of Valsalva aneurysm

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Accelerated idioventricular rhythm is the most common arrhythmia associated with:
mcqs.explanation: Accelerated idioventricular rhythm is the most common arrhythmia associated with myocardial reperfusion , most commonly in the first 2 days after presentation . Idioventricular rhythm is defined as \037 3 consecutive premature ventricular contractions with a heart rate of <50 bpm. If the heart rate is 60-100 bpm, it is known as accelerated idioventricular rhythm, and if it is more than 100 bpm it is known as ventricular tachycardia. It may be the result of an abnormal focus in the ventricle that generates an impulse faster than the sinus node and therefore assumes control. Other causes of AIVR include : • Buerger disease • Congenital heart disease • Dilated cardiomyopathy • Myocarditis • Drugs: Digoxin toxicity , cocaine toxicity , and various anesthesia agents • Electrolyte abnormality • Postresuscitation Episodes of AIVR have not been found to affect prognosis in acute MI and usually do not require intervention. If AIVR is accompanied by hemodynamic compromise, treatment with atropine or atrial pacing will often suppress the rhythm.875

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Infective Endocarditis and Acute rheumatic fever
mcqs.question: You are asked to collect blood samples for culture from a patient suspected to have infective endocarditis by a typical pathogen . Choose the correct statement for the same.

options.a: 3 separate culture sets - two aerobic and one anaerobic
options.b: 3 separate culture sets - two anaerobic and one aerobic
options.d: 2 separate culture sets - one aerobic and one anaerobic

mcqs.explanation: Option D. According to the Modified Duke 2023 Criteria for infective endocarditis , when a typical organism is suspected , two separate culture sets are required, one aerobic and one anaerobic. If an atypical organism is suspected , three or more separate culture sets are used . According to the new Duke's criteria, there is no specific timing to draw blood for blood culture .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old female patient who is a known case of hypertension , diabetes , and hyperlipidemia presents to the emergency department with a severe headache and vomiting. The patient is agitated and her blood pressure is 220 /120 mmHg. Ophthalmoscopy reveals the presence of papilledema . Which of the following antihypertensive is least useful in the management of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The above scenario points towards the diagnosis of malignant hypertension . The drug which is least useful in the management is furosemide (diuretic ). Volume depletion is common in patients with malignant hypertension , and the administration of a diuretic together with a hypertensive agent can lead to an extreme drop in blood pressure . Diuretics are generally not recommended for the rapid reduction of blood pressure in patients with hypertensive crises. They are used only in conditions of volume overload such as acute pulmonary edema .

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Ischemic Heart Disease - Complications and Mana...
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man post -MI had the following lab values. Which of the following must be his treatment plan?
mcqs.explanation: In this 60 yr old patient with post -myocardial infarction (Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease patient), high-intensity statins should be given irrespective of cholesterol levels . So atorvastatin 80mg is the treatment plan in the given case scenario. Examples of high-intensity statins include high-dose atorvastatin 40–80 mg/day and rosuvastatin 20–40 mg/day. Note : Fenofibrate is not advocated unless TG is more than 500 mg/dl. It can be administered along with a moderate -intensity statin.969

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs used in heart failure is an inhibitor of I(f) current in the sinoatrial node ?
mcqs.explanation: Ivabradine is an inhibitor of If current in the sinoatrial node. It reduces the heart rate without decreasing the force of contraction. It is used in patients with chronic HFrEF with a sinus rhythm and a resting heart rate \03770 bpm who are either on a maximum tolerated beta -blocker dose or have a contraindication for beta -blockers. The concurrent treatment should include ACE inhibitor ( or ARB ) and aldosterone receptor antagonist. Option A: Omapatrilat is a dual neprilysin inhibitor+ ACE inhibitor. Option C: Nesiritide belongs to the intravenous vasodilators class and is a recombinant human brain natriuretic peptide (BNP). Option D: Levosimendan belongs to the positive inotropes class and is a combined calcium sensitizer and PDE3 inhibitor.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.chapter: Diseases of Aorta and Peripheral Arteries
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman complains of bluish discoloration of her fingertips on exposure to cold. Which of the following drugs should be avoided in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Raynaud's phenomenon . Clonidine is avoided in Raynaud's phenomenon as it worsens the condition. Clonidine acts on central alpha-2 adrenoreceptor in CNS and reduces sympathetic outflow . This causes decreased blood pressure and perfusion that can exacerbate Raynaud's phenomenon or any PVD . Drugs that can be used for the treatment of Raynaud's phenomenon : Primary Raynaud's: • Dihydropyridine CCBs- nifedipine , isradipine, felodipine , and amlodipine • Diltiazem • Prazosin , doxazosin, and terazosin Secondary Raynaud's: • Phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitors- sildenafil and tadalafil Digital sympathectomy is helpful in some patients who are unresponsive to medical therapy .1035

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old patient is undergoing EEG with his eyes open . What is the expected frequency of the waves being recorded ?
mcqs.explanation: Beta waves are seen on the EEG of an adult recorded with eyes open . The frequency of these waves on an EEG is >13 Hz.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Infarction of area of distribution of which of the following arteries is most likely to be seen in a patient with hemiplegia ?
mcqs.explanation: Hemiplegia is most commonly associated with infarction of the area of distribution of middle cerebral artery. Middle cerebral artery supplies the motor cortex responsible for sending the output to the motor neurons. Infarction in this territory leads to hemiplegia . Infarction of area of distribution of vertebral, anterior spinal and posterior cerebral arteries can also lead to hemiplegia .1101

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: Disorders of autonomic function should be considered in patients with:
mcqs.explanation: Disorders of autonomic function (dysautonomia) is usually considered in patients with: • Unexplained orthostatic hypotension (OH) • Syncope • Sleep dysfunction • Altered sweating (hyperhidrosis or hypohidrosis ) • Impotence • Constipation or other GI symptoms like bloating, nausea, vomiting of old food, diarrhea. • Bladder disorders such as urinary frequency , hesitancy , or incontinence.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: A patient has a spinal cord lesion at the level of L2 – L4 spinal nerve roots. All of the following may be seen in this patient , except :

options.a: Paralysis of hip flexion and adduction

mcqs.explanation: Lesions at L2 – L4 spinal nerve roots do not cause paralysis of the knee flexors. The paralysis of the flexion at the knee occurs due to the lesion at L5 – S1.

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: What is the most common positive visual aura seen by patients during an attack of migraine?
mcqs.explanation: The most common positive visual aura seen in attacks of migraine is a zig-zag line in front of the eyes . The most common negative visual aura is scotoma. The classic migraine is associated with an aura. The aura can be: • Visual (most common): • Zigzag lines • Tunnel vision • Scotoma • Transient visual loss • Sensory: • Tingling sensation of hands, which spreads proximally

mcqs.subject: Medicine
mcqs.question: During rounds, you see that a patient diagnosed with stroke exhibits wild , flinging movements on his right side . Where is the lesion likely to be?
mcqs.explanation: Unilateral wild , flinging movements are called hemiballismus and is seen due to a lesion in the subthalamic nucleus . The most common cause of hemiballismus is stroke.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Identify the condenser in the following image.
mcqs.explanation: This is a modern compound microscope , and the condenser is located below the stage .The purpose of the condenser lens is to focus the light from the illuminator onto the specimen . Microscopes with a stage condenser lens render a sharper image than those with no condenser lens. The simple microscope was invented first by Antonie van Leeuwenhoek , the father of microscopy and microbiology. It uses 1 lens for magnification. The compound microscope , introduced by Hans and Zacharias Janssen uses 2 lenses , an objective lens and an eyepiece , to provide better magnification power than the simple microscope .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old sex worker presented with a painless ulcer on her vulva . On examination, inguinal lymphadenopathy is present . Which of the following methods has been used to demonstrate the causative agent as per the given image?
mcqs.explanation: 15 A painless genital ulcer with inguinal lymphadenopathy with the presence of spiral organisms on microscopy is suggestive of syphilis . It is caused by Treponema pallidum , demonstrated by dark -field microscopy. Dark -field microscopy images have a dark background with a refractile organism. The dark ground microscope has an optical system that enhances the contrast of unstained bodies . It uses reflected light and has a higher resolving power than the light microscope . Dark -field microscopy is the the most specific and sensitive technique to visualize Treponema pallidum when an active chancre or condyloma lata is present . Other options : Option B: Phase contrast microscopy improves the contrast to delineate structures within cells . A dark image is formed on a light background. Option C: Fluorescent microscopy uses fluorescent dyes like auramine-rhodamine to appreciate Mycobacterial species and malarial parasites . Option D: The electron microscope , invented by Ernst Ruska, helps in appreciating viral structures . It has a very high resolving power .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: In which of the following phases of the bacterial growth curve does sporulation occur?
mcqs.explanation: Sporulation occurs in the stationary phase of the bacterial growth curve, which is marked as C in the image. The bacterial growth curve is obtained when a batch of bacteria is seeded in a liquid medium and incubated . It consists of 4 distinct phases : • Lag phase (A) - The bacteria adapt to a new environment. They synthesize and accumulate enzymes and metabolic intermediates required for multiplication . Thus, there is no increase in cell number but cell size increases. Maximum cell size is obtained towards the end of this phase . • Log or exponential phase (B) - The bacteria start dividing and their numbers increase exponentially with time. Cells are smaller and stain uniformly. The growth rate is constant. • Stationary phase (C) - There is depletion of nutrients and accumulation of toxic products . Thus, cell division reduces and a state of equilibrium is attained , where the number of new cells formed equals the number that die . Growth rate is zero. Sporulation occurs during this phase . Many bacteria produce secondary metabolic products such as exotoxins and antibiotics. • Death phase or the phase of decline (D) - Growth rate is negative . The population decreases due to cell death from nutritional exhaustion, toxin accumulation and the action of autolytic enzymes . Involution forms are common.17

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which organism has the following cell wall structure ?
mcqs.explanation: The presence of teichoic acid and lipoteichoic acid with a thick peptidoglycan layer is a feature of gram -positive bacteria. The cell wall of bacteria provides shape and ridigity to the bacterial cell . It is composed of peptidoglycans .Gram positi ve Gram negat ive Teichoic acid, lipoteichoic aci d Present Absent Thickness (Peptidoglycan ) Thicker Thinner Variety of amino acids Few Several Aromatic and sulfur-containi ng amino acids Absent Present Lipopolysaccharides and oute r membrane Absent Present18 Other options : Option C: The cell wall of fungi consists of chitin, mannan , and polysaccharides (glucan). Option D: The cell wall of mycobacteria have mycolic acid, which is responsible for acid fastness .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following methods is used in the test shown below ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows antibiotic sensitivity testing which uses the lawn culture method . Lawn or carpet culture is the method in which a uniform surface growth of bacterium is present on the medium. It is used for antibiotic sensitivity testing (disc method ) and bacteriophage typing . Stab culture (option D) is used for demonstration of gelatin liquefaction and oxygen requirements of bacterium, for maintenance of stock cultures . Streak culture (option A) is routinely used for the isolation of bacteria in pure culture from clinical specimens . Stroke culture (option C) is used for providing pure growth of bacterium for slide agglutination and other diagnostic tests . Other methods of culture include : • Liquid culture - These are preferred for inocula containing antibiotics and other inhibitory substances . • Pour plate culture - It gives an estimate of viable bacterial count in a suspension .21

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: In which of the following organisms will the following phenomenon not be observed in?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows Quellung reaction (halo around the bacteria) and is seen in capsulated bacteria. Neisseria gonorrhoeae is not capsulated , therefore Quellung reaction will not be observed in it. In Quellung reaction, a suspension of a capsulated bacterium is mixed with its specific anticapsular serum and examined under the microscope . The anticapsular antibodies bind to the capsule and thus the capsule becomes very prominent and appears swollen . Capsulated organisms can be remembered with the following mnemonic: Some - Streptococcus pneumoniae Killers - Klebsiella pneumoniae Have - Haemophilus influenzae Nice - Neisseria meningitidis Capsules - Cryptococcus neoformans

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 32 -year-old laborer working at a construction site presented with fever and hemoptysis . The sputum sample collected for examination showed the following . The smear will be stained by which of the following sequences ?

options.b: Methylene blue - malachite green - acetic acid-water

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical vignette of fever and hemoptysis in a labourer with the sputum smear showing acid-fast bacilli is suggestive of tuberculosis . Mycobacterium tuberculosis , detected on sputum smear, is appreciated by Ziehl-Neelsen staining, which would includes carbol fuschin - acid - alcohol - methylene blue . Acid-fast bacteria (like MTB) in a stained Ziehl-Neelsen (ZN) smear appear bright red against a blue background. Steps involved in ZN staining are: • Place the sample on slide evenly spread it with rotational movement • Air-dry the slide and fix it by passing it over a flame • Apply carbol fuschin stain and heat to fix it. • Wash with water to remove excess stain • Decolourise with alcohol • Apply Methylene blue /Malachite green stain • Wash with water to remove excess stain • View under the microscope Kinyoun modified the classical ZN staining such that heat fixing is not required. It is called the cold method . It involves increasing the concentration of phenol acid and the duration of staining. The slide is then washed with water and decolourized with acid alcohol. Counterstaining with Loeffler 's methylene blue or malachite green is done for a minute and viewed under a microscope . Acid-fast bacteria in a stained smear appear bright red against a blue background. The image attached below summarizes the steps .22 Option A: It depicts the order of Gram staining, which was discovered by Hans Christian Gram in 1884. • Primary staining with para-rosaniline dye (crystal violet, methyl violet or gentian violet). • Application of dilute solution of iodine. • Decolorisation with an organic solvent (ethanol , acetone , aniline). • Counterstaining with the dye of contrasting colour (carbol fuchsin, safranine, neutral red). Option B: It includes the steps for performing Albert's stain which is used for detected Corynebacterium diphtheriae . • A heavy smear of the bacterial isolate is prepared on a glass slide and allowed to dry without fixing. • Albert's stain is applied for (3-4) minutes . Then it is washed with water and Albert's iodine is applied for one minute. • Wash with water and let dry with blotting paper . • Examine the slide under oil immersion. Corynebacterium diphtheriae are slender bacilli with an arrangement resembling the letters V or L. They have metachromatic granules at the poles of bacilli which are also called polar bodies , volutin, or Babes-Ernst granules. Albert staining is useful in the demonstration of metachromatic granules. The presence of metachromatic granules helps to distinguish C.diphtheriae from diphtheroids which lack them. The images below show Corynebacterium diphtheriae .23

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The given image shows a culture medium with lactose fermenting and non-lactose fermenting bacteria. Which of the following is not a component of the culture medium?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows MacConkey agar. Cysteine is not a constituent of MacConkey agar. MacConkey agar is a differential or indicator medium. Lactose-fermenting organisms (Eg: E. coli) produce a pink color, and non-lactose fermenting organisms (Shigella sp., Salmonella sp.) do not change the color. Contents of MacConkey agar include peptone , lactose , agar, neutral red and24 sodium taurocholate (Mnemonic- PLANT ). MacConkey agar is also a selective medium i.e. the bile salts (sodium taurocholate ) and dyes (neutral red) inhibit the growth of Gram-positive organisms and Gram-negative cocci.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an enrichment medium?
mcqs.explanation: The image 'A' represents alkaline peptone water, which is an enrichment medium used for Vibrio cholerae . The other images represent : Image B- Blood agar with P. aeruginosa colonies Image C- Loeffler 's serum slope , which is used to isolate C. diphtheriae Image D- Chocolate agar with F. tularensis colonies Enrichment media suppress the growth of commensal bacteria and allow for the growth of certain organisms. These media are used for samples with mixed flora e.g. stool . They are always liquid media, like alkaline peptone water. Other examples include tetrathionate broth and selenite -F broth for Salmonella sp. and Shigella sp. Enriched medium are those media to which additional nutrients such as blood, serum, or egg are added . They're used to grow bacteria with specific nutritional requirements. Examples include blood agar to test the hemolytic property of bacteria, chocolate agar for isolation of H. influenzae and Loeffler 's serum slope for isolation of C. diphtheriae .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A microbiologist observes the following growth on a blood agar plate . Which of the following will not be the etiological agent ?
mcqs.explanation: The above image shows a swarming type of growth on the agar plate . It will not be caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae . Swarming is the growth of motile bacteria in the form of a thin film on solid culture media. It is exhibited by the following : • Gram-positive bacilli - Clostridium tetani (option A), Bacillus cereus (option D) • Gram-negative bacilli - Proteus mirabilis (option C), Proteus vulgaris • Gram-negative halophilic bacteria- Vibrio parahaemolyticus Swarming can be inhibited by increasing the concentration of agar (6%), alcohol, sodium azide, boric acid, chloral hydrate , sulfonamide, and surface -active agents .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: An orthopedician is performing the following procedure to visualize the anterior cruciate ligament in a patient . Which of the following will be used to sterilise the instrument used ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows arthroscopy being performed . Arthroscopes are sterilized using plasma sterilization which utilises hydrogen peroxide . In plasma sterilisation , radiofrequency energy is applied to create an electromagnetic field through which hydrogen peroxide vapours are passed . This generates plasma which contains free radicals of hydrogen and oxygen . Plasma denatures all organisms and is used sterilize arthroscopes and ureteroscopes . Sterilization control is monitored by Geobacillus stearothermophilus and Bacillus atrophaeus . Option A: Ethylene oxide has both microbicidal and sporicidal activity. It is used for sterilisation heat -sensitive equipment like heart-lung machines, respirators, suture materials etc . Sterilization control is monitored by Bacillius atrophaeus and Bacillus subtilus . Option B: Gamma rays cause breakage of DNA. It destroys spores and vegetative cells , but is not effective against viruses. It is referred to as cold sterilisation and is used in commercial plants to sterilize plastics , syringes , swabs. Sterilization control is monitored by Bacillus pumilius . Option D: Ultraviolet rays are used to sterilise biosafety cabinets , entryways , operation theatres and laboratories.29

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 23 -year-old presents with diarrhea, fever, and vomiting. The given bacteria is implicated . Which toll-like receptor binds to the structure of the bacteria marked A?
mcqs.explanation: The given image and clinical history suggest a typhoid infection . The structure marked A is the flagella of bacteria. Toll-like receptor (TLR ) 5 binds to the flagella of bacteria. Toll-like receptors (TLRs ) are transmembrane receptors that have an extracellular domain, that detect infecting pathogens . • TLR 1 - Mycobacteria and Gram-negative bacteria • TLR 2 - Mycobacteria and Gram-positive bacteria • TLR 3 - Viral RNA • TLR 4 - Gram-negative bacteria • TLR 5 - Flagella • TLR 9 - Bacterial DNA, some herpes viruses, malarial parasite TLRs act through the NF-KB pathway and initiate inflammation.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old woman presents with a fever of 103 \260F, hypotension , confusion, and a diffuse rash as shown below . 3 days back, she had uncontrollable epistaxis for which a nasal pack was placed . What is the likely mechanism of action of the microbial toxin that has caused her current illness ?
mcqs.explanation: This woman presented with fever, hypotension , and a diffuse erythematous rash, three days after a nasal packing was done. This is characteristic of toxic shock syndrome - commonly caused by staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome toxin-1 (TSST -1), which is a superantigen . Superantigens act by causing polyclonal activation of T cells . They activate a large number of T cells irrespective of their antigen specificity . In contrast to regular antigens which bind to the binding groove on T cells , superantigens bind outside the groove directly to the lateral aspect of the TCR \037 chain. This leads to a massive release of cytokines and polyclonal activation of T cells . Clinically, this manifests as fever, hypotension, and skin exfoliation .Examples of organisms that produce superantigens : • Bacterial43 • Staphylococcus aureus- Enterotoxins • Group A streptococci - Pyrogenic exotoxin • Mycoplasma arthritidis- mitogen 1 • Yersinia enterocolitica • Yersinia pseudotuberculosis • Viral • Epstein –Barr virus (EBV) • Cytomegalovirus (CMV) • Rabies nucleocapsid • HIV -encoded negative regulatory factor. • Fungal- Malassezia furfur

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Identify the class of immunoglobulin\037 shown in the image below .
mcqs.explanation: The above image shows a dimeric structure , characteristic of secretory IgA. IgA immunoglobulin is the major antibody responsible for mucosal immunity. Its serum levels are usually low. It is predominantly present in the extravascular secretions . It is present in secretions such as milk, saliva, and tears, and in secretions of the respiratory, intestinal , and genital tracts. When present in the serum, it exists as a monomer similar to IgG. However, when it is secreted , it exists as a dimer. The dimeric structure consists of two monomers, which are stabilized by two additional polypeptides : • J chain, which stabilizes the molecule . • Secretory component , which is incorporated into the IgA when transported through the epithelial cell .45

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which immunoglobulin is majorly responsible for the reaction demonstrated below ?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows blood typing , which works on the principle of agglutination . IgM is mainly responsible for agglutination . It is the most efficient immunoglobulin in agglutination , complement fixation, and other antigen –antibody reactions and is important also in defense against bacteria and viruses. It is a pentamer , and hence is more effective than IgG in opsonization (C3b mediated ), bactericidal action and bacterial agglutination but less effective in neutralization of toxins and viruses.Reaction IgG IgM Precipitation Stron g Wea k Agglutination Weak Stro ng Complement fixati on Mode rate Stro ng Lysis Weak Stro ng

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which among the following statements is false ?

options.a: Muramic acid is present in prokaryotes
options.b: Mitotic division is present in eukaryotes
options.d: Multiple linear chromosomes present in eukaryotes

mcqs.explanation: 80S ribosome is present in eukaryotes, while 70S ribosome is present in prokaryotes. 80S ribosome has subunits 60S and 40S, while 70S has subunits 50S and 30S.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: What are jumping genes known as?
mcqs.explanation: Jumping genes are also called transposons. Transposons are genetic elements that can move between chromosomal and extra-chromosomal DNA molecules. Insertion of a transposon leads to acquisition of new characteristics by the recipient DNA. Transposons contain several genes , including those necessary for their migration from one genetic locus to another. They may contain genes for specialised functions like antibiotic resistance . However, they do not contain genes for their replication. Jumping genes were discovered by Barbara McClintock and she was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1983 for the same. Other options: Options A and B: The cytoplasmic carriers of genetic information are termed plasmids or episomes . Option D: A cosmid is a type of hybrid plasmid that contains a Lambda phage cos sequence . (Cos sites + plasmid = cosmids).

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 3-year-old child presents with a history of repeated sinopulmonary infections caused by encapsulated organisms. Which of the following is most likely to be deficient in this case?
mcqs.explanation: Deficiency of IgG2 results in recurrent sinopulmonary infections with encapsulated organisms. IgG is the only maternal immunoglobulin that is normally transported across the placenta and provides natural passive immunity to the newborn. IgG1 is the antibody maximally transported across the placenta , whereas IgG2 has the least transplacental movement. Deficiencies of other IgG: • IgG1- bacterial infections (diphtheria, tetanus )(Option A) • IgG3- viral infections (Option C) • IgG4- parasitic infections (Option D)

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.chapter: Structure and Functions of the Immune System & ...
mcqs.question: A mother brings her 1-year-old child to the hospital with complaints that he turns blue while breastfeeding . It resolves when he assumes a squatting position. On examination, a cleft palate is seen . Labs show hypocalcemia . Which of the following abnormalities is expected to be seen in the lymphoid organs?

options.a: Decreased size of germinal centres of lymph nodes
options.b: Decreased size of paracortical areas of lymph nodes
options.d: Increased size of the peri arteriolar lymphoid sheath of spleen

mcqs.explanation: Turning blue on breastfeeding with resolution on squatting describes a tet -spell or a cyanotic spell , indicating a congenital cardiac defect . Cleft palate , cardiac defects and hypocalcemia (parathyroid hypoplasia /aplasia) suggest a diagnosis of DiGeorge syndrome. In this disorder, a decreased size of paracortical areas of lymph nodes is noted . DiGeorge syndrome is characterised by thymic aplasia, causing a deficiency of T cells and absent cell -mediated immunity. Thus, paracortical areas of lymph nodes and periarteriolar sheaths of the spleen , where T cells reside , are reduced in size. B cells are usually not affected .62

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.chapter: Structure and Functions of the Immune System & ...
mcqs.question: Which of the following markers is used for the identification of memory T cells ?
mcqs.explanation: CD45RO is used as a marker for the identification of memory T cells . CD45RA is a marker for virgin or nai\037ve T helper cells .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A child, upon ingestion of shellfish , developed a tingling sensation in the mouth, swelling of the face , lips, and tongue , and also complained of abdominal pain and dizziness. What type of reaction is this?
mcqs.explanation: This child who developed tingling in the mouth, and swelling of the lips and face after eating shelf life is an example of an IgE mediated type of hypersensitivity reaction.76 Anaphylaxis is a severe , potentially life -threatening allergic reaction that occurs rapidly and affects the whole body. It is characterized by a sudden release of histamines and other chemicals from the immune system in response to an allergen , such as certain foods , medications , insect stings, or latex. The onset of symptoms can occur within minutes to a few hours after exposure to the allergen .The primary mediators are histamine and serotonin. The secondary mediators are prostaglandins and leukotrienes . Clinically, anaphylaxis can present with a combination of symptoms that typically include : • Respiratory Symptoms : Patients often experience wheezing and respiratory distress due to bronchoconstriction. Other signs may include shortness of breath, coughing , and a feeling of tightness in the chest . • Skin Symptoms : Urticaria (hives) and angioedema (swelling of the skin and mucous membranes) are common. These skin reactions usually develop rapidly, often within minutes to two hours of exposure to the allergen . • Cardiovascular Symptoms : Hypotension (low blood pressure ) is a key indicator of anaphylaxis. Patients may also experience tachycardia (increased heart rate) and, in severe cases , shock. • Gastrointestinal Symptoms : Abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhea, and cramps can occur, particularly if the anaphylaxis is triggered by food allergens . • Neurological Symptoms : Dizziness, lightheadedness , or loss of consciousness can occur due to the sudden drop in blood pressure and reduced oxygen supply to the brain .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: An immunologist orders a nitroblue tetrazolium test on a child suspected to have a primary immunodeficiency disease . What condition is she screening the child for?
mcqs.explanation: The Nitroblue Tetrazolium Test (NBT) is used as a screening test for chronic granulomatous disease (CGD) by assessing the reactive oxygen species (ROS) production in phagocytes . This principle relies on the color change of nitroblue tetrazolium, which transforms from colorless /yellow to deep blue when it encounters ROS. A higher nitroblue test score indicates that the cell is more efficient in producing ROS. In chronic granulomatous disease , there is an NADPH oxidase defect . Hence , the phagocyte cannot produce reactive oxygen species or radicals required for bacterial killing, which results in recurrent infections . Here, the leukocytes fail to reduce nitroblue tetrazolium during phagocytosis . Hence , a negative test (NBT remains colourless to yellow ) is seen in CGD. A positive test result means neutroph ils turn blue , as shown below :88 A negative test means nitroblue tetrazolium remains colourless /yellow , as shown below :

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A college student with a history of intravenous drug abuse presents with a fever for the last 3 weeks . Echocardiography is performed which reveals large friable vegetations on the cusps of the tricuspid valve. Which of the following organisms is the most common cause for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Fever with vegetations on the tricuspid valve points to a diagnosis of right-sided infective endocarditis. Staphylococcus aureus is the most common cause of right-sided infective endocarditis among intravenous drug abusers. Infective endocarditis is the microbial infection of heart valves or endocardium, leading to the formation of vegetations (thrombotic debris and microbial organisms).The following image shows a graphical illustration of vegetations seen in infective endocarditis .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following bacteria gain toxigenicity by lysogenic conversion?
mcqs.explanation: 139 Lysogenic or phage conversion is seen in Corynebacterium diphtheriae . The toxigenicity of diphtheria bacillus depends on the presence of the corynephages (tox+). When the bacillus is cured of the phage , its toxigenic capacity is lost. A bacteriophage is a virus that parasitises bacteria. It can carry host DNA and transfer it to another bacterium. In lysogenic conversion, the viral DNA is integrated with the bacterial DNA and thus can code for new characteristics, like toxin production . The conversion of non-toxigenic bacterial strains to toxigenic by infecting them with bacteriophages is known as lysogenic conversion.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The most common clinical form of actinomycosis is
mcqs.explanation: The most common clinical form of actinomycosis is cervicofacial. Actinomycosis is a chronic granulomatous infection characterized by indurated swellings , mainly in the connective tissue , suppuration , and discharge of sulphur granules. The most common causative agent is Actinomycetes israelli. Various clinical forms of actinomycosis involves cervicofacial, thoracic, abdominal, and pelvic actinomycosis . Among them, actinomycosis most frequently occurs as oral-cervicofacial form presenting as a soft tissue swelling , abscess , or mass lesion involving the angle of jaw.146

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A middle -aged man came with a history of fever and night sweats for the past 2 weeks . He has had noticeable weight loss. Bronchoalveolar lavage was done, but Mycobacterium tuberculosis was not detected . Extra-pulmonary TB is suspected . Which site is most likely affected ?
mcqs.explanation: Lymph nodes are the most common site of extrapulmonary TB . The diagnosis is established by fine needle aspiration biopsy . In descending order of frequency, the extrapulmonary sites most commonly involved in TB are: • lymph nodes • pleura • genitourinary tract176 • bones and joints • meninges , peritoneum and pericardium. In less than 50% of these cases , there is associated pulmonary disease .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A leprosy vaccine is being introduced on a pilot basis in India. Which of the following mycobacterial species is the basis for its development ?
mcqs.explanation: Mycobacterium indicus pranii is the basis for the development of a leprosy vaccine. The leprosy vaccine species was originally called Mycobacterium W (M.w) but was later renamed Mycobacterium indicus pranii. The vaccine is administered via intradermal route. The dose is 0.1 ml. It is divided into two equal doses and given on both arms. Booster doses will be given to maintain the immunity level . These are given only in one arm .189

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: You notice a sputum sample of a patient suspected of having ventilator-associated pneumonia turns progressively redder over time. Microscopic examination of the sample reveals an absence of red blood cells . Which of the following organisms could have caused this?
mcqs.explanation: The given condition of sputum sample turning redder over time can be caused by Serratia marcescens .205 Serratia marcescens are pleomorphic coccobacilli that can grow in sputum after collection and can mimic hemoptysis because they produce a red pigment called prodigiosin. S. macescens mainly cause healthcare -associated infections such as ventilator-associated pneumonia, meningitis, endocarditis , septicemia and peritonitis . They can contaminate IV fluids , surgical instruments, and antiseptic solutions .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: You are administering a Vi capsular polysaccharide vaccine to a child in Germany before his trip to India. Which of the following is false about the antigen used in this vaccine?
mcqs.explanation: Vi capsule polysaccharide antigen is a heat -labile antigen used in the Vi capsular polysaccharide vaccine (ViCPS ) for typhoid . Vi antigen is found in Salmonella typhi , S. paratyphi C and S. dublin. It is a capsular antigen and is a polysaccharide. It acts as a virulence factor by inhibiting phagocytosis and resisting complement activation and bacterial lysis . It envelopes the O antigen, and thus , many S. typhi strains fail to agglutinate with O antiserum. However, it can be destroyed by heat . It is alcohol stable . This antigen is poorly immunogenic. The Vi capsular polysaccharide vaccine (Vi CPS) contains purified Vi polysaccharide . It is given as a single dose of 0.5ml intramuscularly to children over 2 years of age . It is recommended for travellers to areas endemic for Salmonella infections .215

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: An El Tor vibrio was identified to be the causative agent of a diarrhea epidemic . Which of the following is not a characteristic feature of this organism?

options.a: Resistant to El Tor phage V
options.d: Not susceptible to group IV phage

mcqs.explanation: El Tor vibrios are susceptible to El Tor phage V.232

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 20 year old male presents with acute onset cough and thick sticky sputum . There is a history of repeated lung infections since childhood . Chest Xray shows evidence of bilateral upper lobe bronchiectasis . On evaluation, the chloride concentration in his sweat is >60 mEq/L. What is the organism majorly associated with this patient 's respiratory disease ?
mcqs.explanation: Bilateral upper lobe bronchiectasis with a history of repeated lung infections since childhood and evelated sweat chloride concentration suggests a diagnosis of cystic fibrosis (CF). Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a common etiological agent associated with chronic airway infection in patients with cystic fibrosis (CF).242 In cystic fibrosis, there is thick inspissated mucus and impaired mucociliary clearance. Due to these factors, lungs are often colonized in infancy and early childhood with Staphylococcus aureus and Haemophilus influenzae . In adulthood , they are replaced by P. aeruginosa. This results in chronic inflammation, which leads to airway modelling and bronchiectasis . Note : Burkholderia cepacia complex is an opportunistic environmental pathogen . It causes fatal respiratory distress and septicemia in CF patients . This is termed as 'cepacia syndrome'.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 4-year-old unimmunized child presents with whooping cough . Which of the following constituents of the causative organism is responsible for facilitating its adhesion to the respiratory epithelium ?
mcqs.explanation: Whooping cough is caused by Bordetella pertussis . Filamentous hemagglutinin (FHA) is responsible for facilitating the adhesion of Bordetella pertussis to the respiratory epithelium . Bordetella pertussis produces 3 hemagglutinins : Pertussis toxin (PT ), lipid factor and FHA. FHA is a surface protein and is readily shed . Along with fimbrae, it helps in the adhesion of B. pertussis to the cilia of the respiratory epithelium and to erythrocytes . FHA and PT also promote secondary infection by coating other bacteria such as Haemophilus influenzae and Pneumococci. They then assists their binding to respiratory epithelium. This phenomenon has been termed 'piracy of adhesins '.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: The following are true about chancroid:
mcqs.explanation: Chancroid is a painful genital ulcer caused by Haemophilus ducreyi , which is a gram-negative coccobacillus . Microscopic appearance of H. ducreyi is called the school of fish appearance or railroad appearance. Chancroid ulcers have a soft base that bleeds easily to touch . They also cause painful lymphadenopathy . The image below shows the 'school-of-fish' appearance characteristic of H. ducreyi .259 Note : Groove sign is a characteristic sign seen in lymphogranuloma venereum. It refers to the depression created by the inguinal ligament as it passes between the groups of inflamed inguinal lymph nodes .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms do not cause yersiniosis?
mcqs.explanation: The term yersiniosis denotes infections with yersiniae other than Y.pestis . Yersiniosis includes zoonotic infections by Y.pseudotuberculosis and Y.enterocolitica .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 5-year-old girl with thalassemia major was prophylactically immunized with a polysaccharide meningococcal vaccine before being taken up for elective splenectomy . Which group of Neisseria meningitidis would she be susceptible to even after immunization ?
mcqs.explanation: Polysaccharide vaccines of Neisseria meningitidis do not offer protection against group B meningococci . This is because the group B capsule is made up of sialic acid residue which is also expressed on the surface of neural cells in the fetus . So, the B polysaccharide is perceived as 'self ' and is poorly immunogenic. To overcome this issue and provide protection against group B meningococci, a new vaccine was developed based on the surface protein i.e., non-capsular antigen of serogroup B meningococci. This is the multicomponent meningococcal vaccine - 4CMenB. Meningococcal polysaccharide vaccines developed based on capsular antigen can be classified as: • Plain polysaccharide vaccines: • Bivalent (A and C), • Trivalent (A, C and W-135) • Tetravalent (A, C, Y, and W-135) • Conjugated polysaccharide vaccines: • Monovalent (A or C) • Quadrivalent (A, C, Y, and W-135) MenQuadfi vaccine

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Transovarial transmission is a feature of which of the following diseases ?
mcqs.explanation: Transovarial transmission is a feature of Orientia tsutsugamushi which causes scrub typhus . Transovarial transmission refers to passing on the disease -causing bacteria from parent arthropod to offspring arthropod. Orientia tsutsugamushi is maintained by transovarial transmission in trombiculid mites . It is also seen in Rickettsia rickettsii, Rickettsia conorii, and Rickettsia akari . The image below shows a trombiculid mite.Trench fever (option D) is caused by Bartonella quintana .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Lesion scrapings from a genital ulcer show numerous polymorphs , but no bacteria. Which of the following is the most appropriate culture medium for organisms responsible for the above condition?
mcqs.explanation: Clinical scrapings from a genital ulcer showing polymorphs in the absence of bacteria is suggestive of chlamydial infection and the most appropriate culture medium is McCoy cells (human synovial carcinoma cell line). C. trachomatis is a small gram-negative bacterium and an obligate intracellular parasite that appears as an intracytoplasmic inclusion body. The gram stain of the cervical smear would show leucocytes but no organisms. Hence , selective culture media like the McCoy cells culture is used to isolate the organism. Option B: Thayer–Martin agar is used for isolation of Neisseria spp . Option C: Robertson's cooked meat is used for the culture of anaerobes, especially Clostridia Option D: Pleuropneumonia -like organisms (PPLO ) broth is used to culture Mycoplasma spp . and Ureaplasma spp . Note : Abnormal urethral gram stain showing >10 PMNs/1000 \305~ field in women with dysuria but without coliform bacteriuria supports the diagnosis of chlamydial urethritis.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 55 -year old man was brought to the OPD with complaints of rapid decline in cognition, impaired position, and vibratory sense . There is a history of sporadic short-term relationships with many promiscuous sexual partners. Romberg's sign is positive and bilateral Argyll Robertson pupils are seen on checking for pupillary reflex . Which of the following is the investigation of choice ?
mcqs.explanation: 328 The clinical scenario given above with a positive sexual history, Romberg test , and Argyll Robertson pupils is suggestive of neurosyphilis . The investigation of choice for neurosyphilis is VDRL . The CSF VDRL test is highly specific and, when reactive, is considered diagnostic of neurosyphilis . Involvement of the CNS in syphilis is detected by examination of CSF for: • Mononuclear pleocytosis (>5 white blood cells /�ML). • Increased protein concentration (>45 mg/dL). • CSF VDRL reactivity.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 12 -year-old boy presents with right upper quadrant pain, calf pain, conjunctival suffusion , icterus , and fever. Examination shows tender hepatomegaly . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The most likely diagnosis based on the clinical vignette is leptospirosis . Leptospirosis is a zoonosis caused by spirochetes of the genus Leptospira. Patients with mild disease may present with flu-like symptoms of sudden onset , fever with chills, headache , abdominal pain, conjunctival suffusion , and myalgia. The muscle pain usually affects the calves, abdomen, and back. Mild cases can be treated with oral doxycycline , ampicillin, or amoxicillin.333 Severe leptospirosis is rapidly progressive and is associated with high fatality . The classic presentation of the severe disease called Weil's syndrome includes the triad of hemorrhage, jaundice , and acute kidney injury. Jaundice when present can be profound and physical examination may reveal an enlarged , tender liver. Temperature -pulse dissociation /relative bradycardia can be seen . Moderate to severe cases are treated with intravenous penicillin , ampicillin, or ceftriaxone . The image below shows icterus and conjunctival suffusion in a patient with leptospirosis .Leptospira are actively motile organisms and are best seen using a dark -field microscope . They are thin, tightly coiled , and flexible spirochetes with one end forming a hook. Diagnosis is by microscopic agglutination test . Transmission occurs through cuts or breaks in the skin and mucous membranes (conjunctival and oral mucosa). Several outbreaks have been reported that resulted from exposure to floodwaters contaminated by urine from infected animals. The organism enters the bloodstream and lodges in the parenchymatous organs (liver and kidneys) leading to hemorrhage and necrosis of the tissue334 causing dysfunction of the organs. The lifecycle of Leptospira is shown below .Illness is classically biphasic after an incubation period of up to 1 month. The stages are: • Acute leptospiremic phase - the organism can be cultured from blood. • Resolving immune phase - the organism can be cultured from urine. The stages may not be clinically distinguishable . Other options : Option A - Chikungunya is a viral disease that presents with saddle -back fever, conjunctival suffusion , and photophobia . Migratory arthralgia, especially involving small joints may also be seen . A maculopapular or petechial rash is frequently seen on the trunk. Option C - Dengue hemorrhagic fever is a form of severe dengue with bleeding manifestations . Evidence of plasma leakage and thrombocytopenia is also generally seen . Option D - Encephalitis due to Hepatitis A is seen in fulminant hepatitis , a rare complication. Patients present with confusion, disorientation, ascites , and edema .335

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following viruses shows an enveloped icosahedral symmetry?
mcqs.explanation: Enveloped icosahedral symmetry is seen in the rubella virus.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: While drawing blood from a patient with hepatitis B, it splashes into the eyes of a nurse. Which of the following markers will appear first in her blood if she gets infected ?
mcqs.explanation: HBsAg is the first marker to appear in the blood after infection . It can be detected even before the elevation of serum transaminases and onset of clinical illness . Usually, it disappears within 2 months of onset of clinical disease but may last for even 6 months and beyond . If it persists beyond 6 months, it indicates chronic hepatitis . Anti-HBs is the protective antibody, which appears soon after HBsAg, disappears and remains in serum for a long time.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
