mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man with heroin addiction presents with fatigue , palpable purpura, joint pains, and abdominal pain. Urine analysis shows massive proteinuria. Which of the following viruses should be tested for in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of mixed cryoglobulinemia , which is strongly associated with hepatitis C. Hence , the patient should be tested for hepatitis C.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old bisexual man goes to an ICTC centre for counselling about HIV . Which of the following is false about HIV transmission?

options.a: Male -to-female HIV transmission has more risk of causing infection than female -to-male transmission
options.b: The risk of acquiring HIV with unprotected receptive anal intercourse is lower than that with penile -vaginal intercourse
options.c: The quantity of HIV -1 in plasma is a primary determinant of the risk of HIV -1 transmission
options.d: Male circumcision is associated with a lower risk of HIV acquisition for heterosexual men

mcqs.explanation: The risk of HIV acquisition associated with unprotected receptive anal intercourse is relatively higher than that seen in penile -vaginal intercourse . This is because the rectal mucosal membrane is thin and fragile and anal intercourse is associated with microtrauma (rectal tears). The differences in transmission rates between men and women are because the vagina and cervix are exposed to semen for a longer duration, increasing the risk of transmission. However, the penis and urethral orifice are exposed relatively briefly to infected vaginal fluid , lowering the risk .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 4-year-old girl with a history of fever, rhinorrhea , sore throat, and myalgia presented with multiple episodes of vomiting and seizures . She was diagnosed with Reye 's syndrome. Which of the following is incorrect about the most likely etiological agent ?

options.a: Virus shedding is present before symptoms begins
options.b: 5-12 years is a high risk group

mcqs.explanation: The most likely etiological agent in the given case of Reye 's syndrome is the influenza virus. Children <5-years, especially those <2-years of age are at the highest risk of serious complications related to influenza infection . Other high-risk groups for influenza include adults \02460 years of age , persons with chronic diseases , persons who are immunocompromised. Option A: The virus is shed in respiratory secretions a day before the onset of illness and for 3-4 days thereafter . Option C: Birds, especially aquatic birds act as reservoirs of influenza viruses. Option D: Secondary attack rate is 5-15%.408 Note : Reye 's syndrome is precipitated by the interaction of a viral infection (such as influenza) with salicylates . Therefore, aspirin is not given to pediatric patients with influenza and influenza-like illness .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true about Japanese encephalitis ?

options.d: Vaccinating pigs is helpful in disease control

mcqs.explanation: Humans are the dead -end hosts for the Japanese encephalitis virus.425 Option A: The disease is transmitted by Culex tritaeniorhynchus and Culex vishnui (common in India) species. Option B: Herons act as reservoir hosts and pigs as amplifier hosts . Option D: The control measures include mosquito control, locating piggeries away from the human dwellings and vaccinating pigs. The image below shows the life cycle of the Japanese B encephalitis virus.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which strain of the Ebola virus has the highest case fatality rate?
mcqs.explanation: The Zaire strain has a case fatality rate of 90% There are five identified Ebola virus strains, four of which are known to cause disease in humans: • Ebola virus (Zaire ebolavirus) • Sudan virus (Sudan ebolavirus) • Ta\357 Forest virus (Ta\357 Forest ebolavirus) • Bundibugyo virus (Bundibugyo ebolavirus).439 The fifth , Reston virus (Reston ebolavirus), has caused disease in nonhuman primates, but not in humans. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus, Zaire ebolavirus, and Sudan ebolavirus have been associated with large outbreaks in Africa. The strain that caused the 2014 –2016 West African outbreak belongs to the Zaire ebolavirus species .

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following features do not support a diagnosis of Zika fever?
mcqs.explanation: A petechial rash is not a primary feature of Zika virus infection . Though petechiae may rarely appear in Zika virus disease it is however not included in the CDC case definition of Zika virus disease . Petechial rash points towards a diagnosis of dengue fever while a maculopapular rash suggests a Zika virus disease . Zika virus infection is characterized by influenza-like clinical signs including fever, headache, and malaise. A maculopapular rash, conjunctivitis, myalgia, and arthralgia usually accompany or follow those manifestations .444 The complications of Zika virus are: • Guillain-Barre syndrome • Fetal microcephaly in pregnant women.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a dimorphic fungus ?
mcqs.explanation: Pneumocystis jirovecii is a yeast -like fungus and not a dimorphic fungus . Dimorphic fungi exist in the yeast form in body tissues and cultures maintained at 37\260C, and in the filamentous form in cultures at room temperature (25\260C). Examples of dimorphic fungi include : • Blastomyces dermatitidis • Coccidioides immitis • Paracoccidioides brasiliensis • Talaromyces marneffei • Sporothrix schenckii • Histoplasma capsulatum • Coccidioides posadasii468

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A 46-year-old farmer came to the clinic with cough and chest pain for one week and fatigue for a month. He was diagnosed to have a hydatid cyst in his right lung. Which of the following classes does the causative organism of this disease belong to?
mcqs.explanation: The causative organism of hydatid disease is Echinococcus granulosus and it belongs to the class cestodes . It is a tape -like , segmented worm. It infects man accidentally , giving rise to hydatid cysts .495 The image below shows the classification of parasites .Note : Zoonoses refers to diseases caused by zoonotic organisms. It is not a class of organisms.

mcqs.subject: Microbiology
mcqs.question: A patient presented to the OPD with cough , chest pain, and expectoration of rusty colored sputum . He is diagnosed to have an oriental lung fluke infection . Which of the following parasites is implicated here?
mcqs.explanation: Paragonimus westermani is commonly known as oriental lung fluke or Japanese lung fluke . It causes a pulmonary syndrome characterised by cough , chest pain and hemoptysis . Paragonimus westermani is a trematode . The transmission to humans occurs by eating raw or undercooked crab or crayfish containing metacercariae. The metacercariae excyst in the human gut and young worms migrate to the lungs , where they become encapsulated in lung tissue . The patient complains of cough , chest pain, and hemoptysis . The viscous sputum is speckled with golden -brown eggs . Treatment: Praziquantel (25 mg/ kg TDS for 1-2 days) is the drug of choice . The following image shows the life cycle of Paragonimus westermani , the oriental lung fluke .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient presented to the gynecology OPD with the following finding. Which structure in men is homologous to the affected structure ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a Bartholin's cyst , which involves the Bartholin's glands. These glands are homologous to the male bulbourethral or Cowper glands. The ducts of Bartholin's glands open in the groove between the hymen and the labia minora at approximately 5 and 7 o'clock positions. They are stimulated by sexual arousal. The glands contain columnar cells that secrete mucus with lubricant properties . Contraction of the bulbospongiosus muscle expresses gland secretions . Bartholin's cyst occurs due to obstruction of the ducts of the Bartholin's glands by proteinaceous material, or due to infection . Symptomatic or recurrent cysts may require marsupialization or gland excision. An infected Bartholin's cyst can lead to an Bartholin's abscess . This requires surgical drainage.15

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Identify the type of hymen.
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows cribriform hymen because it has multiple small openings . Based on the shape of its opening , the hymen may be classified as: Other variants of the hymen: The hymen is lined by stratified squamous epithelium on both sides . The hymen is most commonly torn posterolaterally or posteriorly. It is replaced by tags after childbirth which are called as carunculae myrtiformes.17 Hymen Description Annular Oval central opening Crescen tic Semilunar central opening Vertical Vertical slit-like opening Septate 2 lateral openings partitioned by a bridge of hymenal tissu e Cribrifo rm Multiple small openingsVariants Description Absence of hymen Congenital deformity . Infantile Small central linear opening . Imperforate No opening Fimbriated Free margin has symmetrical indentations anteriorly Ring or fringe-like A narrow ring of thick memb rane is present all around the vaginal orificeIt can easily di stend during sexual intercour se without rupturing the hym en

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The following figure shows the transverse section of the uterus with an implanted zygote . Identify structure A.
mcqs.explanation: In the given image, the decidua basalis is marked as A. This part of the decidua forms the placenta.Implantation occurs 6 to 7 days after fertilization. After implantation, the endometrium is called the decidua . It is of the following types: • Decidua basalis - present over chorion frondosum. Decidua basalis and chorion frondosum form the placenta . • Decidua capsularis - present over abembryonic pole . • Decidua parietalis - present on the opposite side of the uterus . The villi cover the entire surface of the chorion during the early weeks . As the fetus grows, the villi on the embryonic pole continue to grow, giving rise to the chorion frondosum. At the abembryonic pole , the villi degenerate . By the third month, this side of the chorion becomes smooth, and is called the chorion laeve.43 As the fetus grows, the chorion laeve comes into contact with the decidua parietalis on the opposite side of the uterus , and fusion occurs. Thus, the uterine lumen is obliterated . The amnion and chorion fuse , to form the amniochorionic membrane. Rupture of the amniochorionic membrane during labor is called 'breaking of waters '. Note : Superfetation can theoretically occur till the time the uterine lumen is not obliterated .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Identify the structure marked A.
mcqs.explanation: The structure marked A is primary oocyte . Primary oocytes are the germ cells seen in the medullary region of the ovary . These enlarge at the beginning of the growth phase . During this cell growth period , many oocytes undergo degeneration , both before and after birth. A single layer of flattened follicular cells that were derived originally from the germinal epithelium soon surrounds the primary oocytes . The structure that is formed is now called a primordial follicle . These are seen first in the medulla and later in the cortex.45

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A newborn is admitted to the NICU with the following teratoma. Which embryonic layers is this derived from?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows an oropharygeal teratoma, which contains derivatives from all three germ layers. The tumor may include gut , bone, skin, and teeth . These tumors arise from pluripotent stem cells that differentiate into any of three germ layers forming tissues of all three germ layers.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Identify the structure marked as A.
mcqs.explanation: The structure marked A is the allantois. The posterior wall of the yolk sac forms the allantois on the 16th day of development . Its distal portion forms the urachus which forms the median umbilical ligament . The given image shows an embryo at the end of the third week .46

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A primigravida delivered a baby at term with a birth weight of 1.9 kg via normal vaginal delivery. The placenta delivered appears as shown in the image below . What is this condition known as?
mcqs.explanation: 78 The given image shows a circumvallate placenta . The membranes at the periphery are thickened and consist of a double fold of chorion and amnion . Normally, the chorionic plate and basal plates are of the same size. In conditions of extrachorial placentation, the chorionic plate is smaller than the basal plate . There are two types of extrachorial placentation : • Circummarginate placenta - In this type , the space between the fetal membranes and the basal plate is filled up by fibrin and old hemorrhage. • Circumvallate placenta - In this type , the peripheral chorion is thickened into a ridge composed of a double fold of chorion and amnion . Complications associated with circumvallate placenta are: • Preterm delivery • Abortions • IUGR • Antepartum hemorrhage • Retained placenta and membranes79 Option A: Placenta succenturiata has one or more small lobes of the placenta placed at varying distances from the main placental margins. Options B & D: Placenta marginata or circummarginate placenta - a thin margin is present between the chorionic and basal plates.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following types of morbidly adherent placenta is shown in the given image?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows placenta increta. Morbidly adherent placenta occurs due to the partial or total absence of the decidua basalis and imperfect development of the fibrinoid or Nitabuch layer. It is of three types : • Placenta accreta - villi are attached to the myometrium. • Placenta increta - villi invade deep into the myometrium. • Placenta percreta - villi penetrate through the entire myometrium and to or through the serosa. Based on the adherence of placental lobules , all three types of morbidly adherent placenta can be: • Total - involving all lobules of the placenta • Focal - involving a single lobule or part of a lobule of the placenta Morbidly adherent placenta can lead to torrential post -partum hemorrhage. It is managed via C-section and peripartum hysterectomy.81

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Given below is the hysterosalpingogram of a woman who presented with infertility . Identify the uterine anomaly seen .
mcqs.explanation: In a hysterosalpingogram , the uterine anomaly cannot be determined as the external contour of the uterus cannot be seen . Hysterosalpingography (HSG) provides excellent information about the interior contour of the uterine cavity. However, it doesn 't show the external contour, so it cannot distinguish between uterine anomalies such as didelphys , bicornuate, septate or arcuate uteruses . Transvaginal 3-D ultrasonography (3D TV -US) is very accurate for the diagnosis and differentiation of uterine anomalies. It is the first and only mandatory step in the assessment of the uterine cavity in patients with a suspected uterine anomaly. Pelvic MRI without contrast provides excellent delineation of both internal and external uterine contours. It should be reserved for patients in whom 3D TV -US is not possible .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The CTG shown in the image below may be seen in which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: The given CTG shows early deceleration which is seen in cases of head compression.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman brings her son to the hospital for routine immunization . While awaiting his turn, she realizes that her seat is stained with blood. She is rushed to the nearby antenatal clinic. Pulse - 96/min, BP - 110 /80 mmHg. Vaginal bleeding is noted and her NST is shown below . What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario along with the NST showing a sinusoidal pattern point towards a diagnosis of vasa previa. Vasa previa is a condition where fetal vessels travel within the membranes and overlie the cervical os. Hence , there can be bleeding during cervical dilatation or membrane rupture . Fetal mortality is high due to fetal exsanguination. When bleeding is present in vasa previa, an emergency cesarean section is indicated . Causes of sinusoidal pattern on NST include : • Severe fetal anemia - Rh isoimmunisation, vasa previa, fetomaternal hemorrhage, or twin to twin transfusion • Opioids - meperidine , morphine, alphaprodine, butorphanol • Amnionitis • Fetal distress • Umbilical cord occlusion .157

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old woman presented with complaints of 7 weeks of amenorrhea and a positive UPT. Her ultrasound scan is shown below . What does the red arrowhead represent ?
mcqs.explanation: The red arrowhead represents the yolk sac. The yellow arrowhead shows the double ring - outer decidua parietalis and inner decidua capsularis. It is referred to as the double decidua sign and is seen in the first trimester transvaginal sonogram. It is useful to confirm an early intrauterine location for the pregnancy.166

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A woman presents at 33-weeks of gestation and the umbilical artery Doppler imaging shows the following finding. What is the next step of management?

options.c: Terminate the pregnancy at 34 weeks of gestation

mcqs.explanation: The umbilical artery Doppler depicts reversal of end-diastolic flow or REDF (waves appearing below the baseline ) which is seen in intrauterine growth restriction. As the period of gestation has exceeded 32 weeks , the pregnancy can be terminated . In case of absent end-diastolic flow (AEDF), the waves just touch the baseline , but don't appear below it. This suggests a fetal compromise, hence the pregnancy is terminated by C-section if >34 weeks .167 Reversed end-diastolic flow (REDF) suggests impending fetal death , hence the pregnancy is terminated by C-section if >32 weeks .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: The anomaly scan of a G3A2 woman is given below . Identify the sign.
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows banana sign. An abnormal anterior curvature of cerebellum along with effacement of cisterna magna produces this appearance . It is seen in spina bifida associated with Arnold-Chiari malformation.Lemon sign: Axial USG image of the fetal head at the level of the biparietal diameter shows inward concavity of both frontal bones instead of the normally seen convexity. This gives the head the appearance of a lemon. It has a strong association with spina bifida and is very useful for detecting this condition.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A doctor tells a 31 -year-old woman, who is 20 weeks pregnant, that her baby has a developmental defect . She has come to you for a second opinion. The following USG finding is seen . Identify the defect .
mcqs.explanation: 170 The given ultrasound image shows an open defect in the calvaria and skin leading to the exposure of the cranial neural tube . This is consistent with the diagnosis of anencephaly . Anencephaly results from incomplete closure of the neural tube . It is one of the earliest detectable congenital defects that can be detected as early as 10 to 11 weeks of gestation . Screening can also be done by serum estimation of maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein (MSAFP). The following are the radiological signs seen in anencephaly . • Frog eye sign - Absence of cranial calvaria , prominent orbits thereby resembling the face of a frog. • Shower cap sign - The absence of the cranium could lead to the protrusion of a disorganized mass of brain tissue . This resembles a shower cap giving rise to a characteristic triangular facial appearance . Neural-tube defects can be prevented with pre-conceptional supplementation of folic acid. A dose of 4 mg daily is recommended in subsequent pregnancies . The frog eye and showercap signs are shown below :171 Option B: Omphalocele is a midline anterior abdominal wall defect through which the solid abdominal viscera and/or bowel may herniate. The extruded abdominal contents are covered in a sac. Given below is an ultrasound image of the fetus suggestive of an omphalocele (asterix).Cystic hygroma is a congenital multiloculated lymphatic lesion that is classically found in the left posterior triangle of the neck. It occurs as a result of sequestration or obstruction of developing lymph vessels . This defect can be picked up in a first-trimester ultrasound. The images below show the MRI and USG appearance of cystic hygroma, respectively :172 Encephalocele is caused due to defects in the skull through which the meninges and/or neural tissue herniate. The squamous part of the occipital bone is the most frequently affected bone. The image shows a newborn with encephalocele .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a part of the vulva ?
mcqs.explanation: Cervix is not a part of the vulva . The vulva includes : • Mons veneris • Labia majora • Labia minora • Clitoris • Vestibule • Vestibular bulb • Greater vestibular glands. The vulva is posteriorly related to the perineum . The triangular space bounded by clitoris, labia minora and fourchette is the vestibule . It is present between the labia minora anteriorly and the introitus posteriorly . The posterior part of the vestibule between the fourchette and the vaginal introitus is called fossa navicularis . The vestibule has 4 openings :13 • Urethral opening • Vaginal orifice opening • Bartholin's duct on either side • Ducts of paraurethral glands

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A patient with stress incontinence required surgical management. While performing a Burch colposuspension , the surgeon approached the space of Retzius. What is this space also known as?
mcqs.explanation: The space of Retzius is the other name for prevesical or retropubic space . Burch colposuspension is a procedure done to relieve stress urinary incontinence. If an extraperitoneal approach is selected , the retropubic space is entered by perforating the transversalis fascia layer of the anterior abdominal wall. Once the retropubic space is dissected, the bladder neck and the vaginal fascia underneath are identified . The bladder is mobilized to the opposite side . At each side of the bladder neck, two to four, preferably non\037absorbable sutures are placed in the space of Retzius. Note :The presacral space is a retroperitoneal space that lies between the peritoneum of the posterior abdominal wall and the sacrum. It contains the superior and inferior hypogastric plexuses . The sacral sympathetic trunk lies against the sacrum's ventral surface .31

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 32 -year-old woman in labor is referred to a tertiary care center . On PV examination, the resident notes that the fetus is in brow presentation , and the largest diameter of the fetal skull is engaged . Identify this diameter .
mcqs.explanation: In brow presentation , the mentovertical diameter is engaged which is the longest diameter of the fetal skull. Normally, it measures 14 cm. The mentovertical diameter extends from the midpoint of the chin to the highest point on the sagittal suture . Engaging diameters of the fetal skull vary with the attitude of the fetal head as given below :Diameters Attitude of the hea d Suboccipitobregma tic Complete flexion61 Diameters Attitude of the hea d Suboccipito -frontal Incomplete flexion Occipitofrontal Marked deflexion Mento -vertical Partial extension Submentovertical Incomplete extensi on Submentobregmati c Complete extension

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A lady at 30 weeks of gestation came for an antenatal check-up. On examination, the uterus corresponds to 34 weeks of gestation and FHR is normal . Ultrasound revealed an AFI of 26 cm. Which fetal anomaly is most likely to be seen with this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical picture is suggestive of polyhydramnios. It can be seen with a fetus having a cleft palate as fetal swallowing is impaired by this anomaly. Polyhydramnios has the following features : • Fundal height greater than period of gestation • Fetal parts are not well palpable • AFI >25cm • SDP >8cm

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 16-year-old girl with primary amenorrhea has the following features . What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The scenario of a 16-year-old girl with absent secondary sexual characters, normal stature , with XX karyotype and high FSH and LH is suggestive of pure gonadal dysgenesis .103 46 XX and 46 XY gonadal dysgenesis without the phenotype of Turner 's syndrome (short stature , webbed neck) is described as pure gonadal dysgenesis . It is characterized by the presence of primary amenorrhea with or without normal secondary sexual characteristics. Option A: Testicular feminizing syndrome occurs in karyotype XY . Secondary sexual characters are present and the uterus is absent. Option C: Kallmann syndrome is a form of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism . GnRH synthesis is reduced , therefore FSH and LH are low, and secondary sexual characters are absent. Option D: Turner syndrome is associated with short stature and karyotype X0. Secondary sexual characters and the uterus is present , but the ovaries are streaked .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 23 -year-old primigravida presents to the antenatal clinic at 30 weeks of gestation . During examination , which of the following cardiovascular findings would not be a cause for alarm ?
mcqs.explanation: S3 is normally heard during pregnancy. The third heart sound (S3) occurs due to rapid diastolic filling in hypervolemic states such as pregnancy, anemia or thyrotoxicosis . Hypervolemia is a normal physiological change during pregnancy. The auscultation of a fixed split S2, fourth heart sound (S4) or a pericardial knock are suggestive of cardiac pathology .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Head circumference is measured from which of the following ultrasonographic views?
mcqs.explanation: Head circumference (HC) is measured from the transthalamic view by placing an ellipse around the outer edge of the skull HC can also be calculated from the biparietal diameter (BPD) and occipital -frontal diameter (OFD).

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Modified Robson's classification class 1 includes :

options.c: Multiparous without previous CS, spontaneous labour
options.d: Multiparous without previous CS, induced /CS before labour

mcqs.explanation: Class 1 of modified Robson's classification includes nullipara, equal to or >37 weeks , single , cephalic , spontaneous labor. It is the most widely accepted classification system available for analyzing characteristics of delivering women worldwide . It consists of 10 patient population categories . The basis for these categories include : • Parity • Onset of labor and mode of delivery • Gestational age • Fetal presentation • No. of fetuses The modified Robson system classification is as follows :Class Nullipara, equal to or >37 we eks, single , cephalic , spontan eous labor Class Nullipara, equal to or >37 we eks, single , cephalic2a:induce d labor2b :CS before labor Class Multipara, equal to or >37 we eks, single , cephalic , spontan eous labor (excludes previous CS) Class Multipara, equal to or >37 we eks, single , cephalic4a :induce d labor4b:CS before labor Class Multipara, previous CS, equa l to or >37 weeks , single , cep halic Class Nullipara, single , breech Class Multipara, single , breech (inc luding previous CS) Class Multiple pregnancies (with or without previous CS)197 Class Nullipara, equal to or >37 we eks, single , cephalic , spontan eous labor Class Singleton pregnancy, oblique /transverse lie (with or witho ut previous CS) Class Single , cephalic <37 weeks (i ncluding previous CS)

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old primigravida is brought to the labour room in the latent phase of labor. How long will you wait till you declare her latent phase to be prolonged ?
mcqs.explanation: Latent phase is said to be prolonged in a primigravida if it lasts for more than 20 hours. Friedman defined prolonged latent phase as: • A nullipara who has not entered the active phase by 20 hours after the onset of the latent phase • A multipara who has not entered the active phase by 14 hours after the onset of the latent phase

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of these steps would you undertake for the management of a patient with shoulder dystocia along with performing the McRoberts manoeuvre?

options.c: Flex the legs over the abdomen

mcqs.explanation: Applying a gentle suprapubic pressure is the first step in the management of shoulder dystocia along with McRoberts manoeuvre. Fundal pressure is not a method of delivery in such cases . Hernandez and Wendel suggested the use of a shoulder dystocia drill to better organize emergency management: • Call for help and mobilize labour assistants , anaesthesia and pediatric doctors. • An attempt at traction is tried followed by episiotomy to afford room posteriorly . • Apply pressure suprapubically , not fundally , with the palm or fist, directing the pressure on the anterior shoulder . • This should be both downward (below the pubic bone) and laterally (toward the baby's face or sternum) in conjunction with the McRoberts manoeuvre. These manoeuvres will resolve most cases of shoulder dystocia . If the above-listed steps fail, the following steps may be attempted , and any of the manoeuvres may be repeated : • Rubin's manoeuvre • Woods corkscrew manoeuvre • Gaskin (all four's position) • Zavanelli manoeuvre • Cleidotomy (fracture of the clavicle of baby) • Symphysiotomy (divide pubic symphysis of mother).

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old term primigravida was brought to the hospital in labor. Prophylactic ventouse was used due to ineffective expulsive efforts by the mother. What is the maximum negative pressure used in this procedure ?
mcqs.explanation: The maximum negative pressure used in ventouse is 0.8 kg/cm2 Gradual vacuum creation is recommended . This is generated by increasing the suction in increments of 0.2 kg/cm2 every 2 minutes . This is done until a total negative pressure of 0.8 kg/cm2 is reached . This slow incremental approach would allow for a more firm attachment of the vacuum cup to the fetal head and thereby a lower failure rate.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: How long does early puerperium last?
mcqs.explanation: Early puerperium is considered to last up to 1 week after delivery . Puerperium can be divided as follows : • Immediate puerperium : within 24 hours • Early puerperium : up to 7 days • Remote /late puerperium : up to 6 weeks or 42 days

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following factors maximally increases the risk of tubal pregnancy?
mcqs.explanation: Prior tubal surgery for ectopic pregnancy has the highest risk of tubal pregnancy among the given options. Risk factors for ectopic pregnancy: • Prior ectopic pregnancy • Prior tubal surgery for ectopic , recanalization of tube post -sterilization • Pelvic inflammatory disease - most common cause for ectopic pregnancy • Infertility • Artificial reproductive therapy • Endometriosis • Smoking • Maternal age >40 years • Contraceptive methods - intrauterine device , progesterone -only pills

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Abortion and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
mcqs.question: Which of the following conditions does not usually cause recurrent miscarriages?
mcqs.explanation: Infections do not usually cause recurrent miscarriages. Common causes of recurrent miscarriage: • Parental chromosomal abnormalities • Anatomical factors - • Uterine synechiae or Asherman syndrome • Uterine leiomyomas • Congenital genital tract anomalies • Immunological factors - • Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome • Endocrine factors - 361 • Luteal phase defect • Polycystic ovarian syndrome

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old multiparous woman presented at 32 weeks of gestation with complaints of recurrent painless vaginal bleeding . On examination, fundal height corresponded to gestational age and fetal heart rate was 140 bpm. Which of the following is not a risk factor for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: 381 The given clinical scenario is suggestive of placenta previa. Pre-eclampsia is a risk factor for abruptio placenta, not placenta previa. Painless bleeding PV , fundal height proportional to gestational age and presence of FHS are the differentiating features of placenta previa from abruptio placenta . Risk factors for placenta previa are: • Demographic factors • Maternal age >35 years • Multiparity • Cigarette smoking • Clinical factors • Prior caesarean section • Past history of placenta previa • Artificial reproductive technology • Multifetal pregnancy • Succenturiate lobe .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In a patient with GDM complicating pregnancy, there was severe bleeding following the delivery of the placenta . On abdominal palpation , the fundus felt soft and later became hard on massaging. Which of the following is not a risk factor for this condition?
mcqs.explanation: In the above scenario, a soft uterus that becomes hard on massaging indicates an atonic uterus . Uterine rupture is a risk factor of traumatic PPH, not atonic PPH. Uterine atony is the failure of the uterus to contract sufficiently after delivery . Thus, bleeding from the placental implantation site is not arrested . GDM complicating pregnancy can cause macrosomia, which is a risk factor of this condition. Risk factors for atonic PPH: • Primiparity or grand multiparity • Previous PPH • Overdistended uterus as in multi-gestational pregnancy, hydramnios, macrosomia • Precipitate labour • Prolonged labour • Uterine malformations • Uterine fibroid • Induction of labour with prostaglandins or oxytocin • Placental abnormalities like placenta previa/accreta/increta/percreta / abruptio placenta • Obesity • Age >40 years

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Transvaginal sonography in a case of clinically suspected preterm labour revealed a short cervix and funnelling of the internal os. What is the shape of the cervix that is likely to be seen here?
mcqs.explanation: U-shaped cervix is seen on tranvaginal sonography (TVS) in preterm labour. On TVS , the cervix should be assessed to determine whether funnelling (internal os width >5 mm) is present. The following is a TVS image showing a V-shaped cervix:Shape of cervi x Inference T shaped Normal427 Shape of cervi x Inference Y shaped Suspicion of preterm labour V shaped Funneling of internal os U shaped Incompetent osPreterm labo ur

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following are complications that can be seen in a patient with molar pregnancy?
mcqs.explanation: Thyrotoxicosis is seen as a complication of molar pregnancy, not hypothyroidism . Complications in molar pregnancy include : • Immediate: • Early-onset pre-eclampsia - molar placentas produce more antiangiogenic proteins than normal placentas . • Thyrotoxicosis - as �o component of hCG mimics TSH and causes thyroid storm • Acute pulmonary insufficiency - due to embolization of trophoblastic cells • Electrolyte imbalance i.e., hypokalemia, hyponatremia - due to hyperemesis caused by \032 hCG • Shock - hemorrhage due to the separation of vesicles and intra-peritoneal haemorrhage • Disseminated intravascular coagulation • Late: Choriocarcinoma .446

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman was brought by her husband after fainting at home. He gave a history of her being clumsy and forgetful over the last few weeks . Investigations revealed high MCV with hypersegmented neutrophils . How will you manage this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario points to vitamin B12 deficiency . It is treated by vitamin B12 injections with folic acid supplementation . �Mg of IM cyanocobalamin should be given initially every week for 6 weeks , following which it should be given once every month. Megaloblastic anemia caused by Vit B12 deficiency should be identified and treated accordingly because folic acid supplementation alone will not help . Causes of Vit B12 deficiency leading to anemia in pregnancy: • Gastric resection • Addisonian pernicious anemia • Crohn's disease • Ileal resection • Bacterial overgrowth in the small bowel .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A G2P1 patient at 25 weeks of gestation is brought to the emergency with right upper quadrant pain and one episode of seizure . CBC reveals a Hb of 7.6gm/dl and a platelet count of 70,000/microL . What is the definitive management?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario is suggestive of eclampsia and HELLP syndrome. The definitive management is the termination of pregnancy. In cases of pre-eclampsia , indications for termination of pregnancy, irrespective of gestational age , are as follows: • Eclampsia (give MgSO4 followed by induction of labor) • HELLP syndrome • Persistent symptoms of severe pre-eclampsia or severe hypertension • Pulmonary edema • Significant renal dysfunction , coagulopathy485 • Abruption of placenta • Fetal compromise In mild pre-eclampsia , steroids are given and the patient is delivered at 37 weeks . In severe pre-eclampsia : • If pregnancy is >34 weeks - MgSO4 is given for prophylaxis of eclampsia and the pregnancy is terminated. • If pregnancy is at 27-34 weeks - in the absence of contraindications, expectant management is followed and the baby is delivered at 34 weeks , as shown below in the flowchart .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 29-year-old woman with overt diabetes comes to you for pre-conception counseling . Which of the following congenital heart defects are least likely to occur if she were to have a child?
mcqs.explanation: Tetrology of Fallot (TOF) is usually not seen in infants of diabetic mothers. Ventricular septal defect and transposition of great arteries are the most common cardiac anomalies in infants of diabetic mothers. Cardiac defects that present more often in infants of diabetic mothers are: • Transposition of the great arteries (TGA) • Double outlet right ventricle (DORV) • Ventricular septal defect (VSD) • Truncus arteriosus • Tricuspid atresia • Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA)501 The most common cardiac anomaly in an infant of a diabetic mother is a controversial topic . Most resources mention VSD and TGA are the most common and do not specify which among them is more common.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Women with the highest risk of endocarditis in pregnancy are those with _____
mcqs.explanation: Women at the highest risk for endocarditis are those with cyanotic cardiac disease and prosthetic valves. The American heart association recommends prophylaxis for dental procedures with: • Prosthetic valves • Unrepaired cyanotic heart defects518 • Valvulopathy after heart transplantation American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists do not recommend endocarditis prophylaxis for either vaginal or cesarean delivery in the absence of pelvic infection .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.chapter: Hepatic Disorders and Infections in Pregnancy
mcqs.question: A woman presented to the clinic with severe lower abdominal pain and dysuria at 28 weeks of gestation . Suprapubic tenderness was noted on palpation . Urine examination revealed pyuria with microscopic hematuria. All of the following can be used to treat this condition except ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of cystitis . Ciprofloxacin, a fluoroquinolone antibiotic, is contraindicated in pregnancy as it causes cartilage and bone defects in the fetus . Antibiotics are used for treating cystitis in pregnancy. Antibiotics safe in pregnancy include : • Penicillin group • Cephalosporins • Erythromycin • Metronidazole (except in the 1st trimester) Antibiotics unsafe in pregnancy include : • Tetracycline • Aminoglycoside • Chloramphenicol • Metronidazole (in the first trimester) • Fluoroquinolones

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a feature of menometrorrhagia?
mcqs.explanation: Menometrorrhagia refers to menstrual bleeding at frequent intervals.562 Menometrorrhagia means excessive , prolonged bleeding that occurs at irregularly timed and frequent intervals. It can be caused by cervical cancer and granulosa cell tumors.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: During post -op rounds, you note one of the patients has developed fever and flank pain. The nurses inform you that her abdominal drain outputs have been consistently high. Which of the following procedures has the highest incidence of the complication suspected here?
mcqs.explanation: The given case scenario is suggestive of ureteric injury. The highest incidence of this complication is seen with Wertheim's hysterectomy . Urinary tract injury occurs almost exclusively in major gynecologic surgery that involves surgical dissection in proximity to the ureters or bladder . Vaginal hysterectomy tends to have lower rates of ureteric injuries than open (abdominal, Wertheim) or laparoscopic routes . The highest risk for ureteric injury is associated with the following procedures : • Surgical debulking of gynecological cancers • Advanced pelvic reconstructive surgery • Laparoscopic hysterectomy Patients with ureteric injuries have a complicated post -operative period . They can present with the following features : • Fever • Flank pain • Abdominal distension • Prolonged paralytic ileus - bowel sounds are absent • High drain outputs , in case abdominal drains are placed . CT urogram and retrograde pyelography are the investigations of choice . They reveal urinary extravasation from the ureter. Ureteric injuries are prevented by careful division of tissue planes during pelvic or genitourinary surgeries . The condition is managed by prompt surgical repair by ureteroureterostomy or percutaneous ureterostomy .584

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 55 -year-old lady presents with third degree uterine prolapse . Which of the following is the best management for her?

options.c: Vaginal hysterectomy with pelvic floor repair

mcqs.explanation: In the clinal scenario of a 55 -year-old woman with third-degree uterine prolapse , the ideal management is vaginal hysterectomy with pelvic floor repair. Uterine prolapse is the descent of the uterus from its normal position which usually occurs due to laxity of ligaments that offer support , seen often due to childbirth, aging, or trauma. The uterine descent is clinically categorized into: • First degree : the external os remains above the vaginal introitus605 • Second degree : The external os protrudes below the vaginal introitus but the uterine body remains inside the vagina • Third degree (Syn: Complete prolapse ): The uterine , cervix, body, and fundus descend to lie outside the introitus • Procidentia involves prolapse of the uterus with the entire vagina everted . The patient usually presents with a sense of heaviness in the pelvic region with lower back discomfort. Based on the structures involved the patient can additionally have urinary symptoms (like incontinence and urgency ), bowel disturbances (constipation and tenesmus ), or sexual discomfort during intercourse . Symptomatic uterine prolapse is managed surgically with different procedures based on the profile of the patient . Conservative management is done for old asymptomatic women with mild degree prolapse . A vaginal hysterectomy is recommended for patients who satisfy the following criteria: • >40 years of age • Have completed their families • Do not wish to preserve menstrual and child-bearing function Other options : Option A: Fothergill repair or Manchester operation is a procedure done to preserve the reproductive function and vaginal prolapse with supravaginal cervix elongation . It initially involves preliminary curettage with low amputation of the cervix. After Mackenrodt's ligament is plicated , anterior colporrhaphy and colpoperineorrhaphy are performed . Option B: Sling operation (Purandare's operation) is indicated in congenital or nulliparous prolapse without cystocele . The procedure involves the extraperitoneal passage of rectus sheath strips joined to the anterior surface of the cervix by silk sutures . Option D: Shirodkar procedure is a type of abdominal sling surgery done in young women to retain menstrual and reproductive function. It involves using a sling to fix the cervix to the lumbosacral fascia.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Which of the following changes are not seen in fibroids?
mcqs.explanation: Squamous metaplasia is not seen in fibroid.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A young lady who presented with oligomenorrhea and infertility is diagnosed with PCOS. Mutation of which of the following genes can cause this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Mutation of the CYP21 gene can cause polycystic ovarian syndrome.662 The gene for 21 -hydroxylase (CYP21 ) is located in the short arm of chromosome 6. Heterozygosity of the gene has been linked to the development of PCOS. Defects in this gene also lead to congenital adrenal hyperplasia .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: You are inserting Nova-T in a patient for spacing of births. This device contains______.
mcqs.explanation: 689 Nova-T contains both copper and silver. The addition of the silver increases its effective lifespan .In copper -carrying devices , copper wire is wrapped around the vertical stem of a polypropylene frame. Some of them have copper wire wrapped around the arms too. Based on the surface area, they are of various types : • Copper T 380 A • Multiload copper 250 • Copper T 200 • Copper 7 • Copper T 220 • Nova-T They are effective for 3–5 years. It is estimated that about 50 mcg of copper is eluted daily in the uterus . Copper T 380A, known as Paraguard, has a lifespan of 10 years. Nova T has a lifespan of 5 years.690

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: In an obese lady with complaints of vaginal discharge , a vaginal pH of 4.2 was detected . Which organism is implicated in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The likely causative agent in the given clinical scenario is Candida which is known to flourish in an acidic environment. The pH of the vaginal discharge in candidal vaginitis is in the range of 4-4.5.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A 42-year-old woman presented to the emergency room with abdominal pain and fever for the last 48 hours. She has been using a Cu T 380A for contraception for the past 8 years. On examination, cervical motion tenderness was present . What is the most likely organism to have caused her condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario points towards a diagnosis of PID in an IUCD user. The most common organism causing this condition is Actinomyces . It has been reported in 7% of IUCD users if the device is worn for more than 2 years. This emphasizes the need for strict asepsis during insertion of the device and the need for strict follow up of women wearing these devices. Organisms causing PID are:741 Sexually transmitted : • Chlamydia (most common) • Gonococcus • Mycoplasma • Trichomonas Pyogenic Aerobes : • Staphylococci • Streptococci • E Coli Anaerobes: • Bacteroides fragilis • Peptostreptococcus • Clostridium • Actinomyces (most common in IUD users) Other: • Mycobacterium tuberculosis

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: A gynaecologist suspects tuberculous salpingitis in a young woman and suggests some investigations to confirm the diagnosis. Which of the following statements is true about these investigations?

options.a: A differential WBC count shows lymphocytosis in advanced disease .
options.b: The ESR is frequently raised and is non-specific in early disease .
options.c: The Mantoux test is positive and indicative of current exposure to tubercle bacilli.
options.d: The Quantiferon test is positive and indicates latent tuberculosis .

mcqs.explanation: The Quantiferon test will be positive in patients having genital TB . It is an indicator of latent tuberculosis . The Quantiferon test measures the release of interferon-gamma by T cells following stimulation by antigens unique to Mycobacterium tuberculosis . A differential WBC count shows lymphocytosis at all stages of genital tuberculosis . The ESR is frequently raised and is a non-specific investigation at any stage of the disease . None of these tests can be used for confirmation as these markers are raised in many infections . The Mantoux test is positive in 90% of cases of genital TB . It is indicative of past exposure to the tubercle bacilli. It is not a confirmatory investigation but a negative result indicates tuberculosis to be unlikely.

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: What is the diagnostic value of FSH in menopause ?
mcqs.explanation: The diagnostic value of FSH in menopause is >40 mIU/mL . Hormone levels in menopausal women:Hormone Level Estradiol 5 to 25 pg /m l FSH >40 mIU/m L LH 50-100 mIU L/ml Growth hormone, inhibin B, AMH Decreases

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Vulvar carcinoma was diagnosed in a 68-year-old woman who presented with itching and mass over the vulva for 6 months. Sentinel lymph node biopsy revealed positive inguinal nodes . What is the stage of the tumor?
mcqs.explanation: According to FIGO staging , tumor with positive inguinal lymph node is classified as stage III .

mcqs.subject: OBGYN
mcqs.question: Identify the true statement about the staging of cancer cervix.

options.a: Clinical examination is the first step in staging
options.b: Tumor markers are important for diagnosis of metastasis
options.c: CT scan is the best method to assess principal tumors
options.d: MRI is the best method to assess nodal metastasis

mcqs.explanation: Clinical examination is the first step in staging carcinoma cervix. Clinical examination was the principal method in staging until the 2018 FIGO guidelines which recommended the use of imaging and histological investigations when available. USG, CT, MRI, and PET-CT can be used to assess the extent of the tumor, nodal status , and local or systemic spread . MRI is the best method to assess the principal tumor while PET-CT is the best method to assess nodal metastasis. FIGO no longer mandates biochemical investigations, such as tumor markers , for diagnosis of metastasis .847

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old lady presents with the abnormality as shown below . She is diagnosed with uveal melanoma. What is the embryological origin of the cells involved?
mcqs.explanation: Uveal melanomas arise from uveal melanocytes . Uveal and conjunctival melanocytes are derived from the neural crest cells .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A 34-year-old lady comes to the clinic complaining of problems in her vision. On perimetry , a visual field defect as shown below is obtained . Which of the following vessels does not supply the anatomical location of the lesion?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows bitemporal hemianopia, a defect caused by optic chiasmal lesions . The middle cerebral artery does not supply the optic chiasma. Blood supply of optic chiasma: • Anterior cerebral artery - dorsal chiasma • Anterior communicating artery - ventral chiasma • Internal carotid artery - ventral chiasma • Superior hypophyseal artery - ventral (branch of internal carotid artery).

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A 12 -year-old girl you examined in an outreach camp is found to have this abnormality. What is the most common site where the condition is seen ?
mcqs.explanation: The condition depicted in the image is a coloboma of the iris, and the most common site of coloboma is the inferonasal quadrant. A coloboma is a congenital malformation in one of the structures in the eye , such as the iris, retina, choroid, or optic disc, due to the failure of embryonic fissure closure . Coloboma of the uveal tract may be typical (seen in the inferonasal quadrant ) or atypical (occasionally found in other positions ). Typical coloboma is of two types : • Complete : Extends from pupil to optic nerve, causing a corresponding lens indentation. • Incomplete : May involve iris alone, or iris and ciliary body (more common), or iris, ciliary body and a part of choroid. Other embryonic remnants in the eye : • Mittendorf 's dot - Remnant of the anterior end of the hyaloid artery • Bergmeister papilla - Remnant of the posterior end of the hyaloid artery • Persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous (PHPV ) - Failure of fetal vasculature to regress The image below shows a fundoscopy view of persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous.16

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A child was brought with complaints of decreased vision. Fundus examination shows a developmental anomaly as shown below . What is the cause of this anomaly?

options.a: Incomplete closure of the embryonic fissure
options.b: Faulty migration of neural crest cells

mcqs.explanation: The image shows a coloboma of the optic disc, accompanied by a large chorioretinal coloboma located below the optic disc, which is caused by incomplete closure of the embryonic fissure . This developmental anomaly may involve the optic nerve, choroid, retina, and iris. Coloboma of the optic disc can present in two forms: a minor effect often associated with refractive errors like hypermetropia and astigmatism and a fully developed coloboma that appears as a large inferonasal whitish excavation resembling the optic disc. Defective vision and superior visual field defects are typically associated with fully developed coloboma. Additionally , this condition may be associated with chorioretinal coloboma, a congenital anomaly where the developing optic cup fails to fuse completely , leading to abnormal choroidal and retinal development . Note : Faulty migration of neural crest cells results in anterior segment dysgenesis .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: What is the embryological origin of the structure marked in the image?
mcqs.explanation: The lacrimal gland arises from the surface ectoderm .17

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: In the anatomy dissection hall, you are shown the dissected orbit with the markers as shown below . You are asked to choose the muscles causing depression of the eyeball . Which will you choose ?
mcqs.explanation: 22 The muscles responsible for the depression of the eyeball are the inferior rectus (E) and superior oblique (A). Image markings : • A- Superior oblique • B- Levator palpebrae superiors • C- Superior rectus • D- Inferior oblique • E- Inferior rectusNerve supply of extra-ocular muscles : • Oculomotor nerve (III )- Superior rectus , inferior rectus , medial rectus , inferior oblique, and levator palpebrae superioris • Abducens nerve (VI )- Lateral rectus • Trochlear nerve (IV )- Superior oblique23

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: What is the distance between point A and B shown below ?
mcqs.explanation: In the image, point A is the optic disc and point B is the fovea. The fovea is situated about 2 disc diameters (3–4 mm) away from the temporal margin of the optic disc. The optic disc is an area of about 1.5 mm. There is a blind spot / physiological scotoma, corresponding to the optic disc.36

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: You are studying the optics of a patient with regular astigmatism. Identify the point at which the clearest image is formed?
mcqs.explanation: The given figure is a Sturm's conoid. It represents a bundle of light rays formed by a regularly astigmatic surface . The image is clearest or least confusing as point D, the circle of least confusion. When light passes through a regularly astigmatic surface (surface with toric curvature), vertical and horizontal rays converge at different points. The distance between the points of convergence (focus ) of the vertical and horizontal rays is called the focal interval of strum. (distance between points B and F). The circle of least confusion/ circle of diffusion lies at the mid-point of this interval. For the given Sturm's conoid, • At point A, a horizontal oval is formed because vertical rays converge more rapidly than horizontal rays. • At point B, vertical rays come to a focus, while horizontal rays are still converging; so, it will be a horizontal straight line. • At points C, D, and E, the vertical rays are diverging and horizontal rays are still converging.37 • At point D, the vertical rays have diverged as much as the horizontal rays have converged; so, we get a perfect circle called the circle of least confusion. • At point E, a vertical oval is formed. • At point F, a vertical straight line is formed • At point G and beyond , both rays are diverging, and we always get a vertical oval/prolate ellipse .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A woman comes to the ophthalmology OPD because of having vision difficulties for the last 3 months. On fundoscopic examination, the following findings are seen . Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows a fundus typical of pathological myopia due to the stretching of the retina. The tigroid appearance or tessellated appearance of the fundus can be appreciated . As the eye enlarges, the retinal pigment epithelium becomes thinner, resulting in: • A tessellated (checkered ) appearance of the fundus • Increased visibility of the choroidal vasculature Other features of the myopic fundus are as follows : • Lacquer cracks are spontaneous ruptures of the elastic lamina of Bruch's membrane. It appears yellowish -white . it is usually located in the posterior pole . • Annular gray shadow around the optic disc • Lattice degeneration • Foster Fuchs spots • Cystoid degeneration • Total retinal atrophy59

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: While performing the following procedure on a 35-year-old male at a distance of 1 meter, you found out that the red reflex was not moving with the movement of the instrument. How will you interpret your findings?
mcqs.explanation: The above image shows the procedure of retinoscopy (skiascopy) being performed . As the red reflex is not moving with the movement of the retinoscope , the patient is interpreted as having myopia of 1D. Retinoscopy is an objective method of determining the error of refraction. It is based on the principle that when light is reflected from a mirror into the eye , the direction in which tlhe light will travel across the pupil depends upon the refractive stale of the eye . Interpretation of retinoscopy done at 1m is: • No movement of red reflex : Myopia of 1D • Movement of red reflex with retinoscope : Emmetropia , hypermetropia , myopia less than 1D • Movement of red reflex against the retinoscope : Myopia more than 1D

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A physician observed the following finding in a small child who came for an eye exam. This finding is associated with which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows convergent squint or esotropia , which is commonly seen in children with hyperopia , also known as hypermetropia. Esotropia results due to increased accommodative effort in cases where there is under correction of hypermetropia . The condition may be prevented by full hypermetropic correction. If the child is unable to wear the glasses due to flat nasal bridge or if the child is less than 2 years old, the accommodation may be treated with drugs. Miotic drugs with anticholinesterase activity such as di-isopropyl fluorophosphate (DFP) or echothiophate can be used in these children. Further treatment may include orthotropic training or surgical correction of the squint.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Match the images shown with the refractive errors they represent .
mcqs.explanation: 76 The correct answer is 1 - d, 2 - b, 3 - c, 4 - a. Astigmatism is a refractive error in which the rays of light entering the eye are refracted differently in different meridia of the eye . Meridia of the eye correspond to the lines of longitude on a globe . There are two types of astigmatism - regular and irregular. In regular astigmatism, refractive power changes uniformly from one meridian to another. Thus, two principal meridia are present . The rays of light from infinity form two focal points due to the difference in curvature of the two principal meridia. Based on the relation of the two focal points to the retina, regular astigmatism has the following types : • Simple astigmatism: One focal point lies on the retina. In simple myopic type , the second focal point lies in front of the retina while in simple hypermetropic type , the second focal point lies behind the retina. • Compound astigmatism: In compound hypermetropic type , both focal points lie behind the retina. In compound myopic type , both focal points lie in front of the retina. • Mixed astigmatism: One focal point lies in front of while the second focal point lies behind the retina.Imag e Refractive error 1 d. Simple hypermetropic asti gmatism 2 b. Simple myopic astigmatis m 3 c. Compound myopic astigma tism 4 a. Mixed astigmatism77

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: During your morning jogging routine, you found a pair of spectacles lying on the sidewalk . The spectacles are shown below . What type of presbyopic lens is present in these spectacles ?
mcqs.explanation: The given lens in the image is a typical example of progressive lenses . Progressive lenses are identified as such due to the absence of the line of demarcation on the lens. They are gradually optimized for reading vision, distant vision, and for intermediate vision, such as computer work.82

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: The spectacles shown in the image are not used for the management of which of the following ?
mcqs.explanation: 85 The given image shows spectacles made of lenses with two different optical power . Thus, it is a pair of bifocal spectacles which is not used in hypermetropia or myopia. Bifocal glasses have different corrective powers in the upper segment for distant vision and lower segment for near vision. Thus, they are useful in conditions where both distance and near vision are affected , like the following : 1. Presbyopia (option A): It is a definitive indication. It is used to correct age -related near and far vision defects. 2. Aphakia (option B): It provides both near and far vision correction when intra-ocular lens insertion is contraindicated . 3. Paediatric pseudophakia (option C): It is used to correct refractive errors or accommodative fluctuations post intra-ocular lens (IOL) insertion. 4. Non refractive accomodative esotropia In hypermetropia there is defect in near vision only and hence a single vision glasses having uniform corrective power throught the entire surface is used instead of bifocal glasses .86

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding this condition?

options.a: The condition is commonly associated with a benign course .
options.b: It can occur spontaneously in elders with systolic hypertension .
options.c: The blood gets absorbed gradually in 6-8 weeks time without treatment .
options.d: Use of NSAIDs and aspirin to treat the condition should be avoided.

mcqs.explanation: The image given above shows a subconjunctival haemorrhage in the eye . In this condition, the blood gets absorbed gradually in 1-3 weeks time without treatment . A subconjunctival hemorrhage is also called subconjunctival ecchymosis . It is due to the rupture of small blood vessels and can occur spontaneously in elders with systolic hypertension or after local trauma. The condition is commonly associated with a benign course but, if the posterior limit of the hemorrhage is not seen , one should check for the base of the skull fracture. Recurrent episodes warrant investigations for a bleeding diathesis or leukaemia. The use of NSAIDs and aspirin to treat the condition should be avoided.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: The newborn eye is usually ______.
mcqs.explanation: A newborn is usually hypermetropic by +2D to +3D. The anteroposterior (AP) diameter of the eyeball at birth is about 16.5 mm, which is about 70% of the adult size. This reduced axial length causes light to converge behind the retina, leading to12 hypermetropia . Additionally , the corneal diameter at birth is 10 mm. The adult size (11.7 mm) is attained by 2 years of age . The orbit is more divergent (50\260) as compared to adult (45\260). Note : The lacrimal glands are underdeveloped in a newborn and, hence , do not secrete tears.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following structures is attached to Whitnall's tubercle ?

options.a: Check ligament of the medial rectus
options.c: Check ligament of the lateral rectus

mcqs.explanation: Check ligament of the lateral rectus is attached to Whitnall's tubercle . Lateral orbital tubercle or Whitnall's tubercle is a small elevation on the orbital surface of the zygomatic bone, just within the lateral orbital margin. It is about 11 mm below the fronto-zygomatic suture . Four structures are attached to it: • Check ligament of the lateral rectus • Lockwood's ligament (Suspensory ligament of the eyeball ) • Lateral palpebral ligament • Lateral horn of the levator aponeurosis The Whitnall's ligament or the superior transverse ligament of the eye , is attached to the superior tarsal plate and the orbital bone.20

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: A 6-year-old child complains that she cannot see anything on the whiteboard clearly. On ophthalmological examination, she is found to have a 2 mm shortening of the axial length of the eyeball . How much eye power will this lead to?
mcqs.explanation: Shortening of 2mm of the axial length of the eyeball will lead to 6D of hypermetropia . In axial hypermetropia , 1mm shortening of the anteroposterior diameter of the eye results in 3 dioptres of hypermetropia . Therefore, 2-mm shortening will lead to 6D of hypermetropia . In curvature hypermetropia , a 1mm increase in radius of curvature results in 6 dioptres of hypermetropia.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Elementary Optics and Physiology of Vision
mcqs.question: What is the visible range of the electromagnetic spectrum of the human eye ?
mcqs.explanation: The visible range of the electromagnetic spectrum for the human eye is 400 –700 nm. Theories of color vision: • Trichromatic theory (Young –Helmholtz theory ) assumes that there are three types of color receptors . Each receptor is assumed to respond to all wavelengths , however, each has different spectral sensitivities . • Opponent process theory , also known as the Hering theory , assumes three sets of receptor systems —red-green, blue -yellow , and black-white . Each one of these functions as an antagonistic pair (e.g., red light stimulates the red receptors and, at the same time, inhibits the green ). • Edwin Land 's theory has three separate color systems (retinexes ). Each is an analog to a black-and-white picture .44

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following myopias is not associated with high degree of refractive error ?
mcqs.explanation: School myopia or simple myopia is associated with a low to moderate degree of refractive error . Simple myopia is the most common type of myopia. It results from a normal biological variation in the development of the eye i.e. increased anteroposterior diameter of eyeball or increased curvature of the cornea.58 Other options : Options A and D: Pathological /Degenerative /Progressive myopia occurs due to degenerative changes in the retina, leading to a high degree of refractive error . Option B: Congenital myopia is associated with congenital anomalies of the eye , and a high degree of refractive error . Note : Other types of myopia include : 1. Nocturnal myopia: Accommodation is induced by low contrast in dim illumination 2. Induced myopia: Temporary and reversible myopia due to external agents (e.g., pilocarpine-induced accommodation spasm)/variations in blood sugar levels 3. Pseudomyopia : Inappropriately excessive accommodation due to overstimulation/ciliary spasm.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man wants to undergo surgery for hypermetropia . All of the following are options to treat his refractive error except ?
mcqs.explanation: Photorefractive keratectomy is not the surgical modality of the treatment of hypermetropia . Photorefractive keratectomy is a laser ablation technique for the correction of myopia. An excimer laser is used to cause flattening of the central cornea.65

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: What is the accommodative amplitude of a patient with a near point at 20 cm and a far point at infinity?
mcqs.explanation: The amplitude of accommodation for the above patient would be 5. Near point of accommodation (NPA) is the closest distance at which the near object is clearly focussed without blur. Amplitude of accommodation is the maximum power of the lens that permits clear near vision without blur. Its unit is dioptre (D). The amplitude of accommodation is the reciprocal of NPA in meters . 20 cm is 1/5th of a meter. Therefore, accommodative amplitude is its inverse, that is, 5D. The NPA is measured clinically using a scale device such as the Prince, Berens, or Royal Air Force (RAF) ruler.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: A UNICEF volunteer presented with a bilateral red eye of 2 days duration beginning on a return flight from Ghana. The infection spread among all her family members within a day of her return. Initial examination revealed lid edema , serous discharge , and severe sub-conjunctival hemorrhage. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of a patient with bilateral red-eye and a rapid spread of infection to family members points towards a likely diagnosis of hemorrhagic conjunctivitis. Examination findings of lid edema , serous discharge , and subconjunctival hemorrhage further consolidate this102 diagnosis. Causes : • Enterovirus 70 (most important) • Coxsackievirus 24 • Echovirus 34 • Adenovirus • Pneumococcus • Haemophilus There is no treatment currently available . The infection generally resolves itself within a five to seven-day period . The use of steroids can actually cause a corneal microbial superinfection which then requires antimicrobial therapy to eliminate . The image given below shows the eyes of a patient with acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: An 8-year-old boy had to miss school because the matting of his eyelids made it difficult to open them in the morning and caused severe pain. His agonized mother rushed him to the hospital and reported that he had a fever and red eye for 4 days. Which group of lymph nodes is likely to be enlarged ?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical scenario of fever and red eyes , associated with matting of eyelids and pain, is suggestive of conjunctivitis. Lymph from the conjunctiva drains directly into the submandibular and preauricular nodes and hence , these group of lymph nodes are likely to be enlarged . The lymphatic drainage of the conjunctiva is as follows - • From the medial side , one-third of the superior and medial two -thirds of the inferior conjunctiva \033 Submandibular nodes • From the lateral side , two -thirds of the superior conjunctiva and lateral one-third of the inferior conjunctiva \033 Preauricular nodes Specialized collections of T and B lymphocytes underlying a modified epithelium is known as conjunctiva-associated lymphoid tissue (CALT ) present in the stroma (substantia propria). It is critical in the initiation and regulation of ocular-surface immune responses . Note : The stroma also consists of the accessory lacrimal glands of Krause and Wolfring which are exocrine glands responsible for the basal secretion of the middle aqueous layer of the tear film. The image given below shows the lymphatic drainage of the conjunctiva.113

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: All the following statements are true for a 40-year-old diagnosed with scleritis except -

options.a: Scleromalacia perforans is associated with systemic disease .
options.b: Pain is not a prominent feature .
options.d: Retinal detachment is a known complication.

mcqs.explanation: Pain is a prominent feature of scleritis . Scleritis is an inflammation of the sclera. Patients present with moderate to severe eye pain, redness , lacrimation and photophobia . Anterior scleritis affects the sclera in front of the equator and may lead to the following complications : • Acute infiltrative stromal keratitis • Sclerosing keratitis • Peripheral ulcerative keratitis128 • Uveitis • Glaucoma • Hypotony (rarely phthisis ) • Perforation of the sclera Posterior scleritis involves the sclera behind the equator and may lead to uveal effusion with choroidal detachment , disc edema , proptosis or exudative retinal detachment . Scleromalacia perforans is a type of anterior scleritis . It typically occurs in elderly women with rheumatoid arthritis (systemic disease ). There is ischemia and necrosis of the sclera; however, there is no inflammation. Clinically, it is a painless condition with a white eye . Areas of thinned out sclera through which the uvea shines are seen in such patients .

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Basics of Cornea and Infectious Keratitis
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man presents with a history of injury to the eye caused by a leaf 5 days ago, resulting in pain, photophobia , and redness of the eye for 2 days. What would be the most likely pathology ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical vignette of the patient presenting with pain, photophobia , and redness of the eye following trauma by a vegetative matter is suggestive of a fungal corneal ulcer. Fungal corneal ulcer also known as mycotic keratitis is usually caused by trauma from vegetative matter such as branches of trees , leaves and animal tails. Injudicious use of topical steroids and antibiotics increases the predisposition to develop secondary fungal keratitis. Mycotic keratitis can be caused by • Filamentous fungi such as Aspergillus and Fusarium • Yeasts such as Candida and cryptococcus • Dimorphic fungi such as Histoplasma and Blastomyces Typically in fungal corneal ulcers , the signs are more prominent than the symptoms . The symptoms of fungal keratitis are similar to that of bacterial ulcers which include pain, lacrimation, photophobia , blurred vision, and redness of the eyes .146 A typical fungal ulcer has the following signs: • Greyish white looking dry corneal ulcer with rolled out margin. • Feathery finger-like extensions into the corneal stroma under intact epithelium • Wessley ring which is a sterile immune ring that occurs due to the deposition of immune complexes • Multiple small satellite lesions around the ulcer • Hypopyon : The hypopyon in fungal ulcer is immobile and unsterile unlike bacterial ulcer (sterile hypopyon ) • Perforation is rare • Corneal vascularization is usually absent. A diagnosis of fungal ulcer is made by a typical history of trauma with vegetative matter followed by clinical examination and KOH mount or SDA agar cultures from corneal scrappings . The image below depicts a fungal corneal ulcer with the arrowhead indicating a satellite lesion.Other options : Option A: Anterior uveitis is the inflammation of the uveal tissue from the iris up to the pars plicata of the ciliary body. Infectious uveitis can be caused by the exogenous entry of the organisms following penetrating injuries, perforation of corneal ulcer, and post -intaocular operations. Acute anterior uveitis presents with symptoms of pain, photophobia , lacrimation, blurring of vision and redness of the eye . Signs of anterior uveitis include : • Aqueous flare - It is the earliest sign of acute anterior uveitis, it occurs following the leakage of protein particles into the aqueous humor. • Keratic precipitates (KP) - These are pathognomonic for anterior uveitis. They are proteinaceous cellular deposits at the back of the cornea arranged in a triangular fashion. These include mutton fat KP's as seen in granulomatous uveitis and granular KP's of non granulomatous uveitis.147 • Iris nodules : typically occur in granulomatous uveitis. Koppe 's nodules are at the pupillary border and Busacca's nodules are situated near the collarette . Option C: Conjunctivitis is the inflammation of the conjunctiva of which the bacterial conjunctivitis is the most common. Acute bacterial conjunctivitis is characterized by marked conjunctival hyperemia , swelling of the conjunctiva(chemosis), edematous eyelids , sticking together of lid margins and mucopurulent discharge from the eye . The image shows a patient with bacterial conjunctivitis.Option D: Corneal laceration: Partial corneal laceration or lamellar corneal laceration occurs from a blunt trauma and is treated by patching and antibiotics.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Deposition of which of the following is responsible for band-shaped keratopathy?
mcqs.explanation: Band-shaped keratopathy is caused by pathological calcium deposition on the cornea in the form of a band. On exam, there is a white band-like formation of calcium across the corneal surface with irregular borders and a peripheral clearing of cornea between the calcium deposits and the limbus. The calcium deposition is typically found beneath the epithelial layer within Bowman's layer but may extend into the anterior stroma. Once the visual axis starts to get involved, there will be progressive loss of vision. Recurrence is common unless the predisposing cause is identified and treated . Local causes such as chronic ocular irritation or inflammatory conditions and systemic diseases that elevate serum calcium levels are the main causes for band-shaped keratopathy. It can rarely have hereditary causes as well . Image given below shows band-shaped keratopathy.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.question: Which of the following stains is used in identifying granular dystrophy of the cornea?
mcqs.explanation: Masson trichrome stains stromal hyaline deposits in granular dystrophy of the cornea. Granular corneal dystrophy belongs to the stromal dystrophy of the cornea. It is of autosomal dominant inheritance and is caused by a defect in the TGFB1 gene . Granular corneal dystrophy is characterized by milky, granular, hyaline deposits in the anterior stroma, which may coalesce into irregular shapes . The peripheral cornea and the area between the opacities /deposits remain clear. Early symptoms may involve light sensitivity , glare, ocular discomfort, pain, and watering . As opacification progresses with age , visual acuity decreases . The following image shows numerous irregularly shaped discrete crumb-like corneal opacities of Granular dystrophy , which stain bright red with Masson trichrome.

mcqs.subject: Ophthalmology
mcqs.chapter: Retinal vascular disorders and Retinal detachment
mcqs.question: All of the following are true statements regarding retinopathy of prematurity except :

options.a: First screening should be done 32 weeks PMA or 4 weeks PNA, whichever is later
options.b: For infants less than 28 week , screen at 3 week of postnatal age to detect APROP
options.c: Neonates are best examined at ophthalmology OPD and hence should be transported
options.d: Screening is done using indirect ophthalmoscopy by an expert ophthalmologist
