mcqs.question: Cross product ratio can be arrived from:
mcqs.explanation: Cross product ratio (Odds ratio) can be obtained from the case-control study.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A research scholar is preparing to do a prospective cohort study in a hospital to evaluate the association of H. pylori with inflammatory bowel disease. Which of the following measures must she take, before starting the study?

options.a: Enrol all patients taking proton pump inhibitors
options.b: Enrol all patients on whom endoscopy was done
options.c: Exclude all patients diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease
options.d: Exclude all patients with positive urea breath test for H. pylori

mcqs.explanation: All patients diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) must be excluded from a prospective cohort study, as the study progresses from cause to effect. The study begins before the disease under study has occurred.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Basic Definitions in Infectious Disease Epidemi...
mcqs.question: What is the host in which a parasite passes through its sexual stages of maturity called?
mcqs.explanation: A host in which a parasite passes through its sexual stage of maturity is called the definitive host or primary host. A host in which a parasite exists in the larval or asexual form is called an intermediate host or secondary host. A host which acts as the only source of development for a parasite is called the obligate host. Note: A host in which the organism remains alive but no development occurs is called a transport host.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is false about herd immunity?

options.a: It refers to group protection beyond what is afforded by the protection of immunized individuals
options.b: Vaccination allows the possibility of 100% herd immunity against a disease
options.c: It is affected by presence and distribution of alternative animal hosts
options.d: It doesn't protect the individual in the case of tetanus

mcqs.explanation: It is not possible to achieve 100% herd immunity against a certain disease but studies have shown this is not necessary for disease control.154 Herd structure is never constant. It is subject to constant variation because of new births, deaths and population mobility. An ongoing immunization programme will keep up the herd immunity at a very high level.

mcqs.question: You are preparing to administer the BCG vaccine to a newborn at a PHC. Before administering the vaccine, you check the vaccine vial monitor. In which of the following observations on the VVM, will you discard the vaccine?

mcqs.question: According to IMNCI, a 6-month-old child is said to have pneumonia if the child has fast breathing with a respiratory rate more than:
mcqs.explanation: Three key clinical signs are used to assess a sick child with cough or difficult breathing: • Respiratory rate (RR): distinguishes children who have pneumonia from those who do not. Children are classified as pneumonia if: • > 50/min RR for infants 2 months to 12 months • > 40/min RR for children 12 months to 5 years o f age • Lower chest wall indrawing indicates severe pneumonia • Stridor indicates those with severe pneumonia requiring hospital admission. mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: A 5-year-old boy has had 15 episodes of loose stools in the last 24 hours and vomited twice in the last 4 hours. The child is restless and has sunken eyes. On examination, he is irritable but is drinking fluids. What is the optimal therapy for the child?

options.c: Intravenous fluid initially for 4 hours followed by oral fluids

mcqs.explanation: Oral rehydration therapy is the optimal therapy to treat acute diarrheas in some dehydration patients. Recommended formulation: Reduced osmolarity ORS solution, which has a reduced concentration of sodium (75 mmol/liter) and glucose (75 mmol/liter). It helps in reducing the adverse effect of hype rtonicity o n net fluid absorption. According to IMNCI guidelines, irritable child who is able to drink fluids come under some dehydration category.

mcqs.question: What is the dose of diethylcarbamazine for the treatment of Bancroftian filariasis?
mcqs.explanation: The dose of diethylcarbamazine (DEC) for treatment of Bancroftian filariasis is 6 mg/kg/day orally for 12 days. Medicated common salt with 1-4g DEC/kg is a special form of mass treatment, particularly in endemic areas. By this method, very low doses of DEC are given over a long period of time.278

mcqs.question: In individuals exposed to HIV , within how many hours should prophylaxis be initiated?
mcqs.explanation: Post-exposure prophylaxis for HIV should ideally be initiated within 72 hours. It is recommended that it be started as even as early as < 2 hours.311

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a barrier method of contraception?
mcqs.explanation: Lippes loop is an intrauterine device and not a barrier method of contraception. Barrier methods of contraception include: • Physical methods – male and female condoms, d iaphragm, vaginal sponge (Today) • Chemical methods – foam tablets, aerosols, creams, jellies, suppositories, and soluble films (C-films)

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: In a given population, there were 5100 births during the year 2020. Of these, 100 babies were stillborn. Among the living children, the following deaths were recorded. Calculate the infant mortality rate for this population.
mcqs.explanation: The infant mortality rate (IMR) for this population is 100 / 1000 live births. IMR = No. of deaths within 1st year of life over a period of time x 1000 / No. of live births in the same period In this population, there were 5000 live births (5100 – 100) and 500 deaths within the 1st year of life. Hence, IMR = 500 x 1000/5000 = 100 per 1000 live births

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a lower-pressure membrane process for treatment of water?
mcqs.explanation: Microfiltration is a lower-pressure membrane process used for the treatment of water. Membrane processes are employed in the large scale treatment of water. They are classified as high-pressure processes and lower-pressure processes. • High-pressure processes: • R everse osmosis - Rejects monovalent ions and organic molecules of molecular weight > daltons. It is most commonly used for desalination of brackish water and sea water. The membrane pore size is < 0.002 \265 m. • Nanofiltration - Allows monovalent ions such as sodium or potassium to pass but rejects a high proportion of divalent ions like calcium and magnesium and some higher molecular weight organics. The membrane pore size ranges from 0.001 – 0.01 \265m. • Lo wer-pressure p rocesses : • Ultrafiltration - Rejects organic molecules of molecular weight > 800 daltons. The membrane pore size ranges from 0.002 - 0.003 \265 m. • Microfiltration - Rejects colloidal and suspended material. It does not separate molecules and is usually used before reverse osmosis. The membrane pore size ranges from 0.01 – 12 \265m.554

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.question: What sweat excretion rate in acclimatized, healthy young men is indicative of intolerable air temperature?
mcqs.explanation: A sweat excretion rate of > 4.5 L /4 hours in acclimatized, healthy young men is indicative of intolerable air temperature. This is known as McArdle's maximum allowable sweat rate. This is the maximum allowable sweat rate that is compatible with the normal physiological reaction of acclimatized, healthy young men who are exposed to heat. The predicted four-hour sweat rate (P4SR) is obtained from readings of air and mean radiant temperature and air velocity under different work intensities. Based on this value, the zone of comfort can be determined.Zone of comf ort PredictedP4 SR Comfort zone 1 – 3 litres Just tolerable 3 – 4.5 litres Intolerable 4.5 + litres

mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics II - Measures of Location
mcqs.question: You are conducting an epidemiological study on malaria in a town X. The number of cases reported during the last 10 years is given below. What is the most appropriate measure of central tendency for this data?
mcqs.explanation: In this scenario, median is the preferred measure of central tendency as there are outliers. The value of 5000 is an outlier in the given set, i.e., an observed value which is very distant from other observations in the distribution. This indicates the usage of median as the measure of central tendency a s it is not sensitive to extreme values, unlike the mean. By arranging the data in order: 100, 160, 190, 250, 260, 300, 320, 320, 350, 5000, we get the median as (260 + 300) / 2 = 280. Options A and B: Mean is the most affected by the presence of outliers. Mode is the least affected by outliers but it is used mainly for measuring the central tendency of nominal data. Option D: Geometric mean can be used for datasets with extreme values but it is not used when the values can be zero or n egative. In the given scenario, the number of malaria cases reported in a town can also have a zero value.

mcqs.subject: PSM
mcqs.chapter: Descriptive Statistics IV - Measures of Position
mcqs.question: During a school health camp, a group of 250 students are arranged in the ascending order of their height. Which student would have the 40th percentile value for height?
mcqs.explanation: Here, the 100th student will have the 40th percentile value for height. To arrive at this, we use the formula R = P/100 x (n + 1). where R is the rank of the desired observation, P is the quantile/percentile desired and n is the number of variables in the data. Thus, R = 40/100 x (250 + 1) = 0.4 x 251 = 100.4. This is rounded up to the closest number making R = 100.

mcqs.explanation: The change described in the question is called metaplasia . It is defined as a reversible change in which one type of differentiated cell is replaced by another type . mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: The following finding was noted on the cardiac tissue specimen of an 82-year-old man. Which of the following is false about the given finding?

options.a: It is a tell -tale sign of free radical injury
options.b: It is injurious to the cell and its function
options.c: It is derived through lipid peroxidation
options.d: It can also be seen in liver of aging patients

mcqs.explanation: The given histopathological image shows yellow -brown lipochrome or lipofuscin pigment . It is not injurious to the cell or its functions.53 Lipofuscin is a wear-and-tear pigment derived from the peroxidation of lipids of subcellular membranes. It is an indicator of free radical injury to the cells . It is an insoluble , brownish yellow , granular intracellular material that is seen in the liver, brain , and heart due to normal aging. The brown pigment in large amounts can give a characteristic appearance to the tissue called brown atrophy. It can also be seen in patients with severe malnutrition and cancer cachexia.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A pathologist is examining a liver biopsy specimen from a patient with liver disease . The following finding is noted . Which of the following is the most likely cause of this finding?
mcqs.explanation: The given histopathological image shows hepatic macro-vesicular steatosis along with intraparenchymal cholestasis , which is suggestive of fatty liver. This condition can occur due to alcoholism. The lipid accumulates in the hepatocytes as vacuoles. These vacuoles have a clear appearance on hematoxylin and eosin staining.54 A few causes of fatty liver are as follows : • Alcoholism - most common cause in developed countries • Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) - associated with diabetes and obesity • Toxins • Malnutrition • Dyslipidemia • Anoxia Fatty change is mostly seen in the liver because it is the major organ involved in fat metabolism. It may also occur in the heart, muscles , and kidneys. The most common form of lipid accumulation is triglycerides . Other forms of lipid that can be accumulated include cholesterol , cholesterol esters , and phospholipids .55

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old male patient presented with backache. Urine examination revealed nephrotic range proteinuria with Bence-Jones proteins. Laboratory reports showed hypercalcemia . Histopathological examination of the bone marrow aspirate showed the findings as given below . The findings seen on histopathology are due to the accumulation of:
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and the histopathological image showing Russell bodies are suggestive of multiple myeloma. These are globular, eosinophilic intracellular accumulations of immunoglobulins.56

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: An elderly man diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the lung underwent surgical resection . Histopathological examination of the resected hilar lymph nodes revealed the following finding as given below . Which of the following is the most likely cause for this?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario and histopathological image of the lymph node showing abundant black-colored pigment within the macrophages are characteristic of pulmonary anthracosis. The black color is due to the deposition of carbon particles . The inhaled carbon particles are engulfed by the lung macrophages and then transported to the hilar lymph nodes , which causes the blackening of the tissues . The carbon dust may also induce fibroblastic reaction or emphysema that may lead to a condition called coal worker's pneumoconiosis . It is commonly seen in people who work in environments where there is high air pollution with carbon particles , such as coal mines.58 The following images show the accumulation of various types of pigments within cells .59

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which molecule plays a major role in the following phenomenon seen in leukocytes ?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows diapedesis by leukocytes . CD31 or platelet endothelial cell adhesion molecule (PECAM-1) plays a major role in diapedesis . Diapedesis or transmigration refers to the migration of the leukocytes through the endothelium . It mainly occurs in postcapillary venules.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: What does the following image show?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows the phenomenon of emperipolesis . Here, intact hematopoietic cells are seen within the cytoplasm of the host cell without any damage . The cells frequently involved are neutrophils, lymphocytes , and plasma cells . Both the cells are viable and there are no physiological and morphological consequences to either of them.84

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Lymph node biopsy of a patient with tuberculosis demonstrated the following findings. From which of the following are these cells derived?
mcqs.explanation: The given histopathological findings in a patient with tuberculosis are suggestive of granulomatous inflammation, with epithelioid and multinucleated giant cells . These cells are derived from the monocyte -macrophage lineage .106 Macrophages activated by IFN-\034 develop into cells with abundant cytoplasm . They resemble epithelial cells and are thus called epithelioid cells . Some activated macrophages may fuse , forming multinucleated giant cells . Collections of activated macrophages , often with T lymphocytes are seen in granulomatous inflammation. Sometimes it is associated with central caseating necrosis. Granulomas may be formed in response to various stimuli: • Immune granulomas - due to T-cell mediated response ; macrophages activate T cells to produce cytokines, such as IL -2 and IFN-\034 • Foreign body granulomas - due to inert foreign bodies in the absence of a T-cell mediated response

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A pathologist observes the given findings during the examination of a lymph node sample . Which of the following is the least likely cause ?
mcqs.explanation: The given histopathological image of a lymph node shows a non-caseating granuloma. Tuberculosis is least likely as it is commonly associated with caseating granulomas. Non-caseating granulomas can be seen in the following conditions: • Leprosy • Cat-scratch disease • Sarcoidosis • Berylliosis • Crohn's disease • Hypersenitive pneumonitis • Foreign body granuloma • Q fever • Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Wegener's). • Hodgkin's lymphoma

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old man comes with the following findings. He says that he cut himself while shaving 3 months back. What is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The history of a shaving cut and the image showing a large area of scar tissue are suggestive of a keloid . A keloid refers to excess accumulation of collagen at the scar site with growth of the scar tissue beyond the boundaries of the original wound . It does not regress . Option A: Exuberant granulation or proud flesh refers to the protrusion of excessive amounts of granulation tissue above the level of the surrounding skin. This blocks re-epithelialization . Option B: The accumulation of excessive amounts of collagen may give rise to a raised scar known as a hypertrophic scar. However, it remains within the boundaries of the original scar. Option D: Pyogenic granuloma is a benign, vascular tumor.119

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A patient presented to the OPD with the following finding on her finger. She says that she cut her finger while chopping vegetables 2 weeks ago. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario and clinical findings are suggestive of exuberant granulation. It is a deviation in wound healing where excessive amounts of granulation tissue protrude above the level of the surrounding skin and blocks re-epithelialization . It is also known as proud flesh .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A patient presented with the following finding. Which of the following can cause this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The finding seen in the given image is pitting edema . Edema can be caused by elevated hydrostatic pressure and reduced colloid osmotic pressure . Under normal circumstances , there is little net movement of fluid out of vessels due to the balance of: • Vascular hydrostatic pressure which has the tendency to push water and salts out of capillaries into the interstitial space • Plasma osmotic pressure or colloid oncotic pressure which has a tendency to pull water and salts back into vessels . The pressure dynamics seen inside a capillary is given below .Atarterial end Atvenous end Capillary hydrostatic pressur e = 30-35 mmHg Capillary hydrostatic pressur e = 15-20 mmHg Osmotic Pressure = 25 mmH g Osmotic Pressure = 25 mmH g Hydrostatic Pressure > Osmo tic Pressure \035Fluid moves o utof the capillary Hydrostatic Pressure < Osmo tic Pressure \035Fluid moves in to the capillary128 Many pathologic disorders are associated with an increase in capillary hydrostatic pressure or a decrease in plasma osmotic pressure , which lead to edema .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Following autopsy , an H&E stained specimen of the lung was obtained which is given below . What could be the likely cause of death ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows the presence of laminated swirls of squamous cells in the pulmonary arteriole which is characteristically seen in amniotic fluid embolism(AFE).137 AFE is a life -threatening obstetric emergency characterized by sudden cardiorespiratory collapse and disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). The underlying cause is the infusion of amniotic fluid or fetal tissue into the maternal circulation via a tear in the placental membranes or rupture of uterine veins. Findings at autopsy include : • Presence in the maternal pulmonary micro-vasculature of- • Squamous cells shed from fetal skin • Lanugo hair • Fat from vernix caseosa • Mucin derived from the fetal respiratory or gastrointestinal tract • Marked pulmonary edema • Diffuse alveolar damage • Presence of fibrin thrombi in many vascular beds due to DIC

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old man is being evaluated for weakness and atrophy of distal limb musculature . Physical examination showing characteristic facies is given below . What is the mode of inheritance of this disease ?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario and image showing the characteristic hatchet facies are suggestive of myotonic dystrophy (dystonia myotrophica). It is an autosomal dominant genetic disorder affecting muscle function. There are mainly two types : • DM1 - In this type , the affected gene is DMPK, which codes for myotonic dystrophy protein kinase, a protein expressed predominantly in skeletal muscle . The gene is located on the long arm of chromosome 19.156 • DM2 - It is caused by a defect of the CNBP gene on chromosome 3.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: How many base pairs the human genome is made of?
mcqs.explanation: The human genome is the complete set of nucleic acid sequences for humans and is made up of 3.2 billion base pairs. It is encoded as DNA within the 23 chromosomes (haploid ). In 2007, a multinational project called Encyclopedia of DNA Elements (ENCODE ) concluded that about 80% of the human genome does not code for the proteins . However, they allow for the binding of proteins or are involved in the regulation of gene expression , in a cell type -specific fashion. They are known as functional non-protein-coding genes .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 34-year-old woman is undergoing evaluation for premature cataracts, thinning of skin, alopecia , osteoporosis , and atherosclerosis . She is found to have a hereditary genetic mutation in the WRN gene . This gene encodes which of the following proteins ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical features are suggestive of Werner syndrome, a premature aging disorder. The mutated gene encodes a DNA helicase . Werner syndrome is an autosomal recessive disease caused by mutations in the WRN gene . This gene encodes a protein with multiple DNA-dependent enzymatic functions including: • ATPase • Helicase • Exonuclease DNA helicase is involved in DNA replication and repair. A defect in this enzyme causes rapid accumulation of damaged chromosomes that may mimic the injury that normally accumulates during cellular aging. Affected persons show various manifestations of premature aging including: • Atherosclerosis • Senile cataract • Skin atrophy • Alopecia • Osteoporosis They are also at risk for the development of a variety of cancers. Patients typically die in the 5th decade from either cancer or cardiovascular disease .67

options.a: It is a non-inflammatory edema or effusion
options.b: It is a protein-poor and cell -poor fluid
options.c: It has a specific gravity of less than 1.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: What is the most common cause of death in Marfan syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: Cardiovascular lesions , like rupture of aortic dissections , are the most life -threatening features of the Marfan syndrome. The weakening of the media predisposes the aorta to an intimal tear. It may initiate an intramural hematoma that cleaves the layers of the media to produce aortic dissection . After causing the cleavage of the aortic layers for a considerable length , sometimes extending to the root of the aorta or down to the iliac arteries, the hemorrhage often ruptures through the aortic wall. Although mitral valve lesions are more frequent, they are clinically less important than aortic lesions. Loss of connective tissue support in the mitral valve leaflets makes them soft and billowy , creating a so-called floppy valve.162 Valvular lesions , along with the lengthening of the chordae tendineae , frequently give rise to mitral regurgitation. Similar changes may affect the tricuspid and, rarely, the aortic valves.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman presents with complaints of post -coital bleeding . On per speculum examination , a friable mass is seen and a punch biopsy is done. The presence of which of the following features in microscopic examination of biopsy specimen differentiates invasive carcinoma from carcinoma in situ?
mcqs.explanation: Once the tumor cells breach the basement membrane, the tumor is said to be invasive . Progression of cancer occurs in the following stages : dysplasia \035carcinoma in situ\035invasive carcinoma In situ carcinoma is when dysplastic changes are marked and involve the full thickness of the epithelium , but the lesion does not penetrate the basement membrane. It is a pre-invasive neoplasm . The tumor is said to be invasive when the basement membrane is breached by the tumor cells .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Molecular Basis of Cancer and Tumor Immunity
mcqs.question: Which of the following disorders is not associated with defective homologous recombination DNA repair mechanism?
mcqs.explanation: Fanconi syndrome is not associated with defective homologous recombination DNA repair mechanism. It is a rare disorder of kidney tubule function. Diseases with defects in DNA repair by homologous recombination: • Bloom syndrome and ataxia–telangiectasia triggered by DNA-damaging agents such as ionizing radiation • Fanconi anemia is an autosomal recessive disease caused by mutations in multiple genes responsible for coding for proteins that participate in DNA repair pathways and are triggered by DNA-crosslinking agents like chemotherapeutic drugs. • Familial breast cancer is due to inherited gene defects in BRCA1 and BRCA 2 genes

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 51-year-old male patient who is a chronic smoker presents with dry persistent cough and progressive dyspnea . You are suspecting small cell carcinoma of lung. Which of the following tumor markers is likely to be elevated in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of small cell carcinoma of the lung (SCLC) in which levels of neuron-specific enolase (NSE) are elevated . NSE is also called gamma enolase or enolase 2 (ENO2) and is encoded by ENO2 gene . It is a phosphopyruvate hydratase that is produced by small-cell lung carcinomas, which are neuroendocrine in origin. Their levels have been implicated as a prognostic factor for patients with small-cell lung cancer.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is responsible for autoimmunity in Epstein -Barr virus infection ?
mcqs.explanation: Autoimmunity in Epstein –Barr virus (EBV) infection is the result of polyclonal B cell activation. Microbes may induce other abnormalities that promote autoimmune reactions. Some viruses, such as EBV and HIV , cause polyclonal B-cell activation, which may result in the production of autoantibodies . The role of infections in autoimmunity is exemplified by the following : • Molecular mimicry of antigenic cross-reactivity: The structural similarity of the microbial antigens and self -antigens. Rheumatic heart disease is an example in which streptococcal proteins cross-react with myocardial proteins causing myocarditis. • Upregulation of co-stimulatory molecules by infectious organisms. • Polyclonal B cell activation: Caused by EBV and HIV , resulting in the production of autoantibodies . • Alteration of tissue antigens: Infections may alter tissue self -antigens so that they activate T cells and lose the property of self -tolerance .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: In lardaceous spleen , deposition of amyloid occurs in which of the following sites ?
mcqs.explanation: Lardaceous spleen is due to the deposition of amyloid in sinusoids of the red pulp . Sago spleen is due to the deposition of amyloid in splenic follicles (white pulp ).

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 53-year-old woman presents with complaints of light -headedness every time she stands up. She is a known case of rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate . On examination, she has pallor and brittle nails. Which of the following statements is true regarding her condition?

options.a: Serum iron and tissue iron levels are normal
options.b: Anemia can be normocytic and normochromic

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of anaemia of chronic diseases (ACD). In this condition, the anaemia initially can be normocytic normochromic . ACD occurs in the setting of persistent systemic inflammation. It is associated with • Low serum iron • Reduced total iron-binding capacity • Abundant stored iron in tissue macrophages352 Inflammatory mediators like IL -6 stimulate an increase in the production of hepcidin . This inhibits ferroportin function in the macrophages and reduces the transfer of iron from the storage pool to developing erythroid precursors in the marrow . As a result , erythroid precursors are starved for iron despite the availability of plenty of iron in tissue macrophages .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following features would you least expect to see in a patient with hereditary spherocytosis ?
mcqs.explanation: Hemoglobinuria is not seen in hereditary spherocytosis where extravascular hemolysis occurs. It is a feature of intravascular hemolysis . Pigment gallstones , pallor and splenomegaly can be seen in this condition. Cinical features of extravascular hemolysis include : • Anaemia • Jaundice • Splenomegaly Causes of extravascular hemolysis : • Hereditary spherocytosis • Thalassemia • Sickle cell anaemia Note : G6PD deficiency and autoimmune hemolytic anaemia can cause both intravascular and extravascular hemolysis .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A patient with large platelets on peripheral smear is diagnosed to have Bernard -Soulier disease . Deficiency of which of the following causes this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Bernard –Soulier disease is due to deficiency of Gp Ib/ IX. Bernard –Soulier syndrome is characterized by large platelets . Ristocetin aggregation is abnormal . Factor VIII deficiency causes hemophilia .Deficiency Defect Disease Gp Ib/IX Adhesion of platelets Bernard –Soulier syndro me Gp IIb /IIIa Aggregation of platelets Glanzmann thrombasth enia von Willebrand fact or Adhesion>Aggregation Von Willebrand disease423

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following can be used to store blood for up to 35 days?
mcqs.explanation: Citrate dextrose phosphate adenine-1 (CDPA-1) can be used to store blood for up to 35 days. It helps in improving ATP synthesis during storage . Hence , it increases the shelf life .449 The disadvantage of using CDPA-1 is that it increases uric acid stone formation. The shelf life of storage with other components are: • Acid Citrate dextrose – 21 days • Citrate-phosphate dextrose – 21 days

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Increased levels of serum muramidase are seen in patients with which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Serum muramidase or lysozyme levels are seen to be increased in patients with acute myelomonocytic leukemia (AML - M4). It is also increased in chronic myelomonocytic leukemia and chronic myeloid leukemia (CML).

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 53-year-old man was evaluated for painless lymphadenopathy . Biopsy showed a homogenous population of small lymphocytes with cleaved nuclear contours. Which translocation is seen in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical picture and pathological findings point toward the diagnosis of mantle cell lymphoma. The lymph node biopsy typically shows proliferation consisting of a homogenous population of small lymphocytes . The nuclei of these cells have irregular or deeply cleaved contours. Mantle cell lymphoma has(11 ;14) translocation involving the IgH locus on chromosome 14 and the cyclin D1 locus on chromosome 11 that leads to overexpression of cyclin D1. Option A: Follicular lymphoma has t(14:18), not t(18:14). Hence , it is not the answer.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.chapter: Multiple Myeloma and Plasma Cell Disorders
mcqs.question: What do Bence Jones proteins in the urine of multiple myeloma patients represent ?
mcqs.explanation: Bence Jones proteins are immunoglobulin light chains (paraproteins) produced by neoplastic plasma cells. They can be kappa (most of the time) or lambda. The light chains can be immunoglobulin fragments or single homogeneous immunoglobulins . In patients with plasma cell tumors, the level of free light chains is usually elevated . One of the light chains is elevated with a reduction in the other. Free light chains are excreted in the urine because they are small in size, where they are referred to as Bence Jones proteins . Tests for Bence Jones protein are: • Heat test • Urine protein electrophoresis • Immunofixation

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not compatible with a diagnosis of chronic myelomonocytic leukemia?

options.c: More than 20 % blasts in blood or bone marrow
options.d: Absent or minimal dysplasia in myeloid lineages

mcqs.explanation: More than 20 % of blasts in the blood or bone marrow are not compatible with a diagnosis of chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML). In this condition, blasts are less than 20 %. WHO 5th edition diagnostic criteria (2022 _for chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML) include : Prerequisite criteria: • 1. Persistent absolute (\0300.5 \327 109 / L) and relative (\03010%) peripheral blood monocytosis . • 2. Blasts constitute <20% of the cells in the peripheral blood and bone marrow .598 • 3. Not meeting diagnostic criteria of chronic myeloid leukemia or other myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN).b • 4. Not meeting diagnostic criteria of myeloid /lymphoid neoplasms with tyrosine kinase fusions.c Supporting criteria: • 1. Dysplasia involving \0301 myeloid lineage .d • 2. Acquired clonal cytogenetic or molecular abnormality. • 3. Abnormal partitioning of peripheral blood monocyte subsets .e Pre-requisite criteria must be present in all cases : • If monocytosis is \030 1 \327 109 / L: one or more supporting criteria must be met. • If monocytosis is \0300.5 and <1 \327 109/ L: supporting criteria 1 and 2 must be met. Subtype criteria: • Myelodysplastic CMML (MD-CMML): WBC < \327 109 /L • Myeloproliferative CMML (MP-CMML): WBC \030 \327 109 /L a. Blasts and blast equivalents include myeloblasts , monoblasts, and promonocytes . b. MPN with monocytosis can mimic CMML. In these instances, a documented history of MPN excludes CMML. The presence of MPN features in the bone marrow and/or a high burden of MPN-associated mutations (JAK2, CALR , or MPL) tends to support MPN with monocytosis rather than CMML. c. Criteria for myeloid /lymphoid neoplasms with tyrosine kinase fusions should be specifically excluded in cases with eosinophilia . d. Morphologic dysplasia should be present in \03010 % of cells of a hematopoietic lineage in the bone marrow. e. Based on the detection of increased classical monocytes (>94%) in the absence of known active autoimmune diseases and/or systemic inflammatory syndromes.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following myocardial infarcts cause aneurysm as a post -MI complication?
mcqs.explanation: Anterior transmural infarcts are involved in causing aneurysm as a post -MI complication. Posterior transmural infarcts are more likely to be complicated by conduction blocks, right ventricular involvement, or both.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following vascular lesions are commonly seen in patients with Turner syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: 685 The vascular lesions commonly seen in Turner syndrome are cavernous lymphangiomas of the neck. Cavernous lymphangiomas (cystic hygromas) are massively dilated lymphatic spaces lined by endothelial cells and separated by connective tissue stroma. They are typically found in the neck or axilla of children and rarely in the retroperitoneum . They can be enormous causing gross deformities around the neck. Image shows cavernous lymphangioma of the neck associated with a girl having Turner syndrome:

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: What is the most common mechanism behind sudden cardiac death ?
mcqs.explanation: The mechanism behind sudden cardiac death (SCD) is most often a lethal arrhythmia , e.g., asystole or ventricular fibrillation. Coronary artery disease is the leading cause of SCD, responsible for 80% to 90% of cases . But, the mechanism of SCD is most often a lethal arrhythmia . Infarction need not occur. Most of the patients who have SCD but are successfully resuscitated do not show any enzymatic or ECG evidence of myocardial necrosis. Ischemic injury can directly affect the major components of the conduction system . But, most cases of fatal arrhythmia are triggered by electrical irritability of the myocardium.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 5-year-old child was brought to the OPD for evaluation of cognitive impairment. Parents report that the child is overly-friendly with strangers. On examination, elfin facies and hypotonia are noted . Investigations reveal hypercalcemia . Which of the following cardiac defects is associated with this syndrome?
mcqs.explanation: The given features are suggestive of Williams (Williams–Beuren) syndrome. It is associated with supravalvular aortic stenosis . This condition is due to deletions on chromosome 7 which includes the gene for elastin . These mutations may cause supravalvular stenosis by disrupting elastin –smooth muscle cell interactions during aortic morphogenesis . There is thickening of ascending aortic wall and consequent luminal constriction. Other features of the syndrome include : • Elfin facies - wide mouth, chubby cheeks , long philtrum, small nose, and delicate chin (as shown in the image)748 • Cognitive abnormalities • Intellectual disability (usually mild) • Personality changes - over-friendliness to strangers • Hypotonia • Connective tissue abnormalities • Endocrine abnormalities (hypercalcemia, hypercalciuria, hypothyroidism , early puberty )

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 27-year-old woman presents with urinary frequency, urgency , and burning during urination of two days duration. Presence of which of the following additional findings would make you suspect pyelonephritis in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: White blood cell casts are specific features of pyelonephritis . Neutrophil -rich casts (pus casts) indicate renal involvement because casts are formed only in tubules . The urine contains many leukocytes (pyuria) derived from the inflammatory infiltrate. It is found in both upper and lower UTIs and cannot differentiate between them. Fever is also a non-specific finding. Ascending infection is the most common cause of clinical pyelonephritis . Note : Sterile pyuria is defined as white cells in the urine in the absence of significant bacterial growth. It is seen in renal TB .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding renal cell carcinoma ?

options.a: It can invade the renal vein
options.c: It may arise from the proximal convoluted tubule

mcqs.explanation: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is more common among males, with a male to female ratio of 2:1. Renal cell carcinoma may arise from the proximal convoluted tubules (PCT). The classical clinical features of renal cell carcinoma are costovertebral pain, palpable mass, and painless hematuria. It characteristically invades the renal vein and has a high tendency for distant metastasis . Paraneoplastic manifestations of renal cell carcinoma include : • Polycythemia • Hypercalcemia • Hypertension • Hepatic dysfunction841 • Feminization or masculinization • Cushing syndrome • Eosinophilia • Leukemoid reactions • Amyloidosis

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: The biopsy of a resected inguinal mass from a patient shows marked fibrotic changes with prominent Leydig cells and hypoplastic Sertoli cells . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given histopathological features are strongly suggestive of cryptorchidism. Cryptorchidism is histopathologically characterized by the following : • Testicular atrophy: thickening of the basement membrane, arrested germ cell development , marked hyalinization • Tubules showing Sertoli cells but no spermatogenesis • Increase in the interstitial Leydig cells. Cryptorchidism is the failure of the descent of the intra-abdominal testes into the scrotal sac. It is the most common congenital abnormality of the genitourinary tract. The testes can arrest anywhere during descent , and the most common site is the inguinal region. Phases of testicular descent : • Transabdominal phase : Testes come to lie in the lower abdomen or pelvis. This phase of descent is regulated by Mullerian-inhibiting substances . • Inguinoscrotal phase : Testes descend along the inguinal canal and reach the scrotal sac. This phase of the descent is regulated by androgen-induced calcitonin gene -related peptide from the890 genitofemoral nerve. The exact pathogenesis remains unknown, however, deficiency in gonadotropins and Mullerian-inhibiting substance (MIS) and increased expression of estradiol in the placenta are thought to play a role. It is associated with testicular atrophy and dysfunction , which result in sterility . Cryptorchid testes carry a 3–5-fold higher risk for testicular cancer (usually seminoma).

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following causes Laennec cirrhosis?
mcqs.explanation: Laennec cirrhosis is the classic micronodular cirrhosis seen in end-stage alcoholic liver disease . There are three distinctive , overlapping forms of alcoholic liver injury: • Hepatic steatosis (fatty liver) • Fatty change - completely reversible if there is abstention from further intake of alcohol • Starts in centrilobular area • Alcoholic (steato ) hepatitis • Ballooning degeneration and necrosis • Mallory–Denk bodies924 • Neutrophilic reaction • Alcoholic steatofibrosis • Perisinusoidal fibrosis and sclerosis of the central vein • Diffuse nodularity of liver surface • Micronodular/ Laennec cirrhosis • Irreversible

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following organs does not show hemosiderin deposits in hemochromatosis?
mcqs.explanation: The testes do not show hemosiderin deposits in hemochromatosis. Hypogonadism in hemochromatosis is not due to the deposition of iron in the testis . It is due to a derangement in the hypothalamic -pituitary axis. This results in decreased gonadotrophins and testosterone levels . The testis will appear small and atrophic. Deposition of hemosiderin is seen in the following organs in the decreasing order of severity : • Liver • Pancreas • Myocardium947 • Pituitary gland • Adrenal gland • Thyroid • Parathyroid gland • Joints • Skin

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: All of these are characteristic features of pancreatic carcinoma except :

options.a: Cigarette smoking is a risk factor
options.b: Carcinoma of body of pancreas often present with jaundice

mcqs.explanation: Patients with carcinoma of the head of the pancreas develop jaundice due to obstruction of the biliary tract. Cigarette smoking doubles the risk of pancreatic cancer and is the leading preventable cause . The clinical features depend on the location of the tumor. • Head - painless , palpable gallbladder with mild jaundice is suggestive of malignancy (according to Courvoisier's law)975 • Body and tail - may remain asymptomatic until later stages as they do not impinge on the biliary tract and do not cause jaundice Other common pathological features of this condition are: • Desmoplastic reaction - growth of fibrous or connective tissue • Perineural invasion , as well as lymphatic and large vessel invasion

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: What is the most common translocation seen in patients with gastric MALToma ?
mcqs.explanation: The most common translocation in gastric MALToma is t(11;18)(q21 ;q21 ). Three translocations are associated with gastric MALToma : • t(11;18)(q21 ;q21 ) - Most common • t(1;14)(p22 ;q32 ) • t(14;18)(q32 ;q21 )

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following patients is at an increased risk of developing malignancy?

options.d: A 40-year-old man with sessile serrated polyps

mcqs.explanation: Patients with sessile serrated polyps are at an increased risk of developing malignancy. Histologically , sessile serrated polyps appear like hyperplastic polyps , but a serrated architecture throughout the full length of the glands and lateral growth is the differentiating feature . They lack cytological features of dysplasia .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: What is the most common gene mutation associated with pulmonary hypertension ?
mcqs.explanation: Bone morphogenetic protein receptor 2 (BMPR2 ) is the most common gene mutation in pulmonary hypertension . Inactivating mutations in this gene are found in 75 % of the familial cases of pulmonary hypertension , and 25% of sporadic cases . The BMPR2 receptor is a cell surface protein belonging to the TGF-�o receptor superfamily . It is involved in the regulation of growth , differentiation , and apoptosis of pulmonary artery endothelial and smooth muscle cells . Due to the mutation, there is enhanced proliferation and reduced apoptosis of vascular endothelial and smooth muscle cells leading to pulmonary hypertension .

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about solitary thyroid nodule is incorrect?

options.a: They are more common in women
options.c: Solitary nodules are more likely to be malignant than are multiple nodules
options.d: Nodules in younger patients are less likely to be malignant

mcqs.explanation: Nodules in younger patients are more likely to be malignant than those in older patients . The solitary thyroid nodule is a palpably discrete swelling within an otherwise apparently normal thyroid gland. A higher incidence is seen in areas with endemic iodine deficiency . They are more common in women than in men. Malignant transformation is more common in: • Solitary nodules > Multinodular goiter • Solitary nodules in males > females • Cold nodules > Hot nodules However, benign neoplasms are more common than thyroid carcinomas by a ratio of nearly 10 :1.

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: What is the most common site of carcinoma in the breast?
mcqs.explanation: The upper outer quadrant is the most common site of carcinoma in the breast. Approximately 50% of carcinomas are located in the upper outer quadrant , % in each of the remaining quadrants, and about 20 % in the central or subareolar region. A palpable mass is the most common clinical sign of invasive breast carcinoma . Triple assessment is recommended for the diagnosis of any palpable breast lump. It includes : • Clinical examination • Radiological assessment (mammography/USG) • Pathological assessment (FNAC/biopsy ) Techniques of palpation for breast examination are: • Vertical strip/lines pattern • Circular pattern • Wedges or radial spokes pattern1198

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 19-year old man presents with back pain for 2 months. MRI of the spine reveals a bony cystic mass at the L1 vertebra. Biopsy shows multiple , blood-filled cystic spaces separated by septae , composed of multinucleated osteoclast -like giant cells and reactive woven bone. There is no cartilage or necrosis. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of an aneurysmal bone cyst . It affects all age groups , but generally occurs during the first 2 decades of life and has no sex predilection. It usually occurs in the metaphysis of long bones and the posterior elements of vertebral bodies . This is a tumor characterized by multiloculated blood-filled cystic spaces separated by septae , composed of multinucleated osteoclast -like giant cells and reactive woven bone. Radiographically, an aneurysmal bone cyst is seen as an eccentric , expansile , lesion with well -defined margins. Most lesions are completely lytic and often contain a thin shell of reactive bone at the periphery . The spindle cells of aneurysmal bone cyst frequently demonstrate rearrangements of chromosome 17p13, leading to USP6 overexpression. The majority of secondary aneurysmal bone cysts arise in association with: • Benign neoplasms • Giant-cell tumor of the bone (most common) • Chondroblastoma • Osteoblastoma • Fibrous dysplasia • Osteosarcoma

mcqs.subject: Pathology
mcqs.question: A 62-year-old man is brought with tremors of his hands at rest. His son says that he has difficulty initiating movements and seems to be moving very slowly . On examination, shuffling gait, pill-rolling tremors, and rigidity on passive arm movement are noted . Which of the following is not seen in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: This clinical scenario is suggestive of Parkinson 's disease . This condition is not associated with Pick cells and Pick bodies . They are seen in Pick's disease or frontotemporal dementia . In Parkinson 's disease , there is loss of the substantia nigra neurons projecting to the striatum. This leads to pallor of the substantia nigra as well as a decrease or absence of dopamine in the striatum. This leads to slowing of movements and tremors. Lewy Bodies are seen within the neurons of affected patients . They are filamentous projections of the protein \037\037synuclein or ubiquitin. They are present in surviving neurons and can be found in the cortex.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Basics of Neonatology and Routine Newborn Care
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old primigravida delivers a preterm baby at 33 weeks of gestation with a birth weight of 2 kg. She is advised to hold her child as shown below . Which of the following statements about this method is false ?

options.b: Safety and thermal protection is equivalent to incubators
options.c: Reduces severe morbidity in the newborns
options.d: Should be performed only by the mother

mcqs.explanation: Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC ) can be carried out by the mother or any other caregiver. KMC was introduced for the prevention of neonatal hypothermia in low birth weight / premature newborns. It has 4 components — • Skin -to-skin positioning of the newborn on the mother's chest . • Adequate nutrition through breastfeeding . • Early discharge and ambulatory care. • Support for mother and family for child care. Evidence shows that- • It is as good as incubators, in terms of safety and thermal protection (measured by mortality) • Reduces severe morbidity by way of facilitating breastfeeding • Humanization of neonatal care • Promoted bonding between mother and child Eligibility criteria for KMC : It is indicated for all hemodynamically stable low birth weight babies. Short sessions of KMC can be initiated in babies on medical treatment like IV fluids or oxygen therapy . Initiation of KMC can vary with the birth weight of the baby. • Birth weight <1200 g - It may take days to weeks for initiation of KMC • Birth weight =1200 -1800 g - Only a few days may be taken before KMC initiation13 • Birth weight >1800 g - KMC can be initiated immediately after birth All mothers without any serious illness can provide KMC . Positioning for KMC : The baby is placed between the mother's breast in an upright position. The hips are abducted and flexed in the frog position and the arms are also flexed . The abdomen of the baby should be at the level of the mother's epigastrium . In this position, the mother's breathing would stimulate the baby and prevent the development of apnea. The duration of KMC should be gradually increased from short sessions of more than one hour to 24 hours a day. KMC is not necessary once the baby attains 2500 g of weight or 37 weeks of gestation . Note : Incubatory care, feeding via nasal catheter , and prevention of infection are part of intensive care for low birthweight babies.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Basics of Neonatology and Routine Newborn Care
mcqs.question: You are demonstrating findings in a pediatric OSCE examination on a 4-day old neonate . On turning the baby's head to the left , you obtain the finding as shown below . At what age does this reflex normally disappear ?
mcqs.explanation: Asymmetric tonic neck reflex (ATNR ) disappears by 6 months postnatally . The tonic neck reflex is produced by manually rotating the infant's head to 1 side and observing for the characteristic fencing posture (extension of the arm on the side to which the face is rotated and flexion of the contralateral arm ).18 An obligatory tonic neck response , in which the infant becomes "stuck" in the fencing posture , is always abnormal and implies a CNS disorder.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Basics of Neonatology and Routine Newborn Care
mcqs.question: A first-time mother rushes to the OPD with her 4-day old infant and worriedly points to the rash that appears as shown below . You reassure her of its harmless, transient nature. On microscopic examination, these papular lesions on an erythematous base will reveal ________
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical complex describes a case of erythema neonatorum. Wright stained smear of the contents of the pustule will show an abundance of eosinophils . They are papular lesions on an erythematous base, distributed over the trunk and face predominantly. They are seen 1-3 days after birth and may persist for up to a week , after which they resolve spontaneously . Neutrophils are seen in pustular melanosis.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Basics of Neonatology and Routine Newborn Care
mcqs.question: A 5-month-old infant is brought to the OPD for a well -baby check-up. A lesion that was present since birth is noticed as given below . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The above image shows Mongolian spots or dermal melanocytosis . Mongolian spots are benign blue or slate -grey macular lesions , with clearly defined margins, that appear over the presacral region (most common), posterior thighs , legs , back, and forearms. These spots occur due to the presence of melanin-containing melanocytes in the dermis, which is arrested during the migration from neural crest cells to the epidermis . They are non-tender and do not rapidly change in color or size.19

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A male infant born at 34 weeks of gestation by emergency LSCS was found to have the following finding on histopathological examination of his umbilical cord. Anomalies of which of the following systems are most likely to be found in this infant?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows the presence of a single umbilical artery which is associated with an increased risk for an occult renal anomaly. The histopathological image of the cross-section of the umbilical cord shows 2 vessels as marked, a thin-walled umbilical vein and a thicker-walled umbilical artery.26 The normal umbilical cord contains 2 arteries and 1 vein. A single umbilical artery is the most common cord abnormality. Anomalies are seen in 30% of cases with a single umbilical artery. The incidence is higher in twin deliveries . Trisomy 18 is a common association.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a feature of marking B?

options.a: Swelling of the soft tissues of the scalp
options.d: Appears only several hours after birth

mcqs.explanation: The area marked B represents a cephalohematoma . It is not a swelling of the soft tissues of the scalp. Cephalohematoma is a subperiosteal hemorrhage that is always limited to the surface of 1 cranial bone and does not cross suture lines. The swelling appears only several hours after birth. There is no discoloration of the overlying scalp.30 Most cephalohematomas are resorbed within 2 weeks to 3 months, depending on their size. Cephalohematomas require no treatment , although phototherapy may be necessary to treat the associated hyperbilirubinemia (resorption of blood takes place by the breakdown of RBCs).Other markings - A- Caput succedaneum . It is a diffuse ecchymotic or edematous collection in the soft tissues of the scalp with vertex presentation . It can extend across skull sutures and disappears with the first week of life . C- Sub-galeal hemorrhage. This a collection of blood under the aponeurosis of the scalp . It is a large potential space , thus bleeding can be extensive . It occurs as a result of ventouse deliveries due to tears of the emissary veins which connect to the dural venous sinuses . It can also occur in hereditary coagulopathies and in association with skull fractures. D- Epidural hemorrhage. Usually traumatic in origin, these are associated with cephalo -pelvic disproportion, prolonged labor, breech, precipitous labors, or as a result of mechanical assistance in labor. Majority resolve with no intervention.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Diseases in Neonates requiring Special Care
mcqs.question: A neonate undergoing routine ophthalmological examination was found to have the finding shown below . Which among the following can be ruled out as the cause of this finding?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows leukokoria or white pupillary reflex . It is not seen in congenital glaucoma. Leukokoria is seen in: • Congenital cataract • Chorioretinitis • Retinoblastoma • Retinopathy of prematurity • Persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Diseases in Neonates requiring Special Care
mcqs.question: A 1.9 Kg neonate delivered at 32 weeks has abdominal distention and hematochezia on the 11th day of life . The abdomen x-ray is as shown below . What is the stage of disease according to Modified Bell's Staging Criteria?
mcqs.explanation: The above X-ray image shows gas accumulation in the submucosa of the bowel wall- pneumatosis intestinalis , a pathognomonic finding of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), seen in stage IIA , according to the Modified Bell Staging Criteria. mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Where would you attach the oxygen inlet in the instrument given below ?
mcqs.explanation: The above image shows a self -inflating bag and mask. It is used in neonatal resuscitation ; it inflates automatically, without a compressed gas source . • Marking 1 is the pressure release valve. • Marking 2 is the 360 -degree swivel. • Marking 3 is the oxygen inlet. • Marking 4 is the air inlet. The parts of the self -inflating bag and mask are labeled in the image below :62 Absolute contraindication for using the bag and mask ventilation is congenital diaphragmatic hernia

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: By what age is the milestone shown in the image typically attained ?
mcqs.explanation: The milestone shown in the image is a mature pincer grasp, which is seen at the age of 12 months. It is identified as a mature pincer grasp as the object is secured between the opposed thumb and the tip of the index finger. Developmental progression of the grasp: • At 6 months, the infant reaches and holds a larger object in a crude manner using the ulnar aspect of his hand (Ulnar palmar grasp). At 8-9 months, the object is grasped by the radial side of the palm (radial palmar grasp). • At 9 months, the immature pincer grasp develops . The object is secured between the adducted thumb and the extended index finger. • At 12 months, the mature pincer grasp develops . The object is secured between the opposed thumb and the tip of the index finger.75

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: In the image given below , the weight and height of a child are plotted against his age in years. Identify the correct statement .

options.a: WHO growth charts used now are developed by National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS).
options.b: Short stature is defined as a height below 5th percentile .
options.c: Puberty in this child will be normal .
options.d: Bone age of this child is less than chronological age .

mcqs.explanation: Bone age of this child is less than chronological age , as seen in cases of constitutional delay . As seen in the graph, the child was short initially, but the final height is within normal range. Hence , this child has constitutional delay . Other options : • The WHO growth charts are based on Multicentre Growth Reference Study (MGRS). National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) developed growth charts that were used in the past. • Short stature is defined as a height below the third percentile or more than 2 standard deviations below the median height for age and gender (<-2 SD) according to the population standard. • Puberty will be delayed in this child.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A mother brings her baby of 14 months to the clinic after being concerned about the shape of the baby's head . You are suspecting a case of craniosynostosis. The premature fusion of which of the following suture is seen in this child?
mcqs.explanation: The picture is suggestive of a child with left posterior plagiocephaly (as the left side of the head is flattened ) which involves the premature fusion of the left lambdoid suture . In the case of a left anterior plagiocephaly, the premature fusion of the left coronal suture is seen . Other deformities of the skull: Craniosynostosis consists of premature fusion of one or more cranial sutures , resulting in an abnormal head shape . • Primary craniosynostosis: It results from a primary defect of ossification. • Secondary craniosynostosis: It results from the failure of brain growth .Deformity Suture involved Anterior Plagiocephaly Respective side coronal sutur e Posterior Plagiocephaly Respective side lambdoid sut ure Deformation Plagiocepha ly Positional skull flattening (wi thout suture fusion) Brachycephaly Bilateral Coronal suture Trigonocephaly Metopic suture Scaphocephaly Saggital suture99

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Following the delivery of a healthy baby boy, his COVID positive mother slipped into ARDS and passed away. The relatives have arranged a breast milk donor and wish to feed the baby using the device shown in the image. In newborns of which gestational age , would you recommend this as a method of primary feeding ?
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows paladai. It can be used as a primary feeding method during routine feeding in neonates born at gestational age 32 -34 weeks only. Sick mothers or mothers with contraindications to breastfeeding can feed their child using paladai. The milk can either be expressed breastmilk or they can resort to using undiluted cow milk or formula feeds . mcqs.chapter: Deficiency of Water-soluble Vitamins & Trace El...
mcqs.question: The eldest child of a ragpicker from the urban slums of Bandra presents with severe lower limb pain. Examination reveals swelling of costochondral junctions. The X-ray image obtained is given below . What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The clinical vignette involving a neglected child (eldest usually ) from a poor socio-economic background with bone pains due to subperiosteal haemorrhages and scorbutic rosary (swelling of costochondral junctions) is suggestive of scurvy. Radiological features of scurvy: Early changes • The white line of Frankel on the ends of the shafts of the tibia and fibula • Wimberger ring sign: Sclerotic rings around the epiphyses of the femur and tibia. Late changes • Trummerfeld zone: Zones of destruction in the femur and tibia • Pelkan spur at the cortical end The image sums up the X-ray features noted in scurvy.The image attached below shows a child with the scorbutic rosary.160

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Deficiency of Water-soluble Vitamins & Trace El...
mcqs.question: A child is born with the following abnormality. What advice do you give to the mother, with regards to the next pregnancy?

options.c: 400 mcg of folic acid after confirmation of pregnancy

mcqs.explanation: The given image shows spina bifida, the most common neural tube defect (NTD). 4000 mcg of folic acid periconceptionally is given to prevent NTDs in subsequent pregnancies . The normal dose of folic acid in pregnancy is 400 mcg (0.4 mg). However, the history of a previous pregnancy with an NTD raises the risk of another NTD in subsequent pregnancies . An increased dose of folic acid is thus prophylactically given during the periconceptional period to prevent NTD in the next child.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Basics of Neonatology and Routine Newborn Care
mcqs.question: Which of the following timelines would be included in the perinatal period as per WHO?

options.a: 37th week of gestation to 28 days after birth
options.b: 20th week of gestation to 7 days after birth
options.c: 28th week of gestation to 28 days after birth
options.d: 22nd week of gestation to 7 days after birth

mcqs.explanation: The WHO states that the perinatal period commences at 22 completed weeks and ends at seven completed days after birth - 154 days. It corresponds to when the fetus weighs 500g or more. This definition is not to be confused with the period used for the calculation of the perinatal mortality rate (PMR). To calculate the PMR, a fetal weight above 1000 g is considered , which is achieved at 28 weeks of gestation . Therefore, for all statistical purposes , international comparisons, and calculation of perinatal mortality rate, the period from the 28th week of life is considered .10 Perinatal period : from the 22nd week . Perinatal mortality rate calculation: from the 28th week . The neonatal period is defined as the first 28 days after birth. Infancy is defined as the first year of life . The image below shows various time periods . Only the time period for perinatal mortality and the perinatal period are different as shown in the image. For others, corresponding mortality rates are calculated using the same time periods shown.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A lady with wrong dates and a corrected gestational age of 43 weeks presents with labor pains. The CTG suggests placental insufficiency , and she is taken up for emergency LSCS. Which of the following physical signs is unlikely to be seen in this neonate ?
mcqs.explanation: The physical sign of an infant born post-term (43 weeks ) in association with presumed placental insufficiency is abundant hair (not scanty hair). Infants born post -term in association with presumed placental insufficiency may have various physical signs, together termed as postmaturity syndrome (or dysmaturity syndrome). These include : • Desquamation, pale skin, and long nails. • Loose skin around the thighs and buttocks . • Meconium -stained nails, skin, vernix , and umbilical cord. • Presence of placental membranes.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Diseases in Neonates requiring Special Care
mcqs.question: An anxious new mother brings her 18-day-old baby, to the casualty with complaints of poor feeding and yellowish discoloration of the skin. In the casualty , the baby had an episode of seizure . His total bilirubin is 32 mg/dl and he is diagnosed to have kernicterus. Which of the following will not be seen as a late feature of the disease ?
mcqs.explanation: Hypotonia is seen in the early phase of kernicterus. Kernicterus or bilirubin encephalopathy is a neurological syndrome resulting from the deposition of unconjugated (indirect) bilirubin in the basal ganglia and brainstem nuclei . It can result in permanent brain damage .Early Phase (Acut e) Late Phase Poor suck Movement disorders- choreo athetosis , ballismus, tremor Stupor Sensorineural hearing loss Hypotonia Defectiveupward gaze Seizures47

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 35-week neonate with grade 2 meconium-stained amniotic fluid is delivered by emergency LSCS. There is no spontaneous cry and the baby is unresponsive to tactile stimulation also. As the intern assisting in resuscitation , what is the order of suctioning that you will follow ?
mcqs.explanation: During neonatal resuscitation , the mouth is suctioned first and then the nares, in order to decrease the risk of aspiration. A 12 or 14 French suction catheter is used , with the suction pressure kept between 80-100 mmHg. Routine suctioning of the trachea during neonatal resuscitation is not recommended . The suctioning of the esophagus and stomach is avoided if not indicated specifically . It may produce a vagal response - apnea and/or bradycardia due to stimulation of the nerve in the posterior pharynx.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A pediatrician is evaluating a toddler for mental retardation. She hands a bright red ball to the baby and lets him play with it. She then takes the ball and hides it under a blanket in front of him. The child confusedly stares at the blanket and cries instead of searching for it. What is being tested here?
mcqs.explanation: Understanding that objects continue to exist even when not seen is called object permanence . This is due to an ability to form a mental representation of the object . It is attained at the age of 8–9 months. Option A: Separation anxiety begins at about 9 months of age . Children wake up crying from their naps as they realize that their parents are not in the same room as them. This is different from stranger anxiety displayed by the child at the age of 6-7 months, wherein they react to approaching strangers by crying or clinging to their parent. Option B: A transitional object is an object , such as a blanket or a stuffed toy, that is used by many children as a symbol of the absent parent. It is seen at around 18 months. Option C: Symbolic transformations in play: • At 12 months - make-believe (symbolic) play centres on the child's own body, e.g., the child pretends to drink from an empty cup . • At 18 month - symbolic transformations in play are not limited to the child's body, e.g., a doll can be fed from a plate .

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the eruption of teeth is false ?
mcqs.explanation: Primary teeth in the upper jaw erupt earlier than their counterpart in the lower jaw, except for lower central incisors and second molar. No primary teeth till the age of 13 months is called delayed eruption . As seen in the image below , the first primary tooth to erupt is the lower (mandibular) central incisor, at 5-7 months. All primary teeth erupt by 1.5–2.5 years of age .90 The first secondary tooth to erupt is the first molar (maxillary or mandibular), at 6-7 years, followed by the lower central incisor. Causes of delayed eruption : • Idiopathic: Most common • Hypothyroidism • Hypoparathyroidism • Familial • Mechanical blockage of individual teeth

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: You are taking a neonatal case for presentation during your postings . The mother tells you that the child is exclusively breastfed . Which of the following is least likely to corroborate with this history of being exclusively breastfed ?
mcqs.explanation: Exclusively breastfed infants are least likely to have evening colic. The incidence of diarrhoea, allergy to bovine milk, and atopic eczema are least reported in exclusively breastfed infants. Option A: Vitamin K content of milk is low and may contribute to hemorrhagic disease of the newborn. Option B: Breast milk contains inhibitors of glucuronyl transferase and enhances absorption of bilirubin from the gut . This leads to the development of breast milk jaundice . Option C: During the first few days, the breastfed infant has a black-green coloured stool . It changes to golden yellow by the end of the first week .108

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.chapter: Deficiency of Water-soluble Vitamins & Trace El...
mcqs.question: A four-year-old boy presents with petechiae , perifollicular haemorrhages, and swollen , bleeding gums. On examination, you identify the child to be malnourished and suspect scurvy. Which of the following is/are part of biochemical functions of the vitamin deficient in this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Scurvy is a deficiency of vitamin C. The correct answer is 1, 3, 5. Vitamin C is a water-soluble vitamin , which cannot be synthesized in the human body due to deficient L-gulonolactone oxidase enzyme. Breast milk contains adequate amounts of ascorbic acid, whereas the pasteurisation of animal milk at high temperature destroys vitamin C. Functions of Vitamin C / Ascorbic Acid : • Synthesis of collagen (Hydroxylation of proline, which is vital for collagen ; in the formation of the bone matrix). • Neurotransmitter metabolism (conversion of dopamine to norepinephrine and tryptophan to serotonin) • Cholesterol metabolism (conversion of cholesterol to steroid hormones and bile acids) • Biosynthesis of carnitine158 • Antioxidation (electron donor) • For the cellular and immunologic functions of the hematopoietic system The image below shows peri-follicular haemorrhages.

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: The amount of sodium present in ReSoMal is ________
mcqs.explanation: Rehydration solution for malnourished (ReSoMal) contains 45 mmol/L of sodium. Severely malnourished children have excess intracellular sodium (leaky cell membranes and reduced activity of the sodium–potassium pump ). So, sodium intake should be reduced and a low-sodium oral rehydration solution (ReSoMal) is advised. Because severely malnourished children are deficient in potassium , ReSoMal contains extra potassium , as well as extra glucose or sucrose and selected minerals (Mg, Cu, Zn ).

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A 29-year-old woman is homozygous for an autosomal-recessive gene and her husband is heterozygous for the same. They are planning to start a family and wish to know the outcome of their pregnancy. Which out of the following options correctly represent the percentages of the outcome ?

options.b: No child affected , but all are carriers

mcqs.explanation: If the husband is heterozygous and the wife is homozygous for an autosomal recessive gene , 50% of the children will be affected ; the rest will be carriers. This is pseudo -dominant inheritance, which refers to the observation of apparent dominant (parent to child) transmission of a known autosomal-recessive disorder, or it can also mean the inheritance of a recessive trait mimics a dominant pattern. This occurs when a homozygous affected individual has a partner who is a heterozygous carrier , and their children have a 1 in 2 chance to get affected (50%).203

mcqs.subject: Pediatrics

mcqs.question: A 2-year-old girl presented with photophobia and speech delay . On examination, she had bilateral herpetiform corneal ulcers and painful hyperkeratotic plaques on the palms and soles . Which among the following is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: Palmar and plantar hyperkeratosis , herpetiform corneal ulcers , and intellectual disability are seen in hereditary tyrosinemia type 2 (Richner–Hanhart syndrome/ oculocutaneous tyrosinemia) Treatment with a diet low in tyrosine and phenylalanine aiming to achieve plasma tyrosine levels <500 \265 mol/L improves skin and eye manifestations . mcqs.subject: Pediatrics
mcqs.question: A neonate born out of a second -degree consanguineous marriage is suspected to have an inborn error of metabolism . He can present with all of the following except :
mcqs.explanation: Irritability and incessant crying are not classical features of inborn errors of metabolism (IEM). Clinical clues suggesting IEM in a neonate are: • Unexpected deterioration after a normal initial period . • Nonspecific , unexplained features such as poor feeding , lethargy , vomiting, hypotonia, failure to thrive, respiratory abnormalities, apnea, bradycardia, and hypothermia . • Family history of similar illnesses , unexplained sibling deaths , or progressive neurological disease . • Parental consanguinity: Most acutely presenting metabolic disorders are autosomal recessive .
