mcqs.explanation: The best plane for measurement of the volume of the hippocampus is the coronal plane, angled perpendicular to the long axis of the hippocampus in MRI, which is represented by the image marked B. Coronal MRI is taken perpendicular to the long axis of the temporal horn can be used to measure : • Volume of hippocampus - measured in Alzheimer's disease and medial temporal seizures • Medial temporal lobe atrophy (MTA) The planes of MRI are given below .Image marked as D shows the axial section of a CT.40

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: A patient suspected to have biliary tract abnormalities undergoes the investigation shown in the image below . Identify the imaging and structure marked as A.
mcqs.explanation: The image depicts a magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP), and the structure marked as A is the common bile duct . MRCP is a non-invasive test showing a heavy T2 -weighted image. The endoscope or contrast medium is not used as bile itself serves as a contrast medium.41 The image given below shows endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP).

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: The radiograph of a boy is given below . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The X-ray shows a champagne glass pelvis and is suggestive of achondroplasia. Achondroplasia is a genetic disorder resulting in proximal limb shortening (rhizomelic dwarfism). It is the most common cause of disproportionate dwarfism. The iliac blades are flattened giving rise to a pelvic inlet that resembles a champagne glass . The acetabular angles are flattened (horizontal) and the sacrosciatic notch is small.The image below shows a patient with achondroplasia -59 Other options : Option A: Perthe 's disease is characterized by a flattened and later, fragmented femoral head . Option B: Hip dysplasia usually presents with hip dislocation . Option C: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE ) presents with the metaphysis being displaced laterally and not overlapping the posterior lip of the acetabulum as it should normally.

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: Radiograph of a child with history of delayed walking showed the following findings. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given X-ray shows fraying and cupping of the metaphysis with a widening of joint spaces . The radiological features are characteristic of active rickets.

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: What is the dense zone of calcification seen at the metaphysis in scurvy?
mcqs.explanation: Dense zone of calcification at growing metaphysis seen in scurvy is known as Frankel's line.

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following conditions is least likely to cause the following appearance on a radiograph?
mcqs.explanation: The given radiograph shows the bone within a bone appearance , which describes bones that appear to have another bone within them on a radiograph. This finding is least likely to be seen in hyperparathyroidism . Causes of bone within bone appearance on a radiograph include : • Osteopetrosis • Paget 's disease • Caffey disease • Sickle cell anemia • Thalassemia • Congenital syphilis • Gaucher disease

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: A young soccer player presents with complaints of pain in his right shoulder . He fell while alternating from jumping jacks to push -ups during a warm-up drill. His shoulder 's radiograph is shown below . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario along with the light bulb sign in the X-ray is suggestive of a posterior dislocation of the shoulder . It occurs most commonly during a convulsion, or after an electric shock. It can also happen after a fall on the flexed , adducted arm , either by a direct blow to the front of the shoulder or due to a fall on the outstretched hand. There is internal rotation of humeral head which causes changes to the normal radiographic contour of the head of the humerus. Radiological signs described in posterior dislocation of the shoulder in the AP view are as follows : • Light bulb sign - Shape of humeral head appears like that of an electric bulb • Rim sign - Widening of the glenohumeral joint space > 6 mm • Vacant glenoid sign - Glenoid fossa looks empty as the humeral head has moved away from it • Trough sign - Vertical line seen on the anteromedial part of the humeral head due to the impression fracture by the glenoid labrum66

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: A young male presents with pain in his right shoulder . He slipped during his treadmill workout and tried to hold on to the side rails. The x-ray image obtained is given below . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario describes a patient who developed pain in his shoulder after forced abduction of his shoulder after a fall. The x-ray shows the head of the humerus is below the glenoid and the shaft in the abducted position. This is suggestive of an inferior shoulder dislocation , also known as luxatio erecta . It is rare and occurs when the arm is forcefully pulled up when in full abduction (hyper -abduction force) due to high-energy trauma. The patient will present with the arm locked in almost full abduction .

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: A 7-year-old boy is brought to the casualty after a fall on an outstretched hand. An X-ray of the patient is given below . Identify the true statement regarding the condition.

options.a: It commonly leads to cubitus valgus deformity
options.b: Damage to the median nerve can cause pointing index finger
options.c: Myositis ossificans is one of its acute complications
options.d: The most common complication is non union

mcqs.explanation: This patient 's presentation after a fall on the outstretched arm and the x-ray is suggestive of a supracondylar fracture of the humerus. A displaced fracture can damage median nerve causing pointing index sign. A common complication is cubitus varus deformity (gunstock deformity ) due to the malunion of fractured ends . Myositis ossificans is a delayed complication of the fracture.67

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man presented with severe pain in the wrist after suffering a fall on an outstretched hand during his morning jog. His X-ray is given below . What is the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The given features and radiograph are suggestive of volar or reverse Barton 's fracture. Volar -type /reverse Barton 's is a fracture-dislocation of the volar rim of the radius. This type is the most common. Dislocation of the radiocarpal joint is the hallmark of Barton 's fracture. The radiographic findings are the following: • Comminuted intraarticular fracture of the distal radius • Volar rim maintains a relationship with the carpus and both are displaced proximally • Fracture of the radial styloid process with loss of radial inclination Reverse-type Barton 's fracture is similar to Smith's fracture, but the difference is that the fracture line runs obliquely and extends into the joint surface . Another type is dorsal Barton 's fracture which results due to fracture-dislocation of the dorsal rim of the radius.68 The image below shows the lateral and anterior-posterior view of the dorsal-type of Barton 's fracture with dorsal displacement .69

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: All among the following are ionizing radiations except :
mcqs.explanation: MRI is a technique that produces topographic images by means of magnetic fields and radiofrequency waves. The ionizing radiations • Alpha • Beta8 • Gamma • X-Rays The non-Ionizing radiations are: • Radiofrequency waves • UV rays • Microwaves Alpha and beta rays are particulate radiation (particles ) whereas gamma and x-rays are electromagnetic rays. All electromagnetic waves have a constant velocity of 3\327108 m/s and no mass. The electromagnetic spectrum , from low frequency to high frequency consists of: Radiowaves < Microwaves < Infrared < Visible light < Ultraviolet < X-rays < Gamma rays Note : W. C. Roentgen is the father of X-ray and the first medical X-ray by Roentgen was of his wife Anna Bertha's left hand. Physicists Peter Mansfield and Paul Lauterbur developed MRI-related imaging techniques in medicine and they were awarded the Nobel prize in 2003 .

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: The photoelectric effect can be best described as an interaction between :

options.a: High energy incident photon and the inner shell electron
options.b: Low energy incident photon and the outer shell electron
options.c: High energy incident photon and the outer shell electron
options.d: Low energy incident photon and the inner shell electron

mcqs.explanation: The photoelectric effect is an interaction between a low to intermediate energy X-ray beam and the inner shell electron . When the inner shell electron is ejected , the outer electron goes into the inner orbit to occupy the space , and the extra energy is ejected as characteristic radiation, and is called the photoelectric effect . The photoelectric effect is fundamentally important in diagnostic radiography since it is the primary method by which contrast is developed in radiographs. It allows for the differentiation of different types of tissues on the X-ray film.11 Very low-energy X-rays are not capable of producing the photoelectric effect . High energy X-rays are also not capable of photoelectric effect due to random scattering of electrons from the outer shell . This is known as the Compton effect and it can lead to distortion of the image. The goal of X-ray imaging should be to minimize the Compton effect and maximize the photoelectric effect . The penetrating power of X-rays increases with increasing energy , which is directly proportional to the frequency and inversely proportional to the wavelength .

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a water soluble contrast?
mcqs.explanation: Iohexol is a nonionic, water-soluble radiographic contrast medium. It is used to visualize the following structres: • Arteries • Veins13 • Ventricles of the brain • The urinary system • Joints It can be used during computer tomography (CT scan) as well . It can be given orally, intravenously, or can be injected into the body cavity.

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: What does the Hounsfield unit depend on?
mcqs.explanation: Hounsfield unit (HU) depends on the linear attenuation co-efficient . Attenuation is the reduction of the intensity of an X-ray beam as it traverses matter. HU is used to measure the X-ray attenuation values in CT scanning, thus quantifying the radiodensity of the tissue . The Hounsfield scale , named after Sir Godfrey Hounsfield invented CT in the year 1972 and was awarded Nobel Prize for Medicine in the year 1979.Tissues Hounsfield unit Cortical bone +1000 HU (Bright white ) Solid soft tissue +40 to +80 HU (sometimes u pto +300 ) Acute hemorrha ge +45 to +65 HU15 Tissues Hounsfield unit Water 0 HU (Grey) Fat -100 HU Lungs -950 to -700 HU Air -1000 HU (Jet black)

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: What is the initial investigation for evaluating a patient suspected to have an aortic dissection ?
mcqs.explanation: CT is the initial investigation for aortic dissection as it is more widely available and takes a shorter time when compared to MRI. MRI, though highly accurate for acute aortic disease evaluation, is usually confined to cases of severe renal insufficiency or when the use of iodinated contrast medium is absolutely contraindicated . The image below depicts CT chest showing Type A aortic dissection from the aortic root. (A) Axial view and (B) sagittal view. The arrows indicate the intimal flap.The image below shows the classification systems used for aortic dissection .17

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is not echogenic on ultrasonography ?
mcqs.explanation: Bile is not echogenic on ultrasound. Echoes are not produced if there is no difference in acoustic density . Hence , homogeneous fluids are seen as echo -free structures . Examples of homogenous fluids include blood, bile , urine, cyst contents , ascites , and pleural effusion . Homogenous fluids transmit sound exceptionally well and render increased echoes to those structures deeper to them. This is called acoustic enhancement / posterior enhancement / enhanced through transmission. Acoustic shadowing is present behind bony structures , calculi, and air.The image given below shows posterior enhancement of a renal cyst .28 The below image shows a gall bladder stone with acoustic shadowing .

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: The Doppler waveform of the venous blood flow in lower limb DVT is _____.
mcqs.explanation: The Doppler waveform of the venous blood flow in lower limb DVT is monophasic proximal to the level of obstruction. The normal venous waveform shows a variation (phasicity ) secondary to respiration referred to as respirophasic waveform. Loss of this phasic variation results in a monophasic waveform suggestive of venous obstruction proximal to the level of interrogation. A normal artery has a triphasic signal. The waveform becomes biphasic in mild-moderate stenosis and monophasic in severe stenosis . The image given below shows the normal triphasic signal from an artery.Monophasic waveform:32

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: What is the metallic shielding used in MRI rooms called ?
mcqs.explanation: MRI rooms are shielded completely by a continuous sheet or wire mesh of copper called Faraday cage , which provides radiofrequency (RF) shielding . Faraday cage is a conductive box used to shield out stray electromagnetic interference . It is most commonly made of wood panels wrapped with copper . Other metals like aluminium and galvanized steel can also be used . It serves two functions: • To prevent external radiofrequency pulses from interfering with the detector • To prevent radiofrequency pulses generated by the scanner from interfering with the external environment

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following pathological conditions can be identified with diffusion -weighted MRI ?
mcqs.explanation: Diffusion -weighted (DWI ) MRI can identify the following : • Acute infarct can be detected within 3-30 mins (CT/MRI can detect only after 24 hours) • Brain abscess and epidermoid cyst appear bright on DWI . Hence , they can be differentiated from necrotic tumours and arachnoid cysts , respectively . • It can also differentiate herpes encephalitis from diffuse temporal gliomas. This type of imaging is based on Brownian motion i.e., structures that allow diffusion will not appear bright. The region with less diffusion has more T2 signal, which is why dead tissue appears bright.42 The image given below shows DWI in acute infarct of the brain .Bone marrow edema can be visualized by STIR (short tau inversion recovery). Note : The most common site of epidermoid cyst in the brain is CP angle.43

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following bone lesions is not associated with the doughnut sign during a radiotracer uptake study ?
mcqs.explanation: Multiple myeloma does not show the doughnut sign during radiotracer uptake as the lesion has only lytic activity. Radiotracer is actively taken up by bone-forming areas. Doughnut sign occurs because of radiotracer accumulation at the periphery of the lesion where there is a reactionary bone formation, with little activity at its centre . Causes include : • Aneurysmal Bone cyst • Giant cell tumor • Chondrosarcoma • Telangiectatic osteosarcoma Shown below is the donut sign seen in a case of aneurysmal bone cyst .63

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man complains of right hip pain while walking up the stairs. He has been on long-term steroid therapy for rheumatoid arthritis. Physical examination and radiograph of the hip are unremarkable. What is the best imaging modality for his condition?
mcqs.explanation: The given scenario of a patient with hip pain on chronic glucocorticoid therapy , with non-significant findings on radiographs and exam, is suggestive of avascular necrosis (AVN) of the femoral head . The best imaging modality for this is MRI. Long-term steroid usage is a risk factor for the development of AVN . MRI allows the identification of avascular necrosis of the femoral head in earlier stages and also helps determine the exact stage and extent of the pathologic process . The X-ray below shows flattening of the femoral head and degenerative changes associated with osteonecrosis or AVN .75 The radiographic appearance of avascular necrosis of the femoral head may show the following changes : • Sclerosis of the femoral head • Flattening or loss of sphericity of femoral head • Crescent sign - subchondral fracture overlying the necrotic segment of the femoral head • In severe stages , it may show femoral head collapse and arthritic changes in the joint

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: Chest X-ray is most commonly performed in which of the following views?
mcqs.explanation: Chest X-ray is most commonly performed in posteroanterior view (PA view) because it minimizes the magnification of the cardiac silhouette . In PA view, the anterior structures are closer to the detector . It is usually done in full inspiration and standing position. Ideally , there should be no rotation. If there is no rotation the distance between the medial end of the clavicle and the spinous process will be equidistant , on both sides . In a normal chest X-ray, the left dome of the diaphragm is lower than the right because the heart pushes the left dome down. In anterior-to-posterior (AP) radiographs, the posterior structures are closer to the detector . Identification of PA and AP view chest X-ray:PA view AP view Clavicl es Seen over the lung fields Seen above the apex of lung f ields Scapul a The inner border is seen awa y from lung fields The inner border is seen over the lung fields Ribs Posterior ribs are more visibl e Anterior ribs are more visible89

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: A 62-year-old male with COPD presents with sudden onset chest pain and shortness of breath. On auscultation , breath sounds were absent on the left side . What is the best chest x-ray view to diagnose this condition?
mcqs.explanation: The patient most likely has pneumothorax . The best chest x-ray view to diagnose a pneumothorax is PA view in full expiration. Expiratory chest X-ray is done in pneumothorax, conditions causing air trapping (foreign body, partial bronchial obstruction), and diaphragmatic palsy . Image showing left -sided pneumothorax:94

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: The chest radiograph of a patient showed silhouetting of the left border of the heart. Pathology of which part of the lung does this indicate ?
mcqs.explanation: Silhouetting of the left border of the heart indicates a pathology in the lingula segments . The principle of silhouette sign is that the mediastinal borders can be obscured only by a pathology that is in direct anatomical contact. Positive silhouette sign and corresponding anatomical site of pathology : • Right heart border- right middle lobe or medial right lower lobe • Left heart border - lingula segments of the left upper lobe • Left hemidiaphragm or descending aorta - left lower lobe • Aortic knuckle - left upper lobe (posterior segment ) • Right hemidiaphragm - right lower lobe • Right paratracheal stripe - right upper lobe Recognition of this sign is useful in localising areas of airspace opacities , atelectasis , or mass within the lung. The radiograph below shows the silhouette sign- the left cardiac border is obscured due to pneumonia of the lingula of the left lung.102

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding Kerley A lines?

options.a: Radiate from the hilum of lungs
options.b: Runs perpendicular to the pleural surface and extend out to it
options.d: Short lines which do not reach the pleura

mcqs.explanation: Kerley A lines radiate from the hilum of the lungs . Kerley lines are seen when the interlobular septa in the pulmonary interstitium become prominent. This may be because of lymphatic engorgement or edema of the connective tissues of the interlobular septa . They usually occur when pulmonary capillary wedge pressure reaches 20 -25 mmHg. Types of Kerley lines:106 • Kerley A lines: • Thin , oblique lines(2-6cm long and thickness under 1mm ), radiating from the hilum to the upper lobes . • HRCT is the most effective imaging technique to identify these lines. • Kerley B lines: • Thin , horizontal lines (1-2 cm long), seen at the lung periphery , usually near the bases . • Run perpendicular to the pleural surface and reach it, representing thickened subpleural interlobular septa . • Kerley C lines : • Short, irregular lines with a spider web-like appearance . • Unlike Kerley B and D lines, they do not extend to the pleura ; unlike Kerley A lines, they do not radiate outward from the hila. • Kerley D lines - the same as Kerley B lines, except that they are seen on lateral chest radiographs in the retrosternal air gap The image below depicts the Kerley B line, perpendicular to the pleural surface :

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.chapter: Lung Infections, Sarcoidosis and Lung Cancer
mcqs.question: In which condition is popcorn calcification seen ?
mcqs.explanation: 133 Popcorn calcification is seen in pulmonary hamartoma . Popcorn calcification is defined as a pattern of calcification in rings and arcs that resemble popped corn kernels. The presence of fat in a well -circumscribed solitary pulmonary nodule that does not demonstrate significant growth is pathognomonic of a pulmonary hamartoma . Chest x-ray showing pulmonary hamartoma:

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.chapter: Lung Infections, Sarcoidosis and Lung Cancer
mcqs.question: Which type of lung carcinoma can mimic consolidation on chest X-ray?
mcqs.explanation: Adenocarcinoma in situ mimics consolidation on X-ray. It is also known as minimally invasive adenocarcinoma / broncho-alveolar carcinoma . Unlike other lung carcinomas, broncho-alveolar carcinoma is known to show air bronchogram. They spread along the bronchial wall, which is known as the lepidic spread . In general , an air bronchogram is absent in bronchogenic carcinoma since the bronchus is obstructed . Below is a CT chest showing focal consolidation with a patent bronchus.136

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: What is the earliest sign of left atrial enlargement on a chest x-ray ?

options.d: Elevation of left main bronchus and widening of carina

mcqs.explanation: Enlargement of the left atrial appendage is the earliest sign of left atrial enlargement (LAE) on a chest x-ray. It is seen as a fullness below the pulmonary artery. Other radiographic signs seen in LAE include :152 • The third mogul sign represents an enlargement of the left atrial appendage along the upper left cardiac border, leading to straightening of the left heart border. • Posterior displacement of the oesophagus - seen on the lateral view of the barium swallow study . • Elevation of left main bronchus and widening of the carina . • Double density sign or double atrial shadow - the enlarged LA extends towards the right cardiac border, hence , both RA and LA borders can be seen distinctly over the right heart border (as shown below ):The X-ray below demonstrates straightening of the left cardiac border and widening of the carina , with the carinal angle becoming more obtuse , reflecting left atrial enlargement .The causes of left atrial enlargement are as follows : • Congenital : Ventricular septal defect , Patent ductus arteriosus • Acquired: Mitral valvular disease , left ventricular failure, left atrial myxoma153

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: Pruning of pulmonary arteries is seen in which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Pulmonary artery hypertension is associated with peripheral pruning of pulmonary vessels . This means that the blood vessels appear cut off before they reach the outer 1/3 of the lung. Hence , the edge of the lung fields is darker than usual , and the central area is often whiter . Plain radiographic findings in pulmonary artery hypertension include elevated cardiac apex due to right ventricular hypertrophy , enlarged right atrium, prominent pulmonary outflow tract, enlarged pulmonary arteries, and peripheral pruning.161 The image below shows Chest X-ray findings in pulmonary hypertension :

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: What is the most\037 common site of hypertensive bleed in the brain ?
mcqs.explanation: 176 The most common site of hypertensive bleed in the brain is the basal ganglia (Putamen in particular). The most common cause of intracerebral haemorrhages is hypertension . Following are the typical locations of ICH in order of decreasing frequency: • Basal ganglia haemorrhage (especially the putamen ) • Thalamic haemorrhage • Pontine haemorrhage • Cerebellar haemorrhage

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: Eye of tiger sign on MRI is seen in which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: The eye of the tiger sign can be seen in Hallervorden-Spatz syndrome. The 'eye of the tiger' sign on the T2 -weighted MRI appears as bilateral symmetrical hyperintense signals in global pallidus (due to gliosis and spongiosis ), surrounded by hypointense areas (due to abnormal accumulation of iron). Hallervorden-Spatz syndrome or Pantothenate kinase-associated neurodegeneration (PKAN) is an autosomal recessive disorder causing involuntary spasticity and progressive dementia . It is a subset of neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation (NBIA). It is also seen in Progressive supranuclear palsy , early-onset levodopa -responsive Parkinsonism , and cortical-basal ganglionic degeneration. The image below depicts the eye of the tiger sign:189

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: Basal ganglia calcification can be seen on imaging of patients with all of the following conditions, except :
mcqs.explanation: Basal ganglia calcification is not a feature of hemochromatosis. The causes of pathological basal ganglia calcifications are : • Endocrinopathies : Hypoparathyroidism (primary or secondary), pseudohypoparathyroidism , hyperparathyroidism, hypothyroidism • Vasculitis (e.g. SLE) • Mitochondrial disorders (e.g. Mitochondrial myopathy ) • Infections: Brucellosis , TORCH , Epstein -Barr virus (EBV), HIV • Other inherited disorders: Neuroferritinonpathy , Cockayne syndrome • Radiation • Chemotherapy • Carbon monoxide poisoning • Lead poisoning The following image is a CT brain showing bilateral basal ganglia calcification:210

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: A patient is found to have a cerebellopontine angle mass. The differential diagnosis can include all except :
mcqs.explanation: Tuberculoma is not a cause of cerebellopontine (CP) angle mass. The most common cerebellopontine (CP) tumour is acoustic schwannoma (90%). Other tumours include meningiomas and epidermoid cysts .219 CP angle tumours (Mnemonic- SAME ): • S: Schwannoma (8th nerve > 5th ) • A: Aneurysm, arachnoid cyst • M: Meningioma, metastases • E: Epidermoid , ependymoma The given image shows bilateral CP angle masses (acoustic schwannomas):

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: The hot cross bun sign on MRI would be seen in patients with which of the following conditions?
mcqs.explanation: The hot cross bun sign on MRI, characterised by cruciform pontine hyperintensity due to selective neuronal loss of the transverse pontocerebellar fibres, is most commonly observed in patients with multiple system atrophy-cerebellar type (MSA-C). Multiple system atrophy (a type of synucleinopathies ) is a neurodegenerative disorder with varying degrees of involvement of the basal ganglia and the olivopontocerebellar complex . Autonomic dysfunction is more severe and generalised , often presenting as orthostatic hypotension . MSA has been divided clinically into two forms according to the dominant non-autonomic symptoms : • MSA-C: Predominance of cerebellar symptoms (olivopontocerebellar atrophy) • MSA-P: Predominance of Parkinsonian signs and symptoms (striatonigral degeneration ) MRI is a valuable diagnostic adjunct, often revealing cerebellar and brainstem atrophy causing pontine hot cross bun sign. The axial T2 -weighted image at the level of middle cerebellar peduncles below shows the hot cross bun sign:226 Other options : Option B: Multiple system atrophy-parkinsonian type (MSA-P) is characterised by atypical parkinsonism that is symmetrical and predominantly axial, with tremors less prominent compared to Parkinson 's disease . MRI typically reveals hyperintensities along the lateral aspect of the putamina, and T2 -weighted imaging may demonstrate hypointensity in the striatum due to iron deposition . Although not exclusive to MSA, the hot cross bun sign is more commonly seen in MSA-C than in MSA-P. Option C: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) is a form of atypical parkinsonism characterized by slow ocular saccades , eyelid apraxia, and restricted vertical eye movements with downward gaze palsy . Patients also have hyperextension of the neck with gait disturbances and frequent falls. MRI may reveal characteristic atrophy of the midbrain with normal pons, which is called a hummingbird sign.227

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: A T2 weighted MRI was done for a child who presented with delayed milestones . It showed hyperintensity in frontal white matter with bilateral and symmetrical involvement. What is the likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: 233 The T2 -weighted MRI findings suggest Alexander disease , showing hyperintensity in the frontal white matter with bilateral symmetrical involvement. Alexander disease is a type of dysmyelinating disease that typically progresses posteriorly to involve the parietal white matter and internal and external capsules , often accompanied by the formation of cysts . Dysmyelinating diseases , or leukodystrophies , are inherited neurodegenerative disorders that affect the integrity of myelin in the brain and peripheral nerves. Other examples of dysmyelinating diseases include : • Metachromatic leukodystrophy : • Late infantile (most common), juvenile, and adult types . • Symmetric confluent areas of T2 hyperintensity in the periventricular white matter. • Radiating T2 -hypointense lines through the demyelinated deep white matter represent the sparing of the perivascular white matter. This results in the tigroid and leopard skin patterns when imaged in the long axis or cross-section , respectively . • X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy : Affects the white matter of the central nervous system , adrenal cortex, and testes . • Canavan disease : Spongiform leukodystrophy (extensive vacuolization of subcortical white matter). • MELAS Syndrome: Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes . The following image shows the areas of hyperintensities noted in each of these conditions:234

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the best way to detect minimum pneumoperitoneum on X-ray in a patient with abdominal trauma?

options.c: Right lateral decubitus chest X-ray with horizontal beam
options.d: Left lateral decubitus abdomen X-ray with horizontal beam

mcqs.explanation: Among the given options , the left lateral decubitus X-ray of the abdomen is the best view to visualize the pneumoperitoneum . As little as 1 mL of free gas can be detected on a plain radiograph. Hence the best views to visualize pneumoperitoneum : • Erect chest X-ray - the first, most important and useful view showing air beneath the diaphragm. • Left lateral decubitus abdominal image CT abdomen is the most sensitive imaging technique to detect minimal pneumoperitoneum .265

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: String sign on radiological imaging is seen in all of the following conditions except ?
mcqs.explanation: String sign is not seen in ulcerative colitis. String sign refers to the thin, string-like appearance of a severely narrowed bowel loop on radiographic imaging. This narrowing occurs due to spasms, edema , inflammation or ulceration. It is commonly seen in Crohn's disease (string sign of Kantor), hypertrophic pyloric stenosis , and ileocaecal tuberculosis . Other options :288 Option C: Given below is the barium study showing string sign of Kantor seen in Crohn's disease :Option B: Given below are images showing congenital hypertrophic pyloric stenosis :Option A: Given below is a barium enema showing string sign in ileocaecal tuberculosis :289

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: A patient with chronic alcoholism presented with nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. His lab reports showed elevated serum amylase and lipase levels . Which of the following signs is unlikely to be seen in the radiograph of this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with elevated serum amylase and lipase suggests acute pancreatitis . Grey Turner's sign, seen in this condition, is a clinical sign, not a radiological finding, characterized by flank discolouration due to retroperitoneal haemorrhage. Acute hemorrhagic pancreatitis can present clinically with certain named signs like Cullen 's sign, Grey Turner's sign, Fox sign, and Bryant's sign (discolouration of the scrotum). Radiological signs in acute pancreatitis include colon cut-off sign, preserved renal halo sign, and sentinel loop sign (upper abdomen). Note : The sentinel loop sign may aid in localizing the source of inflammation. For example , the sentinel loop sign in the right lower quadrant may be due to appendicitis .

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: During intravenous pyelography of a patient , the left kidney could not be visualized. What condition is this suggestive of?
mcqs.explanation: Non-visualization of the kidney on IVP is seen in the case of multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK ). MCDK is a form of renal dysplasia characterized by multiple , non-communicating cysts of varying sizes, separated by dysplastic parenchyma, with the absence of a normal pelvicalyceal system . It results from a developmental abnormality due to failure of the renal mesenchyme to unite with the ureteric bud. This condition is associated with ureteral or ureteropelvic atresia, and the affected kidney is non-functional. Most cases of MCDK are detected antenatally through ultrasonography . In some cases , the cysts identified prenatally may regress in utero, resulting in the affected kidney being undetectable on imaging at birth. Renal ultrasonography is the initial investigation of choice . It reveals a soap bubble appearance . Bilateral MCDK can lead to pulmonary hypoplasia and Potter syndrome. The following image shows a non-visualized right kidney (red arrow).336 Other options : Option A: In the duplicated collecting system , the drooping lily sign is seen . It refers to the inferolateral displacement of the opacified lower pole moiety due to an obstructed (and un-opacified ) upper pole moiety . Option B: In polycystic kidney disease, a streaky appearance is seen due to ectatic collecting ducts . Option D: In renal hypoplasia , there is a congenitally small kidney with smaller calyces , lobules , and papillae but essentially normal residual parenchyma. On imaging, a hypoplastic kidney is small but otherwise normal .

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: A 59-year-old man was referred for abdominal pain and sterile pyuria. He was diagnosed with tuberculosis 10 years ago but was non-adherent to treatment . What is the most sensitive imaging modality for his current presentation ?
mcqs.explanation: Sterile pyuria in a patient with history of tuberculosis raises suspicion of renal tuberculosis . The most sensitive imaging modality for diagnosing renal tuberculosis is CT Intravenous Pyelogram. Renal tuberculosis occurs due to hematogenous dissemination of Mycobacterium tuberculosis , making it a secondary infection . There is either reinfection or reactivation of old TB . It is more common in males and typically presents with symptoms such as increased urinary frequency, polyuria, dysuria, hematuria, loin pain/suprapubic pain and sterile pyuria. In sterile pyuria, urine appears pale and opalescent due to the presence of pus cells . Renal TB is a cause of sterile pyuria. Diagnosis is confirmed with a tuberculin test , or at least 3 consecutive early-morning urine specimens are examined for acid-fast bacilli. They are stained with a Ziehl–Neelsen stain and subsequently cultured . The most sensitive imaging modality in renal tuberculosis is CT urography/pyelography . NCCT is the preferred means of visualizing renal calcifications . Manifestations of renal TB as seen on CT are as follows : • Early changes : • Papillary necrosis (single or multiple) and uneven caliectasis • Progressive changes : • Multifocal strictures in any part of the collecting system • Generalized or focal hydronephrosis • Mural thickening and enhancement • Poorly enhancing renal parenchyma, either due to direct involvement or due to hydronephrosis • End-stage :342 • Progressive hydronephrosis results in very thin parenchyma, mimicking multiple thin-walled cysts • Amorphous dystrophic calcification eventually involves the entire kidney (known as the putty kidney ), as shown below :

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: A 62-year-old man is being evaluated for new-onset bilateral pedal edema . He had been diagnosed with left -sided renal cell carcinoma 2 months ago but had declined surgery. What is the investigation of choice to evaluate his current complaints?
mcqs.explanation: Bilateral pedal edema in an elderly patient with left -sided renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is suspicious for tumor extension into the left renal vein and IVC . The investigation of choice to assess the vascular extension of the tumor thrombus is Magnetic resonance imaging. RCC is the most common malignant tumor of the kidney that usually presents in the elderly . Cigarette smoking and hypertension are major associated risk factors. The classic triad of presentation is with flank pain, macroscopic haematuria, and a palpable flank mass. Advanced cases can also present with bilateral lower limb edema . MRI is beneficial for assessing vascular invasion , especially when evaluating the renal vein and IVC. It aids in differentiating between benign and malignant thrombus. However, it does not provide a significant advantage over CT in staging nodal disease . Other options : Option C: Triphasic contrast-enhanced CT is the investigation of choice for diagnosis and staging o f RCC (image given below ). On CT, small lesions enhance homogeneously , whereas larger lesions have irregular enhancement due to areas of necrosis. The CT also provides additional information on the function of the opposite kidney, primary tumor extension , venous involvement, enlargement of regional lymph nodes , the status of the adrenal glands, and intra-abdominal metastatic disease .359 Option A: Intravenous urography is no longer suitable for detecting renal masses , particularly if they occur centrally ; cross-sectional imaging studies are more appropriate for investigating suspected renal mass. Option D: FDG-Positron Emission Tomography plays a limited role in the initial detection and diagnosis of RCC due to low fluorodeoxyglucose uptake by these tumours. However, it can be useful in identifying local recurrence and serves as a complementary tool alongside other cross-sectional imaging methods .

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: A young girl with primary amenorrhea is being evaluated for the presence of a congenital uterine anomaly. What is the gold standard investigation to detect the same?
mcqs.explanation: Magnetic Resonance Imaging is the most accurate imaging technique for investigating and classifying congenital uterine anomalies and is hence considered to be the gold standard. Classifying congenital uterine anomalies is important as fertility outcomes and surgical management vary considerably . Other options - Option B: Computed Tomography and X-ray are not preferred , and in case of suspected pregnancy they are avoided. Option C: Ultrasonography is the primary/initial investigation done. However, not all uterine anomalies can be detected and classified .375 Option D: Hysterosalpingography is also done, however, it cannot differentiate between a septate and bicornuate uterus , as only the uterine interior is visualized, leading to similar images on HSG.

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: Match the following SI units with the parameters measured .
mcqs.explanation: The correctly matched SI units and parameters measured are as follows : The common unit to measure radioactivity is curie. The common unit to measure total radiation exposure is roentgen .SI Unit Parameter measured Gray Absorbed radiation Becquer el Radioactivity Coulom b/kg Total radiation exposur e Sievert Dose equivalent

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: Which of the following radioactive isotopes is not used for brachytherapy ?
mcqs.explanation: I-131 is a beta -emitter used for systemic radiotherapy but not for brachytherapy . It is taken up by thyroid tissue and differentiated thyroid cancers. Brachytherapy is a type of radiotherapy where radioactive sources are placed inside or close to the target area. It delivers radiation over short distances using interstitial , intracavitary , or surface placement techniques . The following isotopes are used in brachytherapy : • Permanent Low-dose rate (LDR ) implants generally use Iodine-125, Palladium-103 , or less commonly Gold-198. • Temporary LDR implants may use Iridium-192 , Cesium -137, Cobalt-60 or others. • High-dose rate (HDR) implants almost always use Iridium-192 .

mcqs.subject: Radiology
mcqs.question: What is the most radiosensitive tissue in our body?
mcqs.explanation: The most radiosensitive tissue in our body is bone marrow . The least radiosensitive tissue is the nervous tissue . Note : The most radiosensitive blood cells are lymphocytes and the least are platelets . RBCs are relatively radioresistant.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A peripherally inserted central catheter line(PICC) was placed in a patient to provide parenteral nutrition. Following the insertion, a chest X-ray was taken, which appeared as shown in the image below . Which of the following is the ideal position of the tip of this catheter ?
mcqs.explanation: The ideal position of the tip of a peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) line, is superior vena cava . Peripherally inserted central catheters are commonly used for providing parenteral nutrition therapy. They are inserted through veins in the upper arm , and guided into the central venous system , such that the tip of the catheter enters the superior vena cava . A chest X-ray is taken to confirm the position of the tip. PICC lines have the advantage of minimizing inconvenience to the patients and clinicians. However, if the patient develops thrombophlebitis , the PICC line may be destroyed . The image below shows (A) a typical PICC line (B) an illustration showing insertion of PICC line (C) a patient with PICC line inserted through the upper arm .The image below shows the chest X-ray confirming the position of the tip of the PICC line (arrows), in the superior vena cava .18

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the size of the cannula shown in the below image?
mcqs.explanation: The given cannula is 20 gauge IV cannula as its color code is pink.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Identify the instrument:
mcqs.explanation: The image shows Babcock's forceps .63 In Babcock's forceps , the distal part of the distal blade is curved with a triangular fenestra which allows soft tissues to bulge out. The tip is non-traumatic with transverse serrations. It has a lock in the proximal part. It is used to hold tubular structures such as parts of the bowel , fallopian tube , appendix , ureter, etc.Option A: Allis tissue forceps have distal blades , not opposing each other. The tip has got teeth in each blade that are opposing . There is a lock in the proximal part. It is used to hold skin flaps , fascia, aponeurosis , and the bladder wall.Option C: Lane's tissue holding forceps have got stout and thick distal blades with oval fenestrae . It has an opposing tooth on the tip and a lock in the proximal part. It is used to hold bulky and tough structures and lymph nodes .64 Option D: Kocher 's hemostatic forceps - It is identified by the opposing tooth on the tip and serrations in the distal blades . It is used to hold pedicles , tough structures , and cut ends of muscles . It is also used to hold ribs during rib dissection , gauze for blunt dissection , and resected bowel .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: For which of the following would you use the instrument shown in the image?
mcqs.explanation: The image shows a sponge holding forceps . It is used to: • Clean skin with a swab dipped in antiseptic solution during all operations • Remove laminated membrane and daughter cysts during operation of hydatid cyst . • Hold the fundus and Hartmann 's pouch of gall bladder during cholecystectomy65 • Swab an abscess cavity • Hold the cervix during cerclage .Ovum forceps is shown below . It is used to grasp products of conception and prevent the crushing of the conceptus . They have no catch and the blades are slightly bent and fenestrated . The absence of catch minimizes uterine injury if accidentally caught . It is introduced with the blades closed and opened up inside the uterine cavity to grasp the products . The instrument is taken out with a slight rotatory movement. The rotatory movement not only facilitates detachment of the products from the uterine wall, but also minimizes the injury of the uterine wall if accidentally grasped .Pile holding forceps are used to hold haemorrhoids.66 Cord holding forceps are typically used to hold spermatic cords.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: You notice your surgery resident use the given instrument to remove gall stones . Identify the instrument.
mcqs.explanation: The above instrument is Desjardin's choledocholithotomy forceps and is used for bile duct stone removal. It may also be used during the removal of kidney, ureteric , or bladder stones . This is a long and slender instrument. There are finger bows but no catch. The shaft is curved. The blades are small, without serrations, and fenestrated centrally .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: For what purpose would you use the instrument shown in the image?

options.d: To hold tough tissue like skin and fascia

mcqs.explanation: 67 The above image is of Lister's sinus forceps which are used for blunt dissection . It is used during Hilton's method of abscess drainage to break the bacterial loculi . It is also used for inserting or removing packing in the sinus cavity.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Identify the instrument:
mcqs.explanation: Doyen's mouth gag is used to keep the mouth open for intraoral surgery when retraction of the tongue is not required or desirable . Mostly used for tongue surgery. It is applied on one side of the mouth on the molar teeth .Option A: Doyen's retractor is used to retract the abdominal wall in abdominal and pelvic surgeries to expose the field of operation.68 Option C: Doyen's intestinal occlusion clamp is used for resection and anastomosis of the intestine in cases of: • Strangulated hernia • Accidental injuries to the gut • Intestinal growths • Gastric/intestinal bypass surgeries .Option D: Joll's thyroid retractor is a self -retaining retractor used in thyroid surgeries to retract skin .69

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Identify the instrument given in the image below :
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows a Morris retractor with a single , flat transversely curved blade and a blunt projecting ridge with backward projection. Morris retractor can be single or double -bladed . It is used to retract abdominal wall incisions, loin incisions, subcostal wounds or any wounds in depth . It can be used to improve visibility on one side of an incision. Thus, it is valuable during the initial phase of a laparotomy.Other options : Option A: Deaver's retractor is a question mark -shaped stout , atraumatic retractor with a broad, gently curved long blade . It is used to retract the abdominal wall and viscera. Moist mops should70 be kept underneath prior to placing this retractor. It is used for major abdominal surgeries , bladder surgeries and lumbar sympathectomy .Option C: Czerny's retractor is a superficial retractor with a thick and small blade on one side and a biflanged hook on the other side in opposite directions . It is used in hernia surgery and laparotomy, especially during closure .Option D: Double -hook retractor consists of two hooks with a handle. It is used in excision of swellings like lipoma, neurofibroma and cyst . It is also used to hold the skin flaps when raising them.71

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following instruments would be best suited to retract the liver out of the field of operation while performing an open cholecystectomy ?
mcqs.explanation: The Deaver's retractor would be most useful in cholecystectomy as it is specifically designed for holding the liver up and out of the way. Deaver's retractor is used carefully to avoid damaging the liver. Some surgeons protect the liver with an abdominal pack before placing the blade on top .Doyen's retractor - It is used to retract the abdominal wall as well as the bladder for proper exposure of the lower uterine segment during a cesarian section .72 Morris retractor is a large retractor useful for providing maximum exposure in large incisions e.g., abdominal incisions. It can be used to improve visibility on one side of an incision. Thus, it is valuable during the initial phase of a laparotomy.Czerny's retractor - This is a double -ended retractor used to retract wound edges for intermediate -type procedures . One end has a blade with a lip which helps to retract without the edge slipping . The other end has two prongs and helps to retract the ends of an incision.73

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: During thyroidectomy , the given instrument was used to retract the strap muscles . Identify the instrument:
mcqs.explanation: The above image is that of a Langenbeck retractor. It is used for holding open wounds , as in an open appendicectomy . Option B: Dyball retractor is used in major abdominal surgeries to retract deeper parts of the abdominal wall, bladder , or uterus while operating on the rectum and entering the rectovesical or rectouterine pouch . It has a lip at the bottom of the blade to prevent slippage . Care should be taken when it is used to retract the liver as it may damage the liver parenchyma.Option C: Goligher retractor is a self -retaining retractor used in operations on the sigmoid colon and rectum, such as anterior resection and the upper end of abdominoperineal resection . The retractor is inserted with the side blades to separate the edges of the abdominal wall. The central blade is then inserted to keep the small bowel away from the operation site .74 Option D: Travers retractor is a self -retaining retractor used for intermediate -type operations, such as: • Herniorrhaphy • Groin dissection for varicose veins • Femoral embolectomy .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Identify the given instrument.
mcqs.explanation: The image shows Kocher 's thyroid dissector which is used during a thyroidectomy to dissect the upper pole of the thyroid. The instrument is blunt and therefore damage to the superior thyroid artery or external laryngeal nerve is unlikely.75

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the size of the given blade used for incision and drainage of a superficial abscess ?
mcqs.explanation: The size of the surgical blade shown is the 11 -size blade (stab knife) that has a triangular shape with an oblique edge and a sharp-pointed tip. Uses : • Incision and drainage (I & D) of an abscess • Insertion of drains and arteriotomy. Other options : Option A: The 10 -size blade is used for skin incisions. It has a curved cutting edge that tapers to a pointed tip. Option C: The 22 -size blade is often used for abdominal incisions. It has a flat, unsharpened back edge and a curved front cutting edge . Option D: The 15-size blade is used for minor surgical procedures (lipoma excision) and precise skin incisions. It is a smaller blade with a small cutting edge .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: The type of knot seen in the image is:
mcqs.explanation: The given image shows the suture material exiting the knot is on the same side as the entry i.e no cross-over is seen . This is seen in a reef knot. A knot is a fastening made of threads intertwined together or on themselves . Each knot consists of- 2 half-hitches placed in sequential throws. Squaring refers to tightening the knot/half-hitch in a manner that the threads lay flat due to the alternating direction of half-hitches in adjacent layers. Types of knots:76 • Granny knot: half-hitch over a half-hitch in the same direction. It has better -holding power than half-hitch • Reef knot: half-hitch followed by a second half-hitch after squaring. • Triple throw knot: Reef knot with another half-hitch knot for added security . Knots made with prolene sutures require 6-8 throws to prevent slippage . • Surgeon's knot: Modification of the reef knot with two half-hitches in the first layer. • Slip knot: Modification of either granny/reef knot formed when one end of the thread is kept taut while tightening the knot.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A man presents to the emergency with a clean lacerated wound on his forearm. You use the given suturing technique to close his wound . Which of the following statements is false?

options.a: This technique has the least cut through rate
options.b: The wound edges should be everted
options.c: Interrupted sutures are used to approximate the wound
options.d: After the first bite , the needle should emerge at the of center the wound

mcqs.explanation: The given image shows interrupted sutures . Horizontal mattress sutures , not interrupted sutures , have the least cut-through rate. In mattress suture , the initial suture is inserted as an interrupted suture , but then the needle either moves horizontally or vertically and traverses both edges of the wound once again as seen in the picture .77 Continuous suture : For a continuous suture , the first suture is inserted in an identical manner to an interrupted suture , but the rest of the sutures are inserted in a continuous manner until the far end of the wound is reached .Subcuticular sutures : Small bites of the subcuticular tissues are taken on alternate sites of the wound and then gently pulled together thus approximating the wound edges without the risk of the cross-hatched markings of interrupted sutures .78

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: During an intra-oral procedure , the resident uses the given suture material to place sutures on the soft palate . What is this suture material called ?
mcqs.explanation: The suture material shown in the image is plain catgut . It is a yellowish absorbable suture material. Chromic catgut is brownish in colour. Vicryl is a violet-coloured absorbable suture material.Silk is a black-coloured , multifilament , natural, braided, and non-absorbable suture material. It is derived from the cocoon of the silkworm larva .79 Prolene is a blue coloured , monofilament, non-absorbable suture .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the normal urine output in adults ?
mcqs.explanation: The average normal urine output is approximately 1500 mL /day. A minimum urine output of 400 mL/day is essential to excrete the end products of protein metabolism . Fluid loss occurs mainly by four routes : • Lungs: Approximately 400 mL of water is lost in expired air every 24 hours. • Skin : In a temperate climate the loss is between 600 and 1000 mL /day. • Urine: The normal urine output is approximately 1500 mL /day. • Faeces : About 60 and 150 mL of water are lost daily in patients with normal bowel function.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Following a road traffic accident , a 23 -year-old man presents with breathlessness . On examination , he has hypotension and distended neck veins. On auscultation , muffled heart sounds are heard. What is this condition primarily associated with?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario of Beck's triad (hypotension , distended neck veins, and muffled heart sounds) is seen in cardiac tamponade . Shock due to cardiac tamponade is primarily an example of obstructive shock.32 Obstructive shock is characterized by a reduction in preload due to mechanical obstruction of the cardiac filling of the left and/or right sides of the heart, which in turn leads to fall in cardiac output . Common causes of obstructive shock include : • Cardiac tamponade • Tension pneumothorax • Massive pulmonary embolus or air embolus Cardiogenic shock is due to primary failure of the heart to pump blood. It may be due to myocardial depression as a result of infarction, cardiomyopathy , blunt myocardial injury. Patients with cardiac tamponade may eventually develop cardiogenic shock as the myocardium is stressed against the obstruction.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most common Gastrointestinal atresia?
mcqs.explanation: The most common Gastrointestinal atresia is duodenal atresia (60%) followed by jejunal and ileal atresia (20%). Colonic atresia is the least common type (7-10%). Duodenal atresias are commonly associated with chromosomal abnormalities such as Down syndrome. It occurs approximately in 1/10 ,000 births.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following drugs have a significant role in the mortality reduction of trauma patients based on the CRASH-2 trial?
mcqs.explanation: The CRASH-2 trial has shown mortality reduction in bleeding trauma patients by early usage of tranexamic acid (preferably within the first 3 hours) with a loading dose of 1 g over 10 minutes and then infusion of 1 g over 8 hours.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Trauma - Spinal, Thoracic and Abdominal Injuries
mcqs.question: A patient develops abdominal compartment syndrome following an emergency laparotomy. Which of the following is false about this condition?
mcqs.explanation: Central venous pressure (CVP ) increases due to inferior vena cava (IVC ) and portal vein compression in abdominal compartment syndrome. Abdominal Compartment Syndrome (ACS) is defined as increased intra-abdominal pressure (IAP ) >20 mm Hg resulting in compression of abdominal structures (Normal IAP = 5-7 mmHg and intraabdominal hypertension IAP �o 12 mmHg). This produces fatal complications due to pulmonary failure and mesenteric vascular compromise. Elevated intra-abdominal pressure leads to a decrease in venous return resulting in decreased cardiac output . An increase in heart rate partly compensates this. Systemic vascular resistance (afterload ) is increased by the compression of both the aorta and systemic vasculature. This also leads to an increase in renal vascular resistance leading to a reduced glomerular filtration rate.170 Causes of primary ACS include : • Abdominal trauma • Hemorrhage • Intestinal obstruction • Retroperitoneal hematoma Causes of secondary ACS include : • Pregnancy • Ascites • Ileus • Intra -abdominal sepsis • Large-volume fluid replacement (greater than 3L )

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.chapter: Breast - Anatomy, Congenital and Benign Diseases
mcqs.question: A female patient presents with a breast abscess . An aspiration was attempted under antibiotic cover which failed to reveal any aspirate. What is the next step in management?

options.d: Stop antibiotics as no aspirate was collected

mcqs.explanation: In a patient with a breast abscess , the next step after a failed aspiration is to attempt aspiration once again under antibiotic cover. Incision and drainage is not preferred , as it can potentially interfere with breastfeeding , and delicate structures such as ducts , lobules , and tubules may be injured, possibly leading to a non-healing milk fistula . A breast abscess is a complication of acute mastitis, which is more common in new mothers at the beginning of lactation (lactational mastitis). Non-lactational mastitis is more common in diabetic , immunosuppressed people and people predisposed by duct ectasia and periareolar infections . Clinical features of a breast abscess include : • Fever and malaise • Localized pain and tenderness • Redness and swelling of the affected breast • Positive fluctuation test .200 An ultrasonogram of the affected breast is performed to confirm the abscess , and treatment proceeds as follows : • Analgesics , antipyretics , and breast support for pain and fever relief . • Aspiration is performed under antibiotic cover, and the pus is cultured . If aspiration proves unsuccessful , it should be reattempted after a few days. • Incision and drainage should be considered in cases of: • Mastitis unresponsive to antibiotics for 48 hours. • Brawny induration. • Progressive mastitis with persistent fever Note :Bacterial mastitis Breast abscess Condition Localized inflammation due t o ascending infection or infec tion due to milk stasis Occurs as a complication of mastitisPus formation Symptoms Dullpain Throbbingpain Signs (if any) TendernessErythema Point tendernessErythemaIn duration of skin(if chronic)Ly mphadenopathyFluctuation t est +vePus pointmay be prese nt Managemen t AnalgesicsAntibiotics (Diclox acillin500 mg every 6 hours orally; Erythromycin if allergi c to penicillin )Adequate brea st support AnalgesicsAdequate breast su pportAspiration of Pus under antibiotic cover; repeated as pirations if requiredIncision & drainage201

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 48-year-old woman with a lump in her right breast was advised to undergo mammography which was reported as BIRADS 3. What will be the appropriate next step of management in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: A BIRADS score of 3 means that it is probably a benign lesion. The next appropriate step is to follow up with this patient every 6 months for the next 2 years. During this period , the score can either downgrade to BIRADS 2 or upgrade to BIRADS 4 or 5.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Which of the following is true regarding sentinel lymph node biopsy in a patient with a T2 N1 M0 breast tumour?

options.a: If biopsy is positive , then axillary dissection is not done
options.b: If biopsy is negative , then axillary dissection is done
options.c: If biopsy is positive then tumour free margin should be > 2 cm

mcqs.explanation: Sentinel lymph node biopsy is only done in node-negative tumors. It is not done in N1 stage tumors.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A patient with a nodule of the neck presents to the surgery OPD. A junior resident performs the following method to palpate it. Identify the procedure shown in the video below .
mcqs.explanation: The video depicts Lahey's method of palpation of the left lobe of the thyroid gland. In Lahey's method , for palpating the left lobe , the examiner initially pushes the right lobe medially with the left hand, and then using the right hand, the border and consistency of the left lobe is palpated . Other options : Option B: In Crile's method the patient is asked to swallow , while the examiner palpates the gland with the thumb. This gives a clear indication regarding the slight enlargement of the thyroid gland or small nodules .286 Option C: Kocher 's method is done to demonstrate the pressure effect of the thyroid gland on the trachea or larynx. Lateral compression will result in stridor. Option D: Pemberton's sign (not method ), is engorgement of neck veins when the patient is asked to raise their hands above the head and the arms should touch the ears. It is seen in patients with retrosternal goiter .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: In a patient with asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism , when will you perform parathyroidectomy ?

options.a: If bone mineral density of > 2.5 SD above peak bone mass
options.c: In the presence of hypercalciuria but absence of nephrolithiasis
options.d: If creatinine clearance is reduced by 30%

mcqs.explanation: Reduction in creatinine clearance by 30% is an indication for parathyroidectomy in patients with asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Neuroblastoma can originate in all of the following except
mcqs.explanation: Neuroblastoma does not originate in the adrenal cortex. Neuroblastoma is an embryonal tumour of the sympathetic nervous system . These tumours arise during fetal or early postnatal life from sympathetic cells derived from the neural crest. Therefore, tumours can originate anywhere along the path which neural crest cells migrate, including: • Adrenal medulla - most common site • Paraspinal sympathetic ganglia • Sympathetic para ganglia such as the organ of Zuckerkandl362 Note : Neuroblastoma is the most common abdominal (extradural) tumour in children and the most common overall tumour in infants.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old male patient presented to the OPD with complaints of increasing heartburn and dyspepsia for the past several months. He was prescribed PPIs for one month but he has no relief . You perform a urea breath test which is found to be positive . What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: 431 The given clinical scenario and the positive urea breath test are suggestive of a Helicobacter pylori infection which is most commonly associated with Type B gastritis. Type B gastritis usually affects the antrum. Intestinal metaplasia associated with chronic pan-gastritis and atrophy is seen . It has greater potential for malignancy as compared to Type A gastritis. Type A gastritis affects the fundus with antral sparing. Its features can be easily remembered by 4 'A's: • Autoimmune condition - has circulating antibodies to parietal cells • Atrophy of parietal cell mass • Achlorhydria - causes chronic hypergastrinemia and microadenomas of enterochromaffin-like (ECL) cells • Anemia - leads to pernicious anemia, due to malabsorption of Vit B12 (as the intrinsic factor is also produced by parietal cells )

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A male patient who was diagnosed with early gastric cancer is planned for endoscopic mucosal resection. Which of the following features would make him a poor candidate for this procedure ?
mcqs.explanation: Endoscopic mucosal resection for gastric cancer should not be performed in case of ulcerated gastric cancer. Indications for endoscopic resection of early gastric cancer: • Tumor smaller than 2cm • Tumor limited to the mucosa • No lymphovascular invasion • No ulceration • Well or moderately well -differentiated histopathology . If any of these are not fulfilled , then gastrectomy with lymph node dissection is indicated .452 For a proximal gastric carcinoma a total gastrectomy is done and for distal gastric carcinoma , subtotal gastrectomy is ideal . For advanced carcinoma gastrectomy can be done as a palliative treatment .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: In a suspected case of bowel obstruction, the presence of which of the following helps you to distinguish the small intestine from the large intestine ?
mcqs.explanation: The presence of valvule conniventes (plicae circulares) helps to distinguish the small intestine from the large intestine . They are prominent mucosal folds seen in the gross examination of the small intestine and are also visible radiographically. They are more prominent in the jejunum. Radiological differences between small bowel and large bowel obstruction are: Investigation of choice : CECT abdomen (adults ); USG abdomen (children)Radiological feature s Small bowel Large bo wel Valvulae connivente s Present in jejunu m Absent No of Loops Many Few Distribution of loops Central Peripher al Haustra Absent Present Diameter 3-5 cm >5 cm485 Radiological feature s Small bowel Large bo wel Solid faeces Absent Present

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old female patient presents with a 9-month history of weight loss, abdominal cramps, and intermittent diarrhea. On examination, a palpable mass in the right lower quadrant of the abdomen is found. Stool cultures are normal . Colonoscopy shows the presence of skip lesions . Biopsy showed the presence of non-caseating granulomas. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: 520 The clinical scenario and the biopsy showing the presence of non-caseating granulomas are diagnostic of Crohn's disease .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: While assisting a laparoscopic appendectomy , you observe the resident use the Fold of Treves as a guide while coagulating vessels in the mesoappendix . Which of the following best describes the anatomical landmark ?

options.a: Mucous membrane projecting into the ileal lumen
options.b: The ilio-cecal fold of the peritoneum
options.c: The fold of the mucous membrane around appendiceal orifice
options.d: The fold of the peritoneum over ascending colon

mcqs.explanation: 550 Fold of Treves is an antimesenteric ileocecal fold of peritoneum . A clinical aid useful for detecting the location of the appendix through small abdominal incisions is the identification of the fold of Treves. It marks the junction of the ileum and cecum . As it does not contain any vessel , it is referred to as the bloodless fold of Treves. It is also used as a guide to determine the extent of coagulation during an appendectomy . This prevents thermal injury to adjacent structures .Jackson Membrane: Adhesion from the right abdominal wall to the anterior tenia of the ascending colon. Gerlach valves: A mucosal fold covering the appendiceal orifice.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: What is the most common extra-colonic cancer in patients with a mutation in MMR genes ?
mcqs.explanation: 580 Endometrial carcinoma is the most common extracolonic carcinoma in patients with mutated MMR genes. Autosomal dominant mutation in DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes , such as hMLH1 , hMSH2, hMSH6, PMS1, and PMS2 lead to various cancers. This condition is known as Lynch Syndrome/HNPCC. Gastric and ovarian carcinoma are also commonly found.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Up to what length of the patient 's rectum will you be able to visualize while using a proctoscope ?
mcqs.explanation: Proctoscopes can be used to inspect the anus, anorectal junction, and 10 -15cm of the lower rectum .Scope Lengt h Anoscope 8 cm Proctoscope –15 cm Rigid Sigmoidoscope and Rec toscope 25 cm Flexible sigmoidoscope 60 cm Colonoscope 160 c m

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Bubonocele is a type of _________.
mcqs.explanation: Bubonocele is a type of indirect inguinal hernia where the hernia is limited to the inguinal canal. Indirect inguinal hernia is more common on the right side because of the delay in atrophy of the processus vaginalis after the normal slower descent of the right testis to the scrotum during fetal development .

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: All of the following are post -hepatic causes for portal hypertension , except _____
mcqs.explanation: Splenomegaly is a pre-hepatic cause of portal hypertension . Sarcoidosis and primary biliary cholangitis are presinusoidal intrahepatic causes of portal hypertension . Portal hypertension occurs when the pressure in the portal vein increases due to either increased resistance to blood flow secondary to fibrosis, active vasoconstriction, or hyperdynamic systemic circulation.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Spontaneous rupture of the liver occurs in ______.
mcqs.explanation: Hepatic adenoma can manifest as a case of spontaneous rupture , with the sudden onset of abdominal pain followed by hypovolemic shock secondary to intraperitoneal bleeding . The clinical presentation may be abdominal pain. In some cases , it can hepatic adenomas present with spontaneous intraperitoneal hemorrhage.

mcqs.subject: Surgery
mcqs.question: Auxiliary orthotopic liver transplantation is indicated in which of the following conditions?

options.b: As standby procedure till a suitable donor is found
options.c: Acute fulminant liver failure that is irreversible

mcqs.explanation: 730 Auxiliary orthotopic liver transplantation (A-OLTX) is indicated in non-cirrhotic metabolic liver disease . Auxiliary partial orthotopic liver transplantation is a technique where part of the diseased native liver is removed and replaced with a part of the healthy donor liver. This is done so the retained native liver can regenerate . In selective cases of acute liver failure, auxiliary partial orthotopic liver transplantation could provide a chance for native liver regeneration and immunosuppression -free life . mcqs.question: A patient presents with pain in the right upper quadrant on the second postoperative day following a cholecystectomy . Evaluation reveals a collection in the subhepatic space . A bile leak was suspected . Which of the following is the best investigation for this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is the best investigation in a patient suspected of post -cholecystectomy biliary leaks. Patients with post -cholecystectomy biliary leak usually present with fever, jaundice and abdominal pain. USG is used for an initial evaluation in such cases and can show a collection in the sub-hepatic space . The most common bile leak following cholecystectomy is from the cystic duct . This can be treated by placing a biliary endoprosthesis (stent ) in the common bile duct across the origin of the cystic duct .774 MRCP shows fluid collections arising from bile leaks but cannot differentiate these from other causes of fluid collections . ERCP is the best investigation as it has the advantage of being both diagnostic and therapeutic . ERCP is useful post -cholecystectomy as there is a high likelihood of a retained stone and stone extraction and/or temporary stenting may be required. HIDA scan is the most sensitive investigation for biliary leakage . CT scan can show focal fluid collections , ascites , biliary obstruction, hepatic atrophy, signs of secondary biliary cirrhosis and any vascular injury.

mcqs.question: A 49-year-old female patient presents with complaints of abdominal pain and foul -smelling , greasy stools for one year. She is known to be diabetic and underwent cholecystectomy one year back. CT scan shows the presence of a tumor in the pancreas. What is the most probable diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: The most probable diagnosis is somatostatinoma. Somatostatin inhibits pancreatic and biliary secretions . Patients with somatostatinoma usually present with vague abdominal pain along with the triad of: • Gallstones - due to bile stasis • Diabetes - due to inhibition of insulin secretion • Steatorrhea - due to inhibition of pancreatic exocrine secretion and bile secretion .

mcqs.question: A 58-year-old man is being evaluated for recurrent attacks of pancreatitis . An ERCP is done and it shows the presence of a fish-mouth sign at the ampulla of Vater. Which of the following statements is true about his condition?

options.a: It is more common in males
options.b: It only involves the main pancreatic duct
options.c: Head of pancreas is most common site of the neoplasm

mcqs.explanation: 856 A fish mouth sign at the ampulla of Vater during ERCP is indicative of intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IPMN). It is most commonly seen in the head of the pancreas. The intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm can be diagnosed with the following findings (Ohashi triad) during endoscopy : • Bulging ampulla of Vater (fish-mouth sign) • Dilated pancreatic duct • Mucin secretion from the opening Equal distribution is seen between males and females in IPMN. Patients are usually in their seventh or eighth decade of life and present with abdominal pain or recurrent pancreatitis . This is caused by the obstruction of the pancreatic duct by thick mucin. Some patients have symptoms secondary to pancreatic insufficiencies like steatorrhea , diabetes , and weight loss. IMPNs are of three types : • Branch -duct IPMN (BD-IPMN) - affects only the small side branches. It is less frequently associated with malignancy. • Main duct IPMN (MD-IPMN) - Affects the main pancreatic duct . Malignant transformation is commonly seen . • Mixed -type IPMN - side -branch IPMNs that extend into the main duct

mcqs.question: Which of the following are risk factors for calcium stone formation?
mcqs.explanation: Hypercalciuria, hyperoxaluria, and hyperuricosuria are risk factors for calcium stone formation.883 Risk factors for calcium stone formation include : • High urine concentration of calcium, oxalate, or uric acid • Low urine concentration of renal stone inhibiting factors such as citrate and magnesium • Abnormal urine pH Renal stone formation is governed by factors promoting and inhibiting stone formation. Stone formation occurs when the concentration product is more than the formation product i.e., CP > FP, where : • Concentration product (CP) - the amount of solute in solution • Formation product (FP) - maximum concentration of solute in solution after taking into account stone inhibiting factors.

mcqs.question: Which of the following should be the treatment of choice for renal cell carcinoma with tumor less than 4 cm in size?
mcqs.explanation: Partial nephrectomy (also known as nephron-sparing surgery) is the treatment of choice for tumors <4 cm. Indications for partial nephrectomy : • Tumors < 4cm • Well-selected tumors between 4-7 cm • Bilateral tumors • Tumor in solitary kidneys • Patients with pre-existing renal dysfunction. Recently , partial nephrectomy is also increasingly being performed for stage T1b tumors. Treatment of renal cell carcinoma : RCC is a radio and chemoresistant tumor. Radical nephrectomy consists of the removal of the kidney, perirenal fat, adrenal gland, and regional lymph nodes . The adrenal gland is no longer removed except in cases of obvious tumor involvement. Lymphadenectomy is indicated only in high-risk patients with large primary tumors and enlarged lymph nodes . Cryoablation is indicated in the T1a stage of RCC if surgery cannot be performed . It is also indicated in advanced/metastatic tumors. mcqs.question: All of the following are indications to perform circumcision in children, except :
mcqs.explanation: A tight frenulum and physiological phimosis are not indications of circumcision in children. Physiological phimosis is seen in children that are less than 6 years of age (2-6 years) due to natural adhesions between the glans and inner preputial skin. It rectifies on its own. Circumcision is the surgical removal of the foreskin that covers the glans penis . Indications of circumcision in children: • True phimosis (associated with a white , scarred preputial orifice, most common just before puberty ) • Paraphimosis • On request (most common) • Balanitis xerotica obliterans (BXO) • Recurrent UTI with abnormal upper urinary tract • Recurrent balanoposthitis Indications of circumcision in adults : • Recurrent balanitis • Tight frenulum (Splitting of frenulum can occur during sexual activity) • Inability to retract the foreskin for intercourse975

mcqs.question: A patient is scheduled to undergo a total parotidectomy with selective node dissection of levels Ib, IIa , IIb , and III . Which of the following groups of lymph nodes will be removed during the procedure ?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options , only submandibular (Level Ib) and middle jugular nodes (Level III ) nodes will be removed. The other nodes that will be removed in the procedure will be upper jugular nodes (Level IIa and IIb ). Selective neck dissection has been used in the treatment of patients with cancer of the upper aerodigestive tract (oral cavity, pharynx, larynx), cancer of the thyroid gland, cutaneous malignancies, and cancer of the salivary gland. The type of selective neck dissection used varies depending on the lymphatic drainage and metastatic pattern associated with the primary cancer site .

mcqs.question: A 58-year-old homeless man was brought to a PHC in Himachal Pradesh during late winter. He was found unresponsive. His rectal temperature was 23 degrees C, pulse was not measurable , heart rate was 30 per minute and respiratory rate was 6. Rewarming with an electric blanket was started . Which organ is most susceptible to dysfunction in this patient ?
mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of hypothermia . The heart is the organ most sensitive to cold and is subject to ventricular fibrillation or asystole when the temperature drops to 21 –24 \260C.1079 Hypothermia affects the dissociation of oxygen from hemoglobin , so less oxygen is released to the tissues . Other complications are coagulopathies and disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), pancreatitis , and acute renal failure. mcqs.question: During a health checkup in a factory, a 52-year-old worker complained of progressive cough and weight loss for the past 6 months. Chest X-ray showed a mass in the right apical region of the lung with pleural effusion . The biopsy sample obtained stained positive for calretinin. Which of the following is false about this condition?

options.a: Immunohistochemical analysis will be positive for TTF -1.
options.c: Asbestos exposure is the major risk factor.

mcqs.explanation: The given clinical scenario with biopsy showing positive calretinin is suggestive of mesothelioma . The immunohistochemical analysis will be negative for TTF -1 in mesothelioma . TTF -1 is positive1156 in adenocarcinoma of the lung. Malignant mesothelioma is the most common tumor of the pleura . Exposure to asbestos is the major known risk factor. The latency period between asbestos exposure and the development of mesothelioma is at least 20 years. It is more common in males, usually seen after 40 years of age . It has a very poor prognosis. Histological subtypes include : • Epithelial • Sarcomatous • Biphasic The physical characteristics of specific fibers are important for causation. They are: • Serpentine fibers: Large and curly, not able to travel beyond larger airways. • Amphibole fibers: The narrow , straight amphibole fibers, in particular, the crocidolite fibers navigate distally into the pulmonary parenchyma and are most clearly associated with mesotheliomas . It is not bilaterally symmetrical. Its clinical features include : • Dyspnoea • Chest pain • Pleural effusion – in 90% cases Diagnostic imaging includes chest X-ray, CT scan, and FDG-PET scan to determine the extent of tumor invasion and to evaluate occult metastases . Thoracoscopy or open pleural biopsy with special staining of tumor samples is required to differentiate mesotheliomas from adenocarcinomas. Treatment includes a combination of surgery, chemotherapy , and radiation therapy . Extrapleural pneumonectomy and total pleurectomy are two commonly used surgical procedures .1157
